title: Sean Payton: Broncos have to get a handle on injuries, look at our pre-practice routine
summary: "You always try to look at your pre-practice routine," Payton said. "Your hydration, obviously. And it’s incumbent on the player."
full_text: Broncos coach Sean Payton wants to see what he can do to keep his team healthier. Payton said at training camp on Monday that he's concerned about the number of soft-tissue injuries his team has suffered so far in camp. “ We’ve got to get a handle on some of the soft-tissues,” Payton said, via the Denver Post . “We’ve had a couple either strains, hamstring or groins. We continue to fight through that.” Payton said he doesn't want to blame the heat but does want to look at how the team can make sure the players are adequately taken care of, and taking care of themselves, before and during practice. “You always try to look at your pre-practice routine," Payton said. "Your hydration, obviously. And it’s incumbent on the player. It’s hard for anyone to know your soft tissue. I’m always looking at maybe what we did leading up to the period when a guy had a strain." The players who have had to miss time in training camp because of soft-tissue injuries include three of the Broncos' most important offensive playmakers, running back J.K. Dobbins and wide receivers Jaylen Waddle and Marvin Mims Jr.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Report: Alec Pierce had a second PRP injection to speed up healing in ankle
summary: Colts wide receiver Alec Pierce has not seen the practice field in 2026.
full_text: Colts wide receiver Alec Pierce has not seen the practice field in 2026. He underwent what the Colts originally called a "clean-up" surgery on his left ankle in late March. Pierce had hoped to avoid surgery by taking a platelet-rich plasma injection after the 2025 season. He was given a 4-6-month recovery timeline, putting the start of the season in doubt. Nathan Brown of the Indianapolis Star reports that Pierce underwent a second PRP injection since then to help with lingering soreness and speed up healing. The injection was not due to a setback in his rehab, Brown adds. It is unclear, though, when Pierce might return as the team has offered no timeline. Pierce remains on the active/physically unable to perform list.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bo Nix is eager for preseason action
summary: Sean Payton said the Broncos will play some starters against the Falcons on Friday night.
full_text: Sean Payton said the Broncos will play some starters against the Falcons on Friday night. He has not decided whether Bo Nix will be one of those to see action in the team's preseason opener. "We haven’t gone through the role yet,” Payton said, via Chris Tomasson of The Denver Gazette . “I’ll let you know when we go through the roles." The game is on the artificial turf at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, which could keep Nix out until the second week of the preseason. Nix is ready, though. He has not played since the Broncos' divisional-round playoff victory over the Bills when he fractured his right ankle. The AFC Championship Game was the first game Nix has missed for injury in his career. “I’m excited,” Nix said of playing in the preseason. “I think preseason’s always a great time to get back out there and get your feet wet a little bit and see defenses in a live situation before the first [regular-season] game.” Nix said he has "no idea" whether he will play Friday. Regardless, the Broncos are expected to use both Jarrett Stidham and Sam Ehlinger against the Falcons as they compete for the backup job.
author: Charean Williams

title: Judge criticizes Jon Gruden for "lack of compliance with the rules" in case against NFL
summary: Gruden is ordered to provide NFL with more information within the next seven days.
full_text: Former Raiders coach Jon Gruden wanted his claims against the NFL and Commissioner Roger Goodell to be resolved in court. Gruden won. And now he has to fully comply with the court's rules. The presiding judge suggested on Monday that Gruden has not done so sufficiently. “I remain concerned with Gruden’s, Gruden’s side’s delays and lack of cooperation, lack of compliance with the rules ,” district judge Joe Hardy said, via Noble Brigham of the Las Vegas Review-Journal . The NFL had complained that Gruden was dragging his feet in the discovery process associated with his lawsuit alleging that the NFL deliberately leaked otherwise confidential emails in an effort to force him out as the Raiders' head coach in October 2021. “No explanation was proffered by Gruden’s side that would address the court’s concern about the delays, particularly in light of months ago, when I said, in Gruden’s favor and against the NFL’s position, we’re going forward,” Judge Hardy said. “Gruden understandably at least represented to me that their side wanted to proceed expeditiously and has done the opposite of that.” Judge Hardy partially granted a request from the league to force Gruden to produce certain documents and to provide supplemental answers to written questions within the next seven days. The NFL had argued that Gruden failed to provide information to which the league was entitled. "[T]he NFL Parties cannot defend this case with both hands tied behind their backs," the NFL's lawyers wrote. "Discovery is the mechanism by which litigants discover the truth, but Gruden does not want the truth discovered." The judge agreed with the NFL — and chastised Gruden. “You’re saying you’re proceeding expeditiously, but clearly you’re not,” Judge Hardy told Gruden's lawyers. Both sides in every civil case are entitled to obtain information from each other. The parties to lawsuits typically try to restrict what is provided. When those squabbles consume the judge's time, the judge is often not pleased. And that same judge will eventually be making fairly important decisions about the case. So it's important for both sides to avoid, speaking in the technical sense, pissing the judge off. Most recently, Gruden's side has not.
author: Mike Florio

title: Fernando Mendoza is listed as QB2 in first Raiders' depth chart
summary: As expected, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft has landed at No. 2 on the first 2026 Raiders depth chart.
full_text: As expected, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft has landed at No. 2 on the first 2026 Raiders depth chart . The preliminary configuration of players has been released. Fernando Mendoza is listed as the backup to Kirk Cousins at the quarterback position. The third quarterback is Aidan O'Connell, who has 17 starts in three seasons with the team. Jacob Clark, an undrafted rookie from Missouri State, is listed as the fourth-string quarterback. The Raiders seem to be intent on starting the season with Cousins under center, and to not having a true competition between Cousins and Mendoza. It's an approach that cuts against the modern approach of getting highly-drafted quarterbacks ready and putting them on the field, if only to give them the reps that will help the game slow down for them sooner rather than later. The initial Las Vegas depth chart contains no real surprises. If Mendoza isn't playing by the end of the 2026 season, that will be a major surprise. The overriding question is whether the Raiders have enough talent to compete in a top-heavy AFC West. On paper, they don't. It will be up to them to defy that once the real games begin.
author: Mike Florio

title: Derek Carr joins UCLA as a special advisor to the head coach
summary: Derek Carr is returning to football.
full_text: Derek Carr is returning to football. But not as a player. As a sort-of coach. UCLA announced that it has hired the former Raiders and Saints quarterback to serve as a "special advisor" to head coach Bob Chesney. Carr will help Chesney and the offensive staff with game-planning. Carr also will work with the UCLA quarterbacks. A second-round pick in 2014, Carr has no ties to UCLA. He played college football at Fresno State. But UCLA General Manager Darrick Yray was an assistant at Fresno State when Carr played there. "I've known Darrick for a long time and have great respect for the work he's done throughout his career," Carr said. "The opportunity to help Coach Chesney, the staff and the quarterbacks at UCLA was one that really excited me. I'm looking forward to sharing my experiences and helping support the program in any way I can." Carr, who last played in 2024, has mused about possibly returning to the NFL. Any team that would be interested in adding Carr would have to strike a deal with the Saints, who still hold his rights.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bills are figuring out the best way to configure video boards at new stadium
summary: When the Bills' new stadium had a soft launch on Saturday, some spoke hard truths about the size of the video boards.
full_text: ' When the Bills' new stadium had a soft launch on Saturday, some spoke hard truths about the size of the video boards. They are, for now, a work in progress. Bills chief operating officer Pete Guelli told PFT on Monday that they are working through the utilization of the new screens. Watch one of the clips. There's space on each side of the videos that isn't being used. When it's time to display a replay during a game, more of the total available space can be utilized. And while the total available space may not be as large as it is in other stadiums, it can become a distraction. In Dallas, for example, the gigantic screen hovering over the field becomes a distraction, drawing the eyes to the video when they should be on the live action below. Whatever they decide, there's no denying that it's an excellent new venue, with an open-air stadium and a grass field and a home for the Bills ideally for decades to come.
author: Mike Florio

title: Mike Macdonald on Terrion Arnold: We are going to do our diligence
summary: Free agent cornerback Terrion Arnold worked out for the Seahawks on Sunday.
full_text: '' Free agent cornerback Terrion Arnold worked out for the Seahawks on Sunday. Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald was asked about Arnold's visit as the third-year player faces four felony counts each of armed robbery and kidnapping. "It's enough right now that we had him in for a great visit, a great tryout ," Macdonald said Monday, via video from Brian Nemhauser of Hawk Blogger. "It's a situation where there are other things that are surrounding it as well, and we're aware of. We are working through the situation right now. But it was a great visit, and I really enjoyed meeting him. I think he enjoyed being here, so we will see how it goes. "We are going to do our diligence. There are a lot of people in Terrion's corner that we respect as to the type of guy he is. We are going to work through that, and I trust our people to make the best decision for us. We also think that this is a great place to come work, too, and that people can be the best version of themselves if given the opportunity." Arnold, who the Lions cut June 29 following his arrest, is scheduled for his arraignment this week. First, though, Arnold will work out for the Saints on Tuesday. He previously met with the Texans and has drawn interest from the Colts and Jets. The Lions drafted Arnold in the first round in 2024, and he played 24 games with 22 starts in two seasons. He has totaled 91 tackles, an interception and 18 pass breakups.
author: Charean Williams

title: Incoming Seahawks owner opens door for conversion to grass field
summary: Vinod Khosla defers to "[t]he team that got us the Super Bowl."
full_text: In lieu of making a broad effort to get NFL owners to convert artificial turf fields to high-quality grass, the NFL Players Association should focus on attempting to persuade specific teams to do it. Starting with the Seahawks . There's now even more reason to do so. Incoming owner Vinod Khosla has opened the door to making the change. Responding to the question of whether he would install grass at Lumen Field, Khosla said this over the weekend on Twitter, via Sofia Schwarzwalder of the Seattle Times : " I’d defer to people at the [Seahawks] who know better than me. The team that got us the Super Bowl." Appearing Monday on CNBC, Khosla reiterated his online message. “That’s for management to decide, not for me to decide,” Khosla said, per Schwarzwalder. If he's talking about the players, we already know what they'd overwhelmingly say. At the outset of camp, veterans Cooper Kupp and Leonard Williams made their feelings known . And there's no reason for the coaching staff or front office to disagree. They're not the ones paying for it. The owners are. If Khosla is willing to cut the check for high-quality grass, it's a no-brainer for everyone else in the organization.
author: Mike Florio

title: 49ers work out RBs Nyheim Miller-Hines, Zamir White
summary: The 49ers worked out running backs Nyheim Miller-Hines and Zamir White on Monday, according to the NFL's personnel notice.
full_text: The 49ers worked out running backs Nyheim Miller-Hines and Zamir White on Monday, according to the NFL's personnel notice. They also hosted running back Blake Watson on a visit. Starter Christian McCaffrey sat out Monday's practice with tightness. Jordan James, Kaelon Black and Isaac Guerendo are also sidelined. Patrick Taylor Jr., Sincere McCormick and Khalil Herbert are the only healthy backs on the roster. That's why it seems likely the 49ers will sign at least one of the running backs they had at the team facility, with a joint practice with the Titans on Tuesday and a preseason game Thursday. Miller-Hines, 29, spent time with the Chargers and Saints last season but had only three touches. He missed the 2023 and 2024 seasons after a jet ski accident left him with a torn ACL and MCL. A fourth-round pick of Indianapolis in 2018, Miller-Hines has 1,200 rushing yards and 10 rushing touchdowns in eight NFL seasons. White, 26, entered the NFL as a fourth-round pick of the Raiders in 2022. He had only 12 carries in six games with the Raiders last season. He has 736 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns in four seasons. Watson, 26, was an undrafted free agent in 2024 and played two games for the Broncos as a rookie. He had four carries for 10 yards, while playing 11 offensive snaps and seven on special teams. He was on the Titans' practice squad last season before going on the practice squad injured reserve. Watson signed a futures deal with the Titans, who cut him April 30.
author: Charean Williams

title: Falcons sign RB Trey Sermon
summary: The Falcons signed Bijan Robinson to a contract extension last week and they added a running back to compete for playing time behind him on Monday.
full_text: The Falcons signed Bijan Robinson to a contract extension last week and they added a running back to compete for playing time behind him on Monday. They announced the signing of Trey Sermon to the 90-man roster. They cut a pair of players earlier in the day and had an open spot available for Sermon. Sermon was a 2021 third-round pick of the 49ers and was claimed off of waivers by the Eagles after cutdown day in 2022. He spent the next two seasons with the Colts and moved on to the Steelers last year. Sermon has 91 carries for 319 yards and two touchdowns in 46 career games. He's also caught 22 passes for 138 yards. Brian Robinson, Tyler Goodson, Nathan Carter, and Cash Jones are the other backs looking for spots on the Falcons' 53-man roster.
author: Josh Alper

title: Mike McDaniel: We'll kinda play hot hand at running back
summary: Chargers running back Omarion Hampton thinks the arrival of offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is going to be a good thing for the team's running backs and McDaniel's plans for the position came up during a press conference on Monday.
full_text: Chargers running back Omarion Hampton thinks the arrival of offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is going to be a good thing for the team's running backs and McDaniel's plans for the position came up during a press conference on Monday. McDaniel was asked if he plans to use Hampton as a workhorse back in the 2025 first-round pick's second NFL season. McDaniel said "there’s going to be opportunities for him to have a ton of touches," but that he also plans to use Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal on a weekly basis and that the usage will be dictated on the fly rather than scripted in advance. “There’s good news and bad news, fantasy owners," McDaniel said. "Good news is I see all three of those guys producing at a very high level. The bad news is I can’t tell you which games those are. . . . Kinda play hot hand once you’re into games. Specifically, I’ll use all three of those guys probably every game. The relative ratio that will be based on opponent and what we’re asking the guys to do." The news might not be good for anyone drafting their fantasy teams, but a robust run game will be good for the Chargers and quarterback Justin Herbert regardless of who is spearheading the attack.
author: Josh Alper

title: Stephen Jones: Quinnen Williams represents everything Cowboys want in a football player
summary: The Cowboys announced the three-year, $105.9 million extension with defensive tackle Quinnen Williams on Monday.
full_text: The Cowboys announced the three-year, $105.9 million extension with defensive tackle Quinnen Williams on Monday. It ties Williams to the Cowboys for the next five seasons. Since the Cowboys traded Micah Parsons to the Packers almost a year ago, they have added Williams, defensive tackle Kenny Clark and outside linebacker Malachi Lawrence in return. Therefore, the trade could end up being a win-win. "It's a big part of all the moving parts that went with our trade last year," Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones said of the extension with Williams, via Tommy Yarrish of the team website. "I think this kind of, at the end of the day, puts a bow on top in terms of knowing that we're going to have Q here for the next five years long term, and have Kenny out there rolling, the deal we made with Rashan Gary and how we used the pick on Lawrence. All these things, you can't say they were all tied to just that, but it's a big deal. "And certainly [Williams] represents everything that we want in a Dallas Cowboys football player. He's not only a great football player, but he's a man. He's a leader who people in the locker room look to every day. I was just talking to Christian [Parker, who said] he's the best player out on the field."
author: Charean Williams

title: Monti Ossenfort: We have no interest in trading Josh Sweat
summary: Cardinals outside linebacker Josh Sweat remains on the active/physically unable to perform list with a knee issue.
full_text: ''' Cardinals outside linebacker Josh Sweat remains on the active/physically unable to perform list with a knee issue. Coach Mike LaFleur has repeatedly said he is not worried about Sweat's availability for the Sept. 13 opener. General Manager Monti Ossenfort reiterated that belief Monday. "Josh is making good progress . Josh is getting closer every day," Ossenfort said, via video from PHNX Cardinals. "I think Josh is going to be out there in due time to get ready for the season opener, and we're excited to get him out there and get him going." Sweat, 29, was the subject of trade chatter in the offseason, as the Cardinals received calls about him. Ossenfort said the Cardinals are not interested in trading Sweat, who had a career-high 12 sacks last season. "I'd say [trade] discussions that come by that, there's always a lot of talk that goes around that," Ossenfort said. "We have no interest in trading Josh. We're excited to have him. Some of those discussions [we're] going to keep private, but excited to have Josh here. [He] had a great year last year. Excited for more good things out of him this year."
author: Charean Williams

title: Lions announce that they've signed Josh Dobbs
summary: Quarterback Josh Dobbs is officially a member of the Lions.
full_text: '' Quarterback Josh Dobbs is officially a member of the Lions. Word that Dobbs would be joining the team came on Sunday and the move was announced on Monday afternoon. Defensive tackle Aidan Keanaaina was placed on injured reserve in a corresponding move. The Lions moved to sign Dobbs after Teddy Bridgewater informed them that he was retiring. Dobbs now steps into the No. 2 role behind Jared Goff with undrafted rookie Luke Altmyer on hand as the team's third quarterback. Dobbs appeared in four games as a reserve for New England last season. He started games for the 49ers, Cardinals, Vikings and Titans in previous NFL stops. Keanaaina signed with the Lions after going undrafted earlier this year.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bills will address concerns over sight lines on "case-by-case basis"
summary: The Bills unofficially opened their stadium on Saturday night, with the team practicing in the brand-new building.
full_text: ' The Bills unofficially opened their stadium on Saturday night, with the team practicing in the brand-new building. The event sparked a variety of images of seats with obstructed views . On Monday afternoon, Bills chief operating officer Pete Guelli told PFT that the team has heard from "less than one percent" of the Personal Seat License account holders regarding sight-line concerns. The Bills, per Guelli, will address these issues on a "case-by-case basis." The Bills marketed the PSLs with a Virtual Venue model that showed the customers the expected view from each seat. The team believed the virtual images were "pretty representative" of the in-seat viewpoint. The team's goal will be to attempt to resolve all concerns. The Bills have more than 17,000 PSL account holders. Each account holder has one or more seats in the new stadium. The photos posted on social media show multiple locations from which the full playing field can't be seen. At least one extreme example , posted by John Wawrow of the Associated Press, was taken from a seat that has not been sold and will not be sold for football games. It could be used for other events, such as concerts. Other seats fall into that same category, we're told. Still, some of the seats created concerns that have been communicated by the PSL account holders to the team. Those issues will be explored and, if necessary, resolved.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cowboys, Quinnen Williams agree to three-year, $105.9 million extension
summary: Williams, who had two years left on his deal, is guaranteed $101 million.
full_text: Maybe the Cowboys won't have room left to sign George Pickens to a long-term deal when the time comes. Cowboys management has repeatedly said Quinnen Williams was at the top of their list to secure a long-term agreement. They did that Monday. Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that the defensive tackle has agreed to terms on a three-year, $105.9 million extension. Williams had two years left on his deal, putting him on a five-year, $153.15 million deal. Williams, 28, will receive $101 million in guarantees. He is headed into his eighth NFL season, his first full season with the Cowboys, who acquired him from the Jets in 2025 for two high draft picks. Williams totaled 25 tackles, 1.5 sacks and an interception in seven games in Dallas last season. He made his fourth consecutive Pro Bowl.
author: Charean Williams

title: Will Howard: Everyone says preseason isn't real football, but to me, it is
summary: Last year as a rookie, Steelers quarterback Will Howard suffered a fractured hand in early August that kept him out of the team’s preseason games.
full_text: Last year as a rookie, Steelers quarterback Will Howard suffered a fractured hand in early August that kept him out of the team’s preseason games. That’s part of why it’s understandable that Howard — a sixth-round pick in the 2025 draft — is so excited to get his first pro exhibition opportunity this week when the Steelers host the Packers on Thursday night. “I’m so fired up. I can’t wait for the game ,” Howard said, via video from Mark Kaboly. "Obviously, I’m trying to take it day by day, and it’s still camp. But, sometimes you can’t help but look forward a little bit and start getting excited just to be out there and [get] live game reps — because I haven’t played in over a year in live game reps. I think the last time was the national championship. So, I’ve been champing at the bit for a while to get out there with the guys in a real game-like setting — uniform on, helmet on. “I just can’t wait. I think tomorrow we’re going to start looking at Green Bay a little bit, do some planning a little bit. I’m just really, really excited.” Howard added, via Chris Adamski of the Pittsburgh Tribune-Review, that he’s expecting to play “a good amount” on Thursday night. But to this point, head coach Mike McCarthy hasn’t set out definitive plans. No matter how long he’s out there, Howard is going to find Thursday night’s experience meaningful. "I know everyone says preseason isn’t real football ,” Howard said, “but to me, it is.”
author: Myles Simmons

title: Packers claim WR Chris Hilton off of waivers
summary: The Packers have added a wide receiver to the roster for the second time in as many days.
full_text: The Packers have added a wide receiver to the roster for the second time in as many days. They announced that they have claimed Chris Hilton off of waivers. They signed Kisean Johnson as a free agent on Sunday. Hilton signed with the Commanders after going undrafted this year and was waived over the weekend. He spent the last five years at LSU and had 41 catches for 780 yards during his time in Baton Rouge. Hilton and Johnson join Christian Watson, Matthew Golden, Jayden Reed, Savion Williams, Skyy Moore, Bo Melton, Will Sheppard, Isaiah Neyor, Kaden Prather, and J. Michael Sturdivant on the receiver depth chart in Green Bay.
author: Josh Alper

title: NFL Network returns to Xfinity, with RedZone good to go for Week 1
summary: Deal gets done in time for start of preseason.
full_text: With the full preseason slate starting in three days, Xfinity customers can stop worrying about not having access to NFL Network. Comcast and Disney struck a deal on Monday to return NFLN and NFL RedZone to the package. "We're pleased to have reached an agreement with The Walt Disney Company to bring NFL Network to our customers in time for the start of the preseason games and to offer NFL RedZone Channel at the beginning of the regular season," Comcast said in a statement. That's very good news for football fans, and it always seemed like the start of the season would be the real deadline for getting something done. NFL Network exited Xfinity on May 1, a month after Disney/ESPN took control of it. Both sides worked out their differences, and the customers will have the ability to consume the NFL-labeled channel and the popular whiparound view of Sunday afternoon games.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jared Goff not even thinking about retirement: "That's going to be a long time"
summary: Lions quarterback Jared Goff was asked today if he has given any thought to retiring.
full_text: '' Lions quarterback Jared Goff was asked today if he has given any thought to retiring. He said that's not even close to a consideration. "No, I'm right in the middle of it. No, I haven't," Goff said. Goff said he believes he has many, many years ahead of him of being a starting quarterback, and he would only walk away when "I don't think I can help a team win a championship." "I think that's going to be a long time," Goff added. The 31-year-old Goff is in his sixth training camp in Detroit and has now been a Lion longer than he was a Ram. Heading into his 11th season, he thinks he has many more good seasons ahead of him.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Steve Keim has ties to alleged scam artist who was recently found dead
summary: With 32 training camps up and running (and plenty of things happening in all of them), other stories can slip through the cracks for us.
full_text: With 32 training camps up and running (and plenty of things happening in all of them), other stories can slip through the cracks for us. Here's one that did, at least at first. Former Cardinals G.M. Steve Keim has ties to a man named Mohamed Coulibaly. A July 15 investigation from Jacob Adelman of Barron's alleged that Coulibaly led a scam that attempted to persuade professional athletes to invest in fake Shopify stores. Coulibaly was found dead in his pool earlier this month. Authorities are investigating. The original report from Barron's suggested that the company, Motion Ventures, had entered phony sales into a dashboard in order to make the businesses seem more profitable than they were. One shopping site, Dailyprodtrend, reflected a $5,000 order from someone in Luxembourg for 100 desktop humidifiers and 120 USB-powered cup warmers. The person living at the supposed shipping address told Barron's he never made the purchase. “Who needs 100 humidifiers and 120 cup warmers?” the man said. Three former NFL players told Barron's that they had lost, collectively, more than $1 million by investing in Motion Ventures. Coulibaly had denied, sort of, the allegations. “I strongly dispute a number of the factual assertions and characterizations contained in the Barron’s article and any follow-up reporting that relies upon them,” Coulibaly told the New York Post after the article was published. (By saying that he disputed "a number" of the assertions and characterizations, Coulibaly was implicitly saying he did not dispute at least some of them.) Keim's connection to the business can't be disputed. A November 2025 pitch deck for Motion Ventures, a copy of which PFT has obtained, identifies Keim as the "chief operation/growth officer." He's the only other person featured in the deck, along with Coulibaly. "Steve plays a critical role in guiding expansion strategy, evaluating new opportunities, and supporting leadership across divisions by navigating high-stakes decision-making, managing large budgets, and leading multidisciplinary teams as Motion Ventures continues to scale nationally and internationally," the pitch deck explains. The deck identifies several NFL figures as "notable clients and partners," including Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter, multiple other current and former Eagles players, Keim, and Seahawks G.M. John Schneider. (There's no indication that any of those individuals authorized their names to be used; PFT has learned that at least one of them did not even know his name was included.) Keim left the Cardinals in January 2023. In 2024, Keim joined Rich Paul's Klutch Sports Group as the general manager of the football division . Keim left Klutch Sports Group in March 2026. No arrests have been made and no charges have been filed in connection with the alleged scam, or in connection with Coulibaly's death.
author: Mike Florio

title: Patriots trade OL Caedan Wallace to Dolphins
summary: The Patriots won't release offensive tackle Caedan Wallace after all.
full_text: The Patriots won't release offensive tackle Caedan Wallace after all. Instead, news that New England was moving on from the 2024 third-round pick led to a trade. The Dolphins are acquiring Wallace and a 2029 seventh-round pick for a 2028 sixth-round pick, the Patriots announced Monday. The Patriots used the 68th overall pick in 2024 on the Penn State product. Wallace, 26, appeared in 10 games in his two seasons in New England. He played only eight snaps last season. The Patriots also announced the re-signing of long snapper Niko Lalos. The team initially signed Lalos on March 16, but released him on May 20.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bears sign WR Ray-Ray McCloud
summary: Veteran wide receiver Ray-Ray McCloud has found a new team.
full_text: Veteran wide receiver Ray-Ray McCloud has found a new team. The Bears announced McCloud's signing on Monday afternoon. They waived wide receiver Kyron Hudson with an injury designation to create room for McCloud on the 90-man roster. McCloud saw time with both the Falcons and Giants last season. He had six catches for 64 yards in four games for Atlanta and caught one pass for five yards in two appearances for the Giants. McCloud has also played for the 49ers, Steelers, Panthers, and Bills. He has 159 catches for 1,523 yards and two touchdowns for his career. He also has experience returning punts and kickoffs.
author: Josh Alper

title: Dolphins put K Zane Gonzalez on IR, sign DB Nick McCloud
summary: Zane Gonzalez's bid to win the Dolphins' kicking job came to an end on Monday.
full_text: Zane Gonzalez's bid to win the Dolphins' kicking job came to an end on Monday. The Dolphins placed Gonzalez on injured reserve. Gonzalez suffered an undisclosed injury over the weekend and head coach Jeff Hafley called him week-to-week in a press conference on Monday morning. Gonzalez can be released once healthy enough to play. Riley Patterson is now the only kicker on the 90-man roster in Miami. The Dolphins also announced that they have signed defensive back Nick McCloud and waived running back Anthony Hankerson. McCloud had 27 tackles and two passes defensed in 15 games for the Bears last season. He has also played for the 49ers, Giants and Bengals in his 63-game NFL career.
author: Josh Alper

title: Teddy Bridgewater: Retirement is official this time
summary: Teddy Bridgewater returned to the NFL after announcing his retirement at the end of the 2023 season, but he was back in uniform before the end of the 2024 season.
full_text: '' Teddy Bridgewater returned to the NFL after announcing his retirement at the end of the 2023 season, but he was back in uniform before the end of the 2024 season. Bridgewater said on Monday that his second retirement is going to be a lasting one. Bridgewater stepped away from the Lions this weekend and they placed him on the reserve/retired list on Sunday. "This time it's official," Bridgewater wrote in a post to his Instagram account. Bridgewater went on to recall his comeback from a 2016 knee injury that he described as "gruesome" and created doubt about his ability to play football again. Bridgewater returned to the Vikings before the end of the 2017 season and played for most of the next decade, but he wrote "this wheel of mine can no longer deal with something as simple as standing around on a turf field." The Vikings selected Bridgewater in the first round in 2014 and he went on to play for the Saints, Panther, Broncos, Lions and Buccaneers. He returned to the Lions as a free agent this offseason, but the newly signed Josh Dobbs is now set to back up Jared Goff in Detroit.
author: Josh Alper

title: NFL tweaks rules to allow coach's designee to initiate replay challenges
summary: The NFL will allow its 32 head coaches to designate a member of their staff to initiate replay challenges this season, Kevin Seifert of ESPN reports.
full_text: The NFL will allow its 32 head coaches to designate a member of their staff to initiate replay challenges this season, Kevin Seifert of ESPN reports. The head coach had been the only member of a team who could throw the red flag to challenge a play. Beginning this season, a member of the staff can take on that assignment from the head coach. But teams will be required to inform officials of that before the start of a game. The NFL did not announce the change at its annual meeting, but the tweak to the challenge system did not require votes from ownership. Rule 15, Section 1, Article 1(a) now reads: "The head coach or head coach's pregame challenge designee can initiate a challenge by throwing a red flag onto the field of play before the next legal snap or kick." Coaches challenged 151 plays in 2025, the highest total since 2019.
author: Charean Williams

title: George Pickens' 2026 season likely to be his Cowboys swan song after Quinnen Williams, Zay Flowers contracts
summary: Pickens' market continues to rise while Dallas just paid All-Pro DT Quinnen Williams
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys and their fan base need to treasure Pro Bowl wide receiver George Pickens while they still can because the 2026 season will likely be his last in Dallas.
While that is an incredibly gloomy thought early on in training camp, the time on the NFL calendar when hope springs eternal for all of the league's 32 teams, it's a realistic conclusion given the continual uptick in the wide receiver contracts market and what Dallas chose to prioritize: extending All-Pro defensive tackle Quinnen Williams on a reported three-year, $105.9 million deal with $101 million in total guarantees and $63.35 million fully guaranteed at signing.
The Baltimore Ravens inked two-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Zay Flowers to a reported four-year, $140 million extension on Aug 4. prior to the start of his fourth NFL season. That deal is identical to Minnesota Vikings 2022 NFL Offensive Player of the Year wide receiver Justin Jefferson's in both years and total contract value, with Jefferson earning $2 million more than Flowers in guaranteed money, $110 million to $108 million. In June, the Atlanta Falcons re-signed wide receiver Drake London , Pickens' 2022 NFL Draft classmate, to a four-year, $141.054 million extension with $99.87 million guaranteed, making him the third-highest-paid receiver in the league.
Pickens, meanwhile, is locked in on the franchise tag, which will pay him $27.298 million fully guaranteed in 2026 after the Cowboys decided not to engage with him and agent David Mulugheta in long-term contract talks this offseason. That's puzzling with Pickens fresh off producing a career year with 1,429 yards receiving and 9 receiving touchdowns on 93 catches. Ranking third in the entire league in receiving yards earned the 25-year-old the first Pro Bowl and All-Pro selections (second team) of his career. Neither Flowers nor London has registered as gaudy a receiving yards total as Pickens did last season.
He leads the trio in career receiving yards (4,270) and career yards per reception average (16.0), while London has the edge in career receptions (309) and a narrow lead in career receiving touchdowns (22). Pickens' 21 career receiving touchdowns are one behind his 2022 NFL Draft classmate. Translation: Pickens can now demand more money than both Flowers and London on a long-term deal with a straight face. That's a significant problem for Dallas for a multitude of reasons, despite Jerry Jones feeling like Pickens having to prove it again on the franchise tag is a win-win situation for both parties.
George Pickens just picked himself and CeeDee Lamb over ANY WR duo in NFL history 😤 🎤: @BMac_SportsTalk pic.twitter.com/n3yDGqMoPD
"This can be a very win-win thing that we've done here: us, George and George being on the team," Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones said at Dallas' opening training camp press conference . "Make no mistake about it: George could be a Cowboy for the rest of his career, and that would be a long time. Make no mistake about it. This [the franchise tag] just fit for us, and thank goodness it fit for him, and we got it done."
The love between Pickens and Jones is mutual ... until the two sides have to sit down at the negotiating table again next offseason.
"Super excited. I'm always super happy when someone thinks highly of me, so shout out to Jerry," Pickens said on July 30, via The Athletic .
Receiving yards per reception
Waiting to extend Pickens, rather than doing so when trading for him as a somewhat distressed asset in May of 2025, has come back to bite them. The talent was always there, and in 2025, Pickens showed how prolific he can be with a quarterback of Dak Prescott's caliber, rather than the mediocre carousel of passers Pittsburgh paraded through its franchise from 2022 to 2024.
Now that Williams is under contract with the Cowboys for the next five seasons, Dallas can get creative with how they structure or spread out the four-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle's salary cap hits. This deal could, in theory, give the Cowboys the wiggle room to squeeze a new contract for Pickens into their salary cap beginning in 2027. Will Jerry Jones be willing to do that though when Pickens' price on a new deal could potentially end up being similar to CeeDee Lamb's with another Pro Bowl campaign in 2026?
Playing the waiting game led Dallas to re-sign their present-day No. 88 to a four-year, $136 million extension with $82 million guaranteed back in 2024. Delaying those negotiations in tandem with Pickens puts the Cowboys in a position where they may feel like they have to choose between paying Lamb or Pickens. Dallas puts a premium on homegrown players they choose to extend, and Lamb has been everything the Cowboys have hoped for: he's developed into an All-Pro, five-time Pro Bowler who is also a team captain. Lamb isn't going anywhere, and there is a world where Jerry and Stephen Jones could attempt to get a deal done with Pickens.
Lamb himself is literally begging the Jones family to do what it takes to keep one of the NFL's most electrifying wide receiver duos together for the foreseeable future. Doing so would force Jerry and Stephen Jones to put up a high level of up-front cash spending on their roster, something they have resisted doing in years past. However, 2026 could perhaps be a new era in Dallas on that front. According to OverTheCap.com , the Cowboys $390.61 million in active cash spending is the second-most in the NFL in 2026 behind only the Baltimore Ravens' $393.54 million figure.
"I'm sure we can make a way," Lamb said, via Yahoo Sports . "I know it's going to be a little crazy, but I know we can make a way for this one. Listen, this is my advocation: '@ Jerry, can you please figure out a way? Let's figure it out. I don't care what needs to happen. Let's figure it out and it's going to get you a couple more championships.'"
Next offseason, if the Jones family ends up reverting to their typical, conservative spending approach, the Cowboys will likely end up either tagging and trading Pickens or allowing him to walk in free agency in exchange for a third-round compensatory draft pick, thanks to their inability to get ahead of the fast-evolving wide receiver market. Either outcome is deflating because Dallas successfully identified a high-level talent who could reach new heights within their high-powered offensive ecosystem. Choosing to procrastinate on addressing his long-term contractual future could lead to him ending up like Parsons: another All-Pro-caliber talent Dallas developed, going on to crush it with another NFL team for the long haul.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Quinnen Williams, Cowboys agree to massive $105.9M extension, making star DT one of NFL's highest-paid
summary: Williams' new three-year deal includes $101 million guaranteed and $63.35 million fully guaranteed at signing
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have reached an agreement with star defensive tackle Quinnen Williams on a mammoth extension, the team announced Monday . Specifically, it's a three-year, $105.9 million deal that will make Williams one of the highest-paid defensive linemen in the NFL , according to NFL Media .
Williams receives $101 million in total guarantees, including $63.35 million fully guaranteed at signing, per ESPN . That is the most guaranteed at signing for a defensive tackle in NFL history. His $35.3 million in average annual value ranks him just above Tennessee Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons ($35.27 million) and behind Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter ($38 million) for the second-richest in the league, per Over the Cap.
Williams and the Cowboys had reportedly been circling around this extension as training camp unfolded and, in a deviation from how previous negotiations have gone down with Jerry Jones, Dallas is getting out in front of locking the 28-year-old down. Under his previous deal (which was signed when he was a member of the New York Jets ), the former All-Pro was under team control through the 2027 season, but the guarantees within the deal ran dry after this season.
Quinnen Williams (Cowboys)
This furthers the investment the Cowboys are making with Williams after acquiring him in the midst of the 2025 season in a blockbuster trade with the Jets. Dallas landed Williams in exchange for defensive tackle Mazi Smith , a second-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft , and a conditional first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft (highest between the Cowboys and Packers picks).
This Williams extension is also just the latest in the Cowboys' concerted effort to fix the defense. On top of this extension, Dallas used its two first-round picks at the 2026 NFL Draft on defense, selecting Ohio State safety Caleb Downs at No. 11 overall and UCF edge rusher Malachai Lawrence at No. 23 overall. They also acquired linebacker Dee Winters in a trade with the 49ers , while signing the likes of edge rusher Rashan Gary , safety Jalen Thompson , and corner Cobie Durant in free agency.
This comes after a 2025 season in which the Cowboys' defense was among the worst in the NFL across the board. That includes allowing a league-worst 30.1 points per game.
Clearly, the Cowboys see Williams as a part of the solution to bring them out of the basement and back into playoff contention. Specifically, he should help improve a Dallas run defense that allowed 24 rushing scores in 2025 (tied with Buffalo for most in the NFL). Last season, Pro Football Focus gave Williams a 91.7 run defense grade, which ranked No. 1 among interior defensive linemen.
Williams entered the NFL as the third overall pick of the Jets in 2019 and has established himself as one of the top defensive tackles in the NFL. Overall, he was named a first-team All-Pro in 2022, and the Alabama product has received a Pro Bowl nomination in each of the past four seasons. Last season between Dallas and New York, he registered 53 tackles, 2.5 sacks, and 12 quarterback hits.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Trevon Diggs' stunning NFL downfall: How former All-Pro went from $97M Cowboys deal to fighting for his career
summary: The 27-year-old Diggs tried out for the Lions on Sunday as he attempts to revive a career that once looked destined for stardom
full_text:
Two-time Pro Bowl cornerback Trevon Diggs ' NFL career is on life support entering what would be his seventh season in the league in 2026.
Diggs, 27, remains a free agent days away from the first full week of preseason action across the NFL. His latest look from an NFL team came Sunday when he tried out for the Detroit Lions , per the NFL's transaction wire .
Detroit is dealing with the surprise loss of 2024 first-round pick cornerback Terrion Arnold after he was charged with four counts of kidnapping and four counts of armed robbery . The Lions could use more depth at the position in a major way. Yet Diggs remains unsigned.
Diggs being a check-the-treads-on-his-tires guy during what were supposed to be the prime years of his career is a tale of misfortune. He exploded onto the scene in his second season with the Dallas Cowboys in 2021 after being selected in the second round of the 2020 NFL Draft , leading the NFL with 11 interceptions, including a league-leading two pick-sixes. That earned him the only first-team All-Pro nod of his career. Diggs followed that campaign with another Pro Bowl selection in 2022 after intercepting three passes and registering 14 passes defended.
Those back-to-back Pro Bowl years drove Cowboys owner/general manager Jerry Jones to do something he rarely does: extend a star player early. He inked Diggs to a five-year, $97 million contract in training camp in 2023 with a year remaining on Diggs' rookie deal, tying him to Dallas through the 2028 season.
That's when the wheels began to fall off for Diggs. He tore his ACL in practice before the Cowboys' Week 3 game at the Arizona Cardinals , knocking him out for the remainder of the season.
After thriving in defensive coordinator Dan Quinn's man coverage-heavy defense with a league-leading 15 interceptions from 2021 to 2023, Diggs failed to find his footing in other schemes after Quinn left to become head coach of the Washington Commanders in 2024. He publicly complained about defensive coordinator Mike Zimmer's defense causing him to "play a little bit slower" in 2024 before getting into a war of words with Dallas' 2025 defensive coordinator, Matt Eberflus.
The 2025 season started on the wrong foot for Diggs after he opted to train on his own in Miami instead of at The Star, the team's facility, while working his way back from a chondral tissue graft procedure on his knee in January of that year. Diggs' decision to do so during voluntary organized team activities led Jerry Jones and team EVP and COO Stephen Jones to dock his 2025 salary by $500,000 .
Then came the public scheme rebuttal.
Eberflus had Dallas running zone coverage on 86.6% of its defensive snaps through the first five weeks of the year, the highest rate in the NFL, according to TruMedia. The Cowboys played man coverage on just 7.9% of their defensive snaps during that span, the lowest rate in the NFL. That was a stark contrast to Dallas' defensive glory years of the 2020s (2021-23 under now-Commanders head coach Dan Quinn), when the Cowboys ran man coverage at the third-highest rate in the NFL at 33.8%, per TruMedia.
After a slow start, Dallas deployed man coverage at a higher rate (14.1% of its defensive snaps) in a 37-22 Week 5 win at the New York Jets , in which the Cowboys had their then-best defensive game of the year. That's when Diggs rubbed Dallas' man coverage success in Eberflus' face with his postgame comments.
"When we have pressure like that, we can call whatever. We can call prevent [defense] and it would've won," Diggs said . "I definitely felt like it [playing more man coverage] worked. We got off the field. The D-line was getting back there so fast. We say when they get back there fast it's called Instant Grits. You know how you make the Instant Grits in the packet? You don't want oatmeal. Oatmeal takes too long. You want Instant Grits. We had Instant Grits [on Sunday]."
When CBS Sports asked Eberflus at the time about Diggs' comments and whether they would lead to more man coverage going forward, the then-Dallas DC clapped back with a sarcastic quip about Diggs' grits metaphor, saying he doesn't like grits.
"We're going to make the decisions based on what we feel is best. Based on the matchups, based on what we have. I don't like grits either," Eberflus said with a smirk.
Just a couple of weeks later, Dallas ruled Diggs out the Friday before its Week 7 matchup with the Washington Commanders after the cornerback suffered a concussion in an accident at his home . While Diggs was in concussion protocol, the Cowboys placed him on injured reserve because of a setback with his knee. They didn't reactivate him until Week 16 as Cowboys coaches continually asked him to "do everything the right way."
Dallas then waived him after its Christmas Day victory in Washington in Week 17, and the Green Bay Packers , the football home of Diggs' BFF Micah Parsons , claimed him a day later.
Despite Green Bay being starved for capable cornerback play, Diggs played just one snap in its wild card round loss at the Chicago Bears , stumbling while attempting to tackle a Bears ball carrier.
The hope for Diggs now is that a team suffers an injury or two in the preseason and becomes willing to gamble on a diminished version of the once-All-Pro cornerback while hoping he can be a good soldier and keep the peace. His 20 career interceptions are tied with Lions All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph for the third-most in the NFL this decade.
An ideal landing spot would likely be the Commanders, which would reunite Diggs with Quinn and his older brother, Stefon. Outside of Washington or Detroit, it's unclear where Diggs' next NFL fit could be.
author: Garrett Podell

title: NFL training camp injuries tracker: Latest updates on Christian McCaffrey, Luther Burden III and more
summary: Keep track of every major injury, setback, and recovery timeline across the league as teams prepare for the upcoming season
full_text:
NFL training camp is typically a time for optimism. Hope abounds that all the changes a team made during the offseason -- whether hiring a new coach, signing players in free agency, acquiring them via trade or selecting them in the draft -- will lead to a better season than the year before.
The one thing every team needs to avoid for that to happen, of course, is injuries. A major injury can derail plans for the entire year, especially if it happens to a key player. Alas, injuries happen every year, and it's important to keep track of who's hurt, when and how the injury happened, and how long they might be sidelined.
With that in mind, consider this your one-stop shop for all the injury news coming out of NFL training camps during July and August.
New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn delivered some troubling news on Tuesday, as first-round pick tight end Kenyon Sadiq is going to miss some time after "having a little setback." There's not an exact timetable for his return, although Glenn doesn't think Sadiq will miss the season opener. The rookie had offseason hernia surgery.
The No. 16 overall pick was the top tight end in his past draft, setting career highs with 51 catches for 560 yards and eight touchdowns for the Oregon Ducks last season. No FBS tight end caught more touchdowns than Sadiq. He was expected to make an immediate impact on this Jets offense, but New York does have another capable tight end in Mason Taylor.
Bailey injured his ankle during Saturday's practice and will likely be considered day-to-day, according to head coach Aaaron Glenn, who also said the linebacker should be "fine."
McCaffrey missed Monday's practice with what the team called "tightness," which obviously doesn't provide much in the way of information. CMC is coming off a season during which he led the NFL with 413 touches, then recorded 37 more in two playoff games. He has a history of breaking down following seasons with huge workloads, so any missed practice time is obviously worth monitoring.
Pearsall is expected to undergo season-ending surgery on his ongoing PCL injury that has been an issue since last season. Niners general manager John Lynch said that Pearsall is expected to make a full recovery.
James is expected to miss time after he suffered a rib fracture during Monday's practice. The 49ers have yet to offer a timeline for his possible return.
Mustapha sat out Wednesday's practice as he is dealing with a hamstring strain. Like James, Mustapha's injury occurred during Monday's practice.
Bosa missed Saturday's practice with "soreness," but 49ers fans can breathe a sigh of relief because head coach Kyle Shanahan said the team has no concerns regarding the star defensive end.
Allen, who had been enjoying a strong start to his first NFL camp, was carted off the field on Saturday after colliding with Kaiir Elam on a special teams drill. ESPN later reported that test conducted on Allen revealed a shin bruise. Nothing was torn or broke, so he appears to have dodged a bullet.
During Saturday's practice, Johnson went down and was unable to put any weight on his right leg as he was aided off the field. He was also seen clutching the area around his Achilles. Despite being carted to the locker room, ESPN reports that Gardner-Johnson merely suffered a lower calf strain, so he avoided any serious injury.
Johnson, 28, was enjoying a solid start to training camp. A seven-year veteran, Johnson's NFL accolades includes a Super Bowl win with the Eagles and leading the NFL in interceptions back in 2022.
Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski that Tagovailoa is working through an injury and will the early portions of training camp. With Tagovailoa sidelined, the Falcons have signed veteran backup Cooper Rush .
Regarding fellow quarterback Michael Penix's status, Stefanski recently said that he still hasn't been cleared for full team activities. Penix is still working his way back from a torn ACL that was sustained during Week 11 of the 2025 season.
Atlanta brought its Aug. 4 practice to a close after Walker went down with a leg injury. It is feared to be a torn ACL for the second-year edge rusher. His Falcons teammates took knees and surrounded him while trainers evaluated him, and he was then carted off the field. Walker sustained the injury in an 11-on-11 two-minute drill at the Falcons' non-padded practice.
The Panthers placed Scourton on injured reserve after he suffered a torn ACL in his right knee on the first day of training camp . Scourton was reportedly in tears as he left the field, and his teammates came over to hug him as he exited.
Head coach Dave Canales said at the time that Scourton would undergo an MRI to determine the severity of the injury, and the results confirmed the second-year edge rusher had torn his ACL.
While the initial plan was for Brazzell to recover without surgery, a second opinion determined that a procedure to repair the moderate LCL tear in his left knee is the best course of action, according to The Athletic . The surgery will force Brazzell to miss his entire rookie season, which is a much longer timeline than the eight weeks that was presented in the immediate wake of his injury. The LCL tear does not appear to be related to the knee issue the third-round pick dealt with leading up to training camp.
Former first-round pick Xavier Legette reportedly went down hard on his back and head while attempting to make a catch during drills on Tuesday. After remaining on the turf for some time, the wideout was helped up and carted off the field, per WCNC .
While it doesn't appear Legette suffered a serious, season-ending injury, it was another scare for a team that has already suffered too many losses in training camp. Legette is still looking to live up to his No. 32 overall pick billing. In 15 games played last year, he caught 35 passes for 363 yards and three touchdowns.
The Saints were hit with awful news on Wednesday as it appears that Bresee suffered a season-ending ACL tear during Wednesday's practice. A former first-round pick, Bresee has quietly become one of the NFL's best defensive linemen. The Saints will now look to try to find his replacement for the upcoming season.
The 2025 first-round pick's Wednesday practice came to an abrupt end after his leg buckled . Stewart -- who played in just eight games during his rookie season -- was carted off the field shortly after sustaining the injury. According to ESPN , Stewart suffered a hyperextended knee with no ligament damage, which seems like best-case scenario given the initial reporting around the injury.
McNeill left Friday's practice with a neck injury suffered in a pile-up during 11-on-11 drills, according to the Detroit Free Press . The Lions are already shorthanded in the secondary and can scarcely use an injury up front. McNeil wasn't himself last season after returning from a torn ACL and it's not a great sign to see him banged up early in camp this year.
The Lions signed former Panthers center Cade Mays to a three-year deal worth $25 million this offseason to replace Graham Glasgow. However, Mays suffered a wrist injury that will force him to miss a "significant period of time," per head coach Dan Campbell. Mays will return at some point this year, "but it will be down the road."
Campbell told reporters that new running back Isiah Pacheco suffered an MCL sprain in practice, but that he is expected to be ready for the season opener vs. New Orleans.
Brown told NFL Media that he dislocated his thumb at a Patriots practice. Brown returned to practice and caught several passes. "Thumb out of place," he said. "You keep going." This is certainly going to be an important injury to monitor.
Bryant suffered a hyperextended knee, bone bruise and small fracture during the Bears' practice on Monday and is expected to miss 8 to 10 weeks, per ESPN . It's a brutal blow for a Bears secondary that was already one of the thinner units on the team. It's also rough for Bryant, who signed a big free-agent deal…
author: Jared Dubin

title: CeeDee Lamb is practically begging Jerry Jones to pay George Pickens: Can Cowboys afford another $40M WR?
summary: Lamb is urging the team to "figure it out" to keep Pickens long term, and the Cowboys seem open to the idea
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys sport one of the best wide receiver duos in the NFL .
CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are each considered top-10 receivers, as evidenced by a recent poll of our staff here at CBSSports.com, where they checked in sixth and seventh in the league. (They also finished exactly sixth and seventh in ESPN's annual poll of league executives .) We also ranked them as the No. 2 duo in the NFL , behind only Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins of the Cincinnati Bengals .
Of course, it's possible the duo could have a short-lived tenure. Last year was the first season Lamb and Pickens played together, and it was the final season of Pickens' rookie-scale contract. But he was so good in 2025 (93 catches for 1,429 yards and five touchdowns, earning Pro Bowl and second-team All-Pro honors) that the Cowboys decided they couldn't possibly let him hit the open market, so they franchise-tagged him rather than allowing him to leave in free agency without a significant return.
Pickens eventually signed the one-year franchise tender instead of negotiating a long-term deal with the team, so it's possible this coming season will be his last in Dallas. But Lamb doesn't want that to be the case. In fact, he's practically begging the Cowboys to make sure it isn't, because he wants to form a dynamic duo with Pickens for years to come and help the Cowboys win the Super Bowl trophy that has eluded them for more than 30 years.
"I'm sure we can make a way," Lamb said, via Yahoo Sports . "I know it's going to be a little crazy, but I know we can make a way for this one. Listen, this is my advocation: '@ Jerry, can you please figure out a way? Let's figure it out. I don't care what needs to happen. Let's figure it out and it's going to get you a couple more championships.'"
Lamb is already one of the highest-paid receivers in the league, having signed a four-year, $136 million contract extension in 2024. The top of the receiver market has crept up since he signed that deal, though, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba setting a new receiver record with a $42.15 million average annual value on the contract extension he signed this offseason.
If Pickens plays well enough this year that the Cowboys feel comfortable giving him a new long-term deal, it seems likely he'd top the $40 million-per-year mark. That would make the Cowboys the only team in the league investing that much money in the wide receiver position.
The Bengals and Detroit Lions have also made significant, top-of-the-market investments in their top two receivers, but the contracts for Higgins and Jameson Williams are much smaller than the one Pickens is likely to command if he has another season like he did in 2025. (The same was true of the Miami Dolphins when they had investments in Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle , as well as the Philadelphia Eagles when they were paying A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith .)
Things could also get complicated because the Cowboys are surely going to want to extend star defensive tackle Quinnen Williams , whom they acquired last year from the Jets and who is now only the 10th-highest-paid interior defensive lineman in the league. And, of course, the Cowboys have the NFL's second-highest-paid quarterback in Dak Prescott , who makes $60 million per year. (They have only themselves to blame for that one, having badly bungled negotiations with Prescott multiple times.)
Still, it can be done if the team wants to do it and is willing to lay out the up-front cash to make it happen. Dallas has always had a reputation as a more free-spending team than it actually is, with Jerry and Stephen Jones constantly referencing the fact that there is only so much pie to go around, even for star players. But Jerry does seem at least somewhat open to keeping Pickens (and Williams) in the fold with Lamb and Prescott over the long term.
"Yeah, just you got to tell me the rest [of our spending], too," Stephen Jones said, again via Yahoo Sports . "At some point, you've got to figure that out. But no, I think it's realistic."
It remains to be seen whether that realistic scenario will become the Cowboys' actual reality, but if Pickens has another strong season, it'll be hard to make an argument against retaining him on a long-term deal.

title: Aaron Donald return could happen this week, plus predicting NFL players who could make 2027 Hall of Fame
summary: Here's everything you need to know about the NFL for Aug. 10
full_text:
