title: ‘I don’t want to stop progress:’ Why Sean Payton handed play-calling to Davis Webb
summary: The news on Monday is that Davis Webb will be on the sideline this season. As Sean Payton said, it’s not as if he and Webb are splitting atoms, but the Denver Broncos new offensive coordinator will call plays from the sideline as opposed to the Broncos’ coaching booth. It’s where Webb has spent his […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL, CO - AUGUST 7: Offensive coordinator Davis Webb, center, talks with his quarterbacks during practice on Friday, August. 7, 2026, at Broncos Park in Centennial, Colo.(Photo by Timothy Hurst/MediaNews Group/The Denver Post via Getty Images) | Denver Post via Getty Images The news on Monday is that Davis Webb will be on the sideline this season. As Sean Payton said, it’s not as if he and Webb are splitting atoms, but the Denver Broncos new offensive coordinator will call plays from the sideline as opposed to the Broncos’ coaching booth. It’s where Webb has spent his time as the quarterback coach in Denver, and clearly feels the most comfortable. Even if Payton and Webb haven’t even discussed it yet. Broncos HC Sean Payton tells @heykayadams that OC Davis Webb will be on the sidelines calling plays this season pic.twitter.com/8JbaDnIKs4 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 10, 2026 “I just think his presence as a teacher and as a coordinator, everyone’s different,” Payton said to the media on Monday. “He and I haven’t even talked about it and I know he felt the same way I did. So we both answered your questions prior to a meeting. We still haven’t had that meeting, but that’s probably … Yes, I see that happening.” Payton went a little deeper into why he gave Webb playcalling duties on Up and Adams with Kay Adams on Monday . He also told her that Webb would call plays from the sideline. Payton told Adams that he saw something special in Webb. At the same time, Payton also told her that he’ll still be involved in the offense and play calls. “Remember driver’s ed when it was in high school?” Payton said to Adams. “And you had the steering wheel but the teacher had the brake and they were right next to you? This is before they went online. So I’ll be next to him.” “Remember driver’s ed… and you had the steering wheel but the teacher had the brake and they were right next you… I’ll be next to [Davis Webb].” Sounds like Broncos HC Sean Payton will still be very involved in offensive play-calling @Broncos | @heykayadams pic.twitter.com/dQMHubcOTU — Up & Adams (@UpAndAdamsShow) August 10, 2026 Payton then immediately said: “He’s not going to fail. He’s going to be great at it. And I’m going to make sure that he is. And we’ll be better as a team for it. … I think this guy has a chance to be special.” Payton then again acknowledged that he wouldn’t do it if he didn’t think it would make the Broncos better. “It was win driven,” he said to Adams. “It was, man, I don’t want to be the one to stop progress, if that’s the case.” As for Webb calling plays from the sideline, quarterback Bo Nix is a fan. “I’ve always loved it, from a quarterback to a play caller, when they’re on the sideline with me,” Nix said to the media on Monday. “I feel like they get the feel of the game a little bit differently. It’s obviously seeing the game from a different vantage point, but I think they get to feel the emotions on the sideline. They get to feel the comments from us coming off the sideline, what we’re seeing and all that kind of stuff. From his point of view and playing quarterback his whole career, I think that’s just where he feels comfortable. “A lot of former quarterbacks like to call it from the sideline. I don’t know that’s the case, but that just seems to be how play callers roll. I like when the play caller is there with me and I can come off and have the eye-to-eye conversation. We can sit down and look at the pictures and go through them together and really get to hear from him and not have to call up to the office or get on a headset. I think the eye-to-eye communication is really important, so I’m excited that he’s going to be down there with us.”
author: Ian St. Clair

title: 2026 Denver Broncos Training Camp: Day 9 News and Notes
summary: Day 9 of Broncos Camp is in the books, and it’s officially game week! The Broncos have their preseason opener on Friday when they travel to Atlanta to take on the Falcons. However, we still have three training camp practices this week ahead of that game. Today, the Broncos were back in pads after a […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL, CO - AUGUST 10: Head coach of the Denver Broncos Sean Payton runs practice during training camp on Monday, August. 10, 2026, at Broncos Park in Centennial, Colorado. (Photo by RJ Sangosti/MediaNews Group/The Denver Post via Getty Images) | Denver Post via Getty Images Day 9 of Broncos Camp is in the books, and it’s officially game week! The Broncos have their preseason opener on Friday when they travel to Atlanta to take on the Falcons. However, we still have three training camp practices this week ahead of that game. Today, the Broncos were back in pads after a day off on Sunday and had some positive injury news! Luke Wattenberg, Marvin Mims, Jordan Turner, Nate Adkins, Eyioma Uwazurike and Sean Fresch Jr. all returned to practice in some capacity, so that was good to see. Star wide receiver Jaylen Waddle remained out, but appears close to returning, so that’s good news too. However, the Broncos did suffer another soft tissue injury, this time to veteran running back JK Dobbins, who left practice early with a trainer. Hopefully, like the rest of the soft tissue injuries this camp, Dobbins will be okay after a few days. After practice, Payton told reporters they’re working to eliminate these injuries and spent more time stretching today, so we’ll see how that goes in the future. Future Hall of Famer Sean Payton on Top 10 All-Time Wins & why I should feel good about the adjustment in play-calling with Davis Webb. Did we waddle again? Maybe! @UpAndAdamsShow https://t.co/BB6gybT320 — Kay Adams (@heykayadams) August 10, 2026 In today’s report, we have Bo Nix calling wide receiver Pat Bryant a positive part of training camp, offensive coordinator Davis Webb calling plays from the sideline, Payton talking injuries, all the injury updates, news and notes, tweets from camp, quotes, and more! Pat Bryant has been a positive part of training camp Wide receiver Pat Bryant has been the talk of training camp thus far. The second-year wide receiver have been making plays all of camp, has been praised by Sean Payton, Davis Webb, and his teammates, and now by quarterback Bo Nix. Pat Bryant, aka Patty 🧊, hype is real @heykayadams asked Broncos HC Sean Payton "how they're going to keep Bryant off the field " He said "we're not" pic.twitter.com/28mrMR6KQR — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 10, 2026 Nix met with the media today after practice and told reporters that Bryant has been a “positive part of training camp” and that the talented receiver plays with an “edge”. When asked about Bryant’s performance in camp thus far, Nix told reporters that he has been extremely consistent but also available the whole training camp. This availability has allowed him to get valuable reps and continue his development. “I think for him, he’s been extremely consistent but also he’s been available the whole training camp. He’s taken a lot of reps and just competed very well. He just has a great edge to him, and I think when he gets out there against our [defensive backs], he competes at a high level and he makes great catches. We see it all the time with him and other guys and they’re just continuing to improve. For him, it’s only Year 2, so he has a lot left in his tank that we’re able to see at practice that I think he’s going to be able to show this year during the season. Overall he’s been a positive part of training camp for sure.” Nix is right. The Broncos receiver room has been a bit banged up during camp. Jaylen Waddle has missed multiple practices, veteran Courtland Sutton is going through load management, and Marvin Mims missed a day due to injury as well. Bryant has been the constant presence at receiver for Nix, and it seems like the two have built up some chemistry. We’ll see if that chemistry continues to grow as we progress through camp and the preseason, but it’s becoming more and more clear that Bryant is going to have a big part in this offense. Davis Webb will call plays from the sideline As we know, Head Coach Sean Payton handed playcalling duties to offensive coordinator Davis Webb this offseason. This will be the first time that Webb will be a coordinator or play caller, so there was some talk about where Webb will be on gamedays. Earlier in camp, Payton told reporters that he wasn’t sure where Webb will be, but the other day, Webb said he would prefer to be on the sideline. Well, Webb got his way as Payton told reporters and Kay Adams that Webb will be calling plays from the sideline this season. Broncos HC Sean Payton tells @heykayadams that OC Davis Webb will be on the sidelines calling plays this season pic.twitter.com/8JbaDnIKs4 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 10, 2026 Payton was asked what the deciding factors will be in determining where Davis Webb will be calling plays this season. He told reporters, “It’s not like we’re splitting the atom”, and that he will likely call plays from the sideline and that he and Webb have the same vision there. He added that Webb’s presence as a teacher and Coordinator will be beneficial, and while the two haven’t officially had a conversation on the topic yet, he does see it happening. “I just think his presence as a teacher and as a coordinator, everyone’s different. He and I haven’t even talked about it and I know he felt the same way I did. So we both answered your questions prior to a meeting. We still haven’t had that meeting, but that’s probably… Yes, I see that happening.” Webb wanted to call plays from the sideline; Payton wants him to call plays from the sideline and has done the same throughout his career as a coach, and we can also add quarterback Bo Nix into the mix of people wanting Webb on the sidelines. He told reporters he always loved it when a play caller is on the sideline with him. Added they can feel the game a bit different, have a feel for the emotions, and that he’s excited he’s going to be down there with us. “I’ve always loved it from a quarterback to a play caller when they’re on the sideline with me. I feel like they get the feel of the game a little bit differently. It’s obviously seeing the game from a different vantage point, but I think they get to feel the emotions on the sideline. They get to feel the comments from us coming off the sideline, what we’re seeing and all that kind of stuff. From his point of view and playing quarterback his whole career, I think that’s just where he feels comfortable. A lot of former quarterbacks like to call it from the sideline. I don’t know what that’s the case, but that just seems to be how play callers roll. I like when the play caller is there with me and I can come off and have the eye-to-eye conversation. We can sit down and look at the pictures and go through them together and really get to hear from him and not have to call up to the office or get on a headset. I think the eye-to-eye communication is really important, so I’m excited that he’s going to be down there with us.” Frankly, I think this is the right move. Nix and Webb have a strong working relationship, and it will be best for both parties and the team if he’s on the sideline. They have enough veteran coaches to put up in the booth to communicate with Webb/Payton if needed. Webb on the sidelines working with Nix, the offense, and Payton is the right choice in my opinion. Sean Payton looking into the amount of soft tissue injuries Since Sean Payton was hired by the Broncos, they went from being one of the most injured teams in the NFL to being one of the least injured. A big part of that was the hiring of Beau Lowery and his strength and conditioning staff. However, through the first week and a half of Broncos Camp, they have been dealing with multiple soft tissue injuries. Players like Jaylen Waddle, Marvin Mims, and today running back JK Dobbins have all suffered soft tissue injuries. Thankfully, they have all been minor and the players have or will return to practice only after sitting out a handful of practices Despite this, Payton told reporters that…

title: Broncos announce that they have activated LB Jordan Turner off the NFI
summary: On Monday morning, the Denver Broncos announced that reserve linebacker Jordan Turner has passed his physical and will be activated off the NFI list. He has been there since the start of camp, but for the first time this summer, Turner is on the practice field and participating in Broncos Camp. Turner joined the team […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - DECEMBER 21: Jordan Turner #55 of the Denver Broncos celebrates during the third quarter of an NFL football game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field At Mile High on December 21, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Monday morning, the Denver Broncos announced that reserve linebacker Jordan Turner has passed his physical and will be activated off the NFI list. He has been there since the start of camp, but for the first time this summer, Turner is on the practice field and participating in Broncos Camp. ILB Jordan Turner has passed his physical and been removed from the Non-Football Injury list. 📰 » https://t.co/2c9W9GmjAV pic.twitter.com/dkzoeZRlQr — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) August 10, 2026 Turner joined the team last season as an undrafted free agent and was a standout player during training camp and the preseason. However, he was among the team’s final cuts, but he did sign on to their practice squad. He would be signed to the active roster during the season and appear in 7 games for the Broncos, playing primarily on special teams. Now, in year two with the Broncos, Turner will be competing for a spot on the team’s 53-man roster and the LB3 job behind starters Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad. The battle for the final two linebacker spots, including that LB3 role, is expected to be a competitive battle throughout the remainder of training camp and into the preseason. Turner will be competing with Karene Reid, who made the 53-man roster last season, Levelle Bailey, and rookies Red Murdock and Taurean York. So, this will be a roster battle to watch as we near the preseason opener this Friday when the Broncos take on the Atlanta Falcons. Special teams will be a big contributing factor to who makes the team and eventually gets that LB3 job. Turner had 117 special teams snaps last season in limited action, so he does have a bit of a leg up on the competition. Karene Reid also had 171 special teams snaps, so he will be someone to keep an eye on as well. Rookie Red Murdock seems like a strong contender for a roster spot and special teams role due to his ability to force fumbles, while Taurean York may have the best instincts of the entire group. So, it should be a fun battle to watch in the coming days and weeks, but getting back Jordan Turner could be a potentially significant addition to the Broncos’ roster.

title: Game week returns to Broncos Country
summary: For the first time since last season’s AFC Championship game, the Denver Broncos will play football this Friday night in Atlanta against the Falcons. While just a meaningless exhibition game, it’s one of the necessary steps toward shocking the football heart back into a beating rhythm for the upcoming season. Speaking of ‘rhythm,’ Broncos play-caller […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 17: Calvin Throckmorton #76 of the Denver Broncos tackles Drake London #5 of the Atlanta Falcons during the first quarter at Empower Field At Mile High on November 17, 2024 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the first time since last season’s AFC Championship game, the Denver Broncos will play football this Friday night in Atlanta against the Falcons. While just a meaningless exhibition game, it’s one of the necessary steps toward shocking the football heart back into a beating rhythm for the upcoming season. Speaking of ‘rhythm,’ Broncos play-caller Davis Webb had this to say: I think I’m looking forward to everyone getting the rhythm — our staff, our players, in and out of the huddle. We’ll learn something every game, every drive. Then we’ll kind of review it as the game goes and especially postgame and try to get three good opportunities before Kansas City on ‘Monday Night.’ It will be rocking, and I know they’ll be a good team. So, it’ll be a good opportunity for us to kind of feel that out because most of these practices are scripted, and we kind of know what we’re going to run and they kind of know what they’re going to run. Not that you need me to tell you, but don’t expect to see many, if any, starters on the field on Friday. If they do find their way onto the field, it won’t be more than a series. Instead, get ready, Broncos Country, to fall in love with that fourth string fullback that flashed against a group of guys with no prayer of making Falcons (or any other team’s) roster – or as I call it, the Joe Don Duncan effect. The gameplans on both sides of the ball will be simplified versions of a limited playbook. Expectations will be focused around execution at every position around every opportunity. Who will rise to the occasion and who shrinks? Are points of emphasis from training camp registering with the players in a way that translates on the field or is there difficulty grasping those core concepts? Expectations in Denver remain high after a disappointing end to an almost-stellar 2025 season. Last season’s excitement won’t return in totality on Friday night, but it’s an important step along the way to getting there. Watch these games to evaluate the position battles. Watch these games to see how Davis Webb and Sean Payton work together (or don’t) to manage the game. Watch these games to root on the Denver Broncos. It ain’t real football yet, but at least it’s football-ish.

title: Detroit Lions announce broadcast crew for 2026 preseason
summary: One of the cool perks of watching NFL preseason games is that teams get to tap local broadcasters for their televised games. On Monday, the Lions announced that for the 2026 preseason, their FOX broadcast crew would once again feature play-by-play announcer Jason Benetti, color analyst T.J. Lang, and Patti Cesarini as the crew’s sideline […]
full_text: Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell, right, shakes hands with Jason Benetti during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Monday, July 28, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co One of the cool perks of watching NFL preseason games is that teams get to tap local broadcasters for their televised games. On Monday, the Lions announced that for the 2026 preseason, their FOX broadcast crew would once again feature play-by-play announcer Jason Benetti, color analyst T.J. Lang, and Patti Cesarini as the crew’s sideline reporter. Benetti returns for his second season as the Lions preseason play-by-play announcer, adding to his already many prominent broadcasting roles in the sports world. Currently, Benetti is in his third year as the Detroit Tigers play-by-play announcer, works nationally for FOX Sports (covering the NFL, college football, college basketball, and baseball), and is the lead announcer for NBC’s Sunday Night Baseball. Here’s an excerpt from the Lions press release announcing Benetti’s return to his preseason role with the Lions: “Recognized for his excellence in sports journalism, he was named the 2024 Michigan Sportscaster of the Year and is a two-time Illinois Sportscaster of the Year. A proud graduate of Syracuse University (2005) and Wake Forest Law School (2011), he also serves as an ambassador for the Cerebral Palsy Foundation, using his platform to support inclusivity and awareness in sports.” Lang, a Metro Detroit native, played on the offensive line locally at Eastern Michigan, won a Super Bowl with the Packers in 2011, and finished his NFL career in Detroit. Cesarini, a new addition to the crew for 2026, played volleyball locally at Oakland University and brings a versatile resume as a reporter, and according to the press release, she has experience covering football, basketball, hockey, and volleyball throughout her career. Here’s an excerpt from the Lions press release: “She brings a strong on-air presence, game insight, and a natural connection to athletes and fans. She has also worked as an in-game host for the United Shore Professional Baseball League and interned with the Windy City ThunderBolts, combining deep sports knowledge with vibrant, engaging storytelling.” Of note, for the Lions’ first preseason game, Benetti is unavailable and will be replaced by Jack Kizer, a play-by-play broadcaster for college sports games on FOX Sports and the Big Ten Network.

title: Teddy Bridgewater reveals reason for sudden retirement
summary: On Sunday, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell informed the media that backup quarterback Teddy Bridgewater was going to “step away” from the team, but stopped short of saying that the veteran quarterback was planning to retire. “Yeah, I mean, I think only he can truly answer that, but I feel like this is where it’s […]
full_text: Detroit Lions quarterback Teddy Bridgewater (5), left, talks to quarterback Jared Goff (16) after practice during mini camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Tuesday, June 16, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co On Sunday, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell informed the media that backup quarterback Teddy Bridgewater was going to “step away” from the team , but stopped short of saying that the veteran quarterback was planning to retire. “Yeah, I mean, I think only he can truly answer that, but I feel like this is where it’s at for sure right now,” Campbell said. “This is where it needs to be and where he felt. And his biggest worry was letting us down—that’s the type of guy he is—and he’s not.” On Monday, Bridgewater took to social media to confirm he was indeed retiring , and released the following statement (emphasis is from the author): “It’s so crazy 10 years ago around this time, I suffered one of the most gruesome knee injuries the game itself, it’s players and some doctors had ever seen. Everything football related since 2016 had been fueled by the “experts” predicting that I would never play football again. We really showed them by playing 10 more seasons! However, this wheel of mine can no longer deal with something so simple as standing around on the turf field. This thing just doesn’t recover the same way it did years ago so I rather officially hang it up . It’s finally run its course and when the body speaks to me, I have to listen so that I can be in one piece and available for my children as they grow up. The game of football was beyond great to me and owes me nothing at all. I really did things my way Lol.” View this post on Instagram Bridgewater was incredibly well-liked, especially amongst his teammates, and many of them—present and former—responded to his retirement post with well wishes and love. Here’s a small sampling: Jared Goff: “Legend!” Amon-Ra St. Brown: Raising hands emoji Alim McNeill: Fire emojis Tyleik Williams: Heart and prayer hands emojis Alex Anzalone: “My guy!!!!! Congrats Bro” Jackson Meeks: 100 emojis and handshake emoji Shelby Harris (Giants DT): “much love and respect my guy” Detroit Lions official: Thank you, Teddy” New Orleans Saints official: “Teddy 2 Gloves” Minnesota Vikings official: Purple heart emojis NFL official: “Legendary” with two glove emojis

title: Lions training camp notes, Day 10: Big day for Detroit’s secondary
summary: The Detroit Lions ramped the intensity back up at training camp for Day 10. The pads were back on, and most of the starters were back in the lineup following a bit of a veteran rest day on Sunday. If you want a full participation list, check out our latest Lions injury news update. Here’s […]
full_text: Detroit Lions safety Thomas Harper (12), left, and safety Chuck Clark (36) during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Monday, August 10, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions ramped the intensity back up at training camp for Day 10. The pads were back on, and most of the starters were back in the lineup following a bit of a veteran rest day on Sunday . If you want a full participation list, check out our latest Lions injury news update . Here’s everything else I noticed from Monday’s practice. Several defensive backs stand out There has been a lot of understandable consternation about the Lions’ secondary with Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph out with injury and Terrion Arnold off the team entirely, but the secondary has been a pleasant surprise early in camp, and that was on display several times during Monday’s practice. So much so that quarterback Jared Goff had to give it up to the DBs. “Obviously the front seven gets the notoriety right now with all the big-time players, but the back end’s doing a good job too with the veteran guys,” Goff said. “I thought Chuck (Clark) made a great play on me today and almost had another one on me. Avonte (Maddox)’s doing a great job, D.J. (Reed), when he’s out there is doing a great job. They’re competing, it’s fun, and it’s competitive.” Clark, indeed, was one of my biggest standouts of practice. In an early red-zone drill, Devin White deflected a pass intended for Jahmyr Gibbs, and Clark picked it off. Then, on a third-and-short in a live drive, Clark jumped a crossing route to Amon-Ra St. Brown to deflect the pass, and it landed in Nick Whiteside’s hands. Clark also continues to be a physical and instinctive presence in the run game. Rock Ya-Sin continues to have competitive battles with both Jameson Williams and Amon-Ra St. Brown, and he logged a decisive tackle for loss in the run game as well. Among the reserves, Christian Izien made a big impression Monday, as well. He split time as the first-team nickel and second-team safety, and made several plays on the day, including an interception where he clearly read the eyes of Luke Altmyer while dropping into a zone. But his biggest impact this year may come on special teams, where he continually reps high and wins his one-on-ones. In my opinion, he’s closing in on the gunner job opposite Khalil Dorsey. Two notable DB exceptions While I’ve been impressed with the above defensive backs, it’s been much more of a mixed bag with two cornerbacks: Ennis Rakestraw and Roger McCreary. On Monday, Campbell referred to both of their camps as “up-and-down” and he seemed particularly tough on Rakestraw. “He’s had some ups and downs. He needs to string a few days together here of some good stuff, but he can do that, and he’s gifted,” Campbell said. Rakestraw has pretty firmly dropped down to the second-team defense, with Nick Whiteside jumping into the starting lineup (with Reed out). To make matters worse, Rakestraw hasn’t performed particularly well on special teams, while Whiteside is making some strides there. McCreary continues to get some first-team nickel reps and outside work with the reserves, and Monday was a perfect example of the highs and lows of his camp. He got flagged for defensive holding—a common problem this camp. But he also avoided an Isaac TeSlaa block to blow up a screen, and had perfect coverage on an Amon-Ra St. Brown wheel route to force an incompletion. First-team defense starts strong, offense finishes The first-team offense and defense faced off for three “real” drives, where the plays count, and they often went live tackling. The initial drive was all defense. Starting deep in their own zone, the offense managed just 6-7 total yards on a pair of plays to open the drive. On third-and-short, Goff tried to hit Sam LaPorta on a crossing route, but Chuck Clark jumped in front of it, tipped the ball into the air, and Nick Whiteside was there to pick it off. The second drive, starting around midfield, was much more successful for the offense. While they ignored what probably would’ve been an Aidan Hutchinson sack (on Blake Miller), they got themselves into a third-and-3 and converted this time. Goff threaded the needle between Clark and Thomas Harper for a big 20-yard gain to Sam LaPorta. After a nice 7-yard run from Jacob Saylors and a big run stuff from Jack Campbell, Goff connected with Amon-Ra St. Brown for a 15-yard touchdown on a post corner route that beat Whiteside. The offense would get the better of the defense in a final situational drill. The situation: Offense is up 23-20 1:53 left in the game Each team has 2 timeouts Ball starting on own 48-yard line The defense started promisingly with a tackle for loss on first down. But on second down, Goff pulled a convincing play-action, and threw a bomb to Jameson Williams, who had beaten Ya-Sin by a single step. A perfect pass resulted in Williams down at the 1-yard line (50-ish yard gain), and the offense kneeled the rest of the clock away. Miscellaneous The play of the day came from Jahmyr Gibbs. He bounced a run outside and was squared up with Nick Whiteside, the only player holding contain on that side of the field. Gibbs absolutely shook him for what was around a 10-yard touchdown run. Another strong day from UDFA linebacker Erick Hunter. He absolutely blew up a pass to Jackson Meeks, jarring the ball loose on a big collision, and was all over Tyler Conklin on a short pickup. He also repped with the primary kick return team, a good sign of his standing there—although the injury absences of Malcolm Rodriguez and Damone Clark are noteworthy. Devin White had a series in which he made a play—either good or bad—on nearly every single down. Working on red zone plays… White bit hard on a play-action pass, resulting in a wide-open Brock Wright for a 10-yard gain. He dropped into coverage and batted a ball intended for Jahmyr Gibbs that was intercepted by Clark. Sam LaPorta beat White into the flats for a fourth-and-short conversion and possible touchdown. White bit again on play-action, leaving Wright wide open for a 2-yard touchdown. When running downhill as a blitzer or run defender, White has been excellent all camp. And even when lined up one-on-one in coverage, he can hold his own. It’s just when offenses can utilize his own aggressiveness against him that he gets into trouble. A typical Jake Bates day: Makes: 39, 39, 46, 47, 51, 54, XP Misses: 47, 51

title: Lions injury report: Latest news on Isiah Pacheco, Juice Scruggs
summary: The big injury news of the day for the Detroit Lions was the untimely injury to starting center Cade Mays, who is expected to miss 8-10 weeks with a fractured wrist. Lions coach Dan Campbell provided some extra updates on Monday, and there were some more developments from training camp Day 10. Headlining the news […]
full_text: Detroit Lions running back Isiah Pacheco (10) practices during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Friday, July 31, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The big injury news of the day for the Detroit Lions was the untimely injury to starting center Cade Mays, who is expected to miss 8-10 weeks with a fractured wrist . Lions coach Dan Campbell provided some extra updates on Monday, and there were some more developments from training camp Day 10. Headlining the news is an update on running back Isiah Pacheco and interior offensive lineman Juice Scruggs, who very well may be this team’s starting center come Week 1. Returned to practice: WR Cedrick Wilson Jr. DT Mekhi Wingo Wilson only missed a few practices with an undisclosed injury, and he was right back in the lineup on Monday. It’s good news for a player in tight competition for the WR5/6 jobs. Wingo also only missed a few practices, although it appeared he’s still working his way back into team drills. Appeared to be limited: QB Josh Dobbs (not injury related) As expected, Dobbs was held out of team work since he just joined the team. That said, he did get plenty of throws in during individual drills. Working with trainers, not practicing: CB D.J. Reed For the first time since suffering a minor groin injury, Reed was getting some training work during practice, sprinting up the hill. That is usually a good sign that he’s on the path to jumping back into the lineup soon. The last update from Campbell was that it wasn’t a “major issue” and “he’ll be back.” Not practicing: RB Isiah Pacheco (undisclosed) RB Sione Vaki (eye, broken nose) WR Greg Dortch (undisclosed) OT Giovanni Manu (NFI) G Juice Scruggs (undisclosed) EDGE Payton Turner (back) DT Aidan Keanaaina (undisclosed) LB Damone Clark (undisclosed) LB Jimmy Rolder (leg) S Kerby Joseph (PUP, knee) S Brian Branch (PUP, Achilles) S Avonte Maddox Campbell finally gave an update on Isiah Pacheco, and it’s mostly good news. The Lions’ backup running back has an MCL sprain, and he’ll still be sidelined “a little bit,” but Campbell isn’t concerned about it jeopardizing his start to the season. “We feel pretty good about him being ready to go, certainly when the season gets here,” Campbell said. “So, I’m not concerned about that.” Vaki was outside at practice with his teammates and wasn’t wearing any sort of protection for his face. His eye was still bloodshot from being poked, but he seems in good spirits. There has been no official timeline for his return. It sounds like Juice Scruggs—who will suddenly be thrust into the starting center competition following Mays’ broken wrist—will be returning to the lineup relatively soon. Campbell called it a soft-tissue injury. “Juice is dealing with a little bit of a injury, a soft tissue,” Campbell said. “So, he won’t be out there today. It’ll be still a few more days before he’s back, but certainly Juice is a candidate.” Until then, it will be Seth McLaughlin at center with the starting lineup, as it was for all of Monday’s practice. Maddox was absent from Monday’s practice with no explanation. We’ll see where he’s at when we talk to Campbell next. In his place, Thomas Harper was a starting safety for most of practice alongside Chuck Clark. Injured during practice OT Devin Cochran (undisclosed) Cochran left practice before the team broke for team drills and did not return. The team did not provide any update on his status. As a result of his absence, we saw a lot of Miles Frazier in at right tackle on the second team with Larry Borom at left tackle.
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: Lions center Cade Mays to miss ‘significant’ time with wrist injury
summary: The Detroit Lions suffered their most significant training camp injury on Sunday, as prized free agent Cade Mays suffered a wrist injury and will miss a “significant period of time.” According to a report from Ian Rapoport, Mays’ injury is expected to sideline him for “roughly 8-10 weeks,” meaning he should be back by the […]
full_text: Aug 2, 2026; Allen Park, MI, USA; Detroit Lions center Cade Mays (64) looks on during Detroit Lions training camp at Meijer Performance Center. Mandatory Credit: Paul Barnick-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions suffered their most significant training camp injury on Sunday, as prized free agent Cade Mays suffered a wrist injury and will miss a “significant period of time.” According to a report from Ian Rapoport, Mays’ injury is expected to sideline him for “roughly 8-10 weeks,” meaning he should be back by the middle of the regular season. “Cade Mays had a wrist injury,” Lions coach Dan Campbell said at his Monday morning press conference. “He will be out for a significant period of time. He will be back for the season at some point, but it’ll be down the road.” Following an unanticipated retirement of Frank Ragnow in 2025 and a lackluster performance from Graham Glasgow during the regular season, the Lions entered the 2026 offseason looking to make significant upgrades at the center position. The Lions acted quickly in free agency, targeting Mays and signing him to a three-year, $25 million contract and hoping he could anchor the center of the offensive line. Through the first two weeks of training camp, Mays performed well, and the Lions were optimistic he would be a pivotal player for them this season. “Of course, you hate it. I hate it for him, because I felt like he was having a good camp and he had grown so much in our system just in spring,” Campbell continued. “So, in that regard, yeah. And for us, too. But at the same time, again, there’s a reason why we’ve got Juice (Scruggs) here, too, and some of these other guys. And they’re going to get a look.” To help bolster their center position, the Lions also traded with the Texans (as part of the deal for David Montgomery) for Juice Scruggs. During training camp, Scruggs filled multiple reserve roles on the offensive line, including backing up Mays at center, while also filling in at left guard with the starters until Christian Mahogany returned to training camp practices. Unfortunately, Scruggs is also dealing with a soft tissue injury at this time, but he is expected to recover soon and should jump into the competition to replace Mays and will likely be considered the early favorite for the job. “Juice is dealing with a little bit of an injury—a soft tissue—so he won’t be out there today,” Campbell shared. “It’ll still be a few more days before he’s back. But certainly Juice is a candidate.” In addition to Scruggs, the Lions also have two more players with center experience, including Michael Niese—who was the Lions’ backup center in previous seasons—and Seth McLaughlin, who will be working with the starters in Monday’s practice. “McLaughlin is going to get looks, obviously. He’ll probably run mostly with the ones today,” Campbell continued. “Niese has also done it.” But the Lions won’t be satisfied simply filling an open spot with a reserve, and they will explore all their options to find the best starting five players to deploy on the offensive line, including continuing starting right guard Tate Ratledge’s cross-training at center. “Ratledge is going to work (at center). I don’t see him doing team (drills at center), but we’ve got to get him back up to speed with doing a little snapping, just in case,” Campbell explained. On a positive note, the Lions still have half their training camp practices and three preseason games to figure out what works best for them to be ready for the season. “We’re going to find the best five,” Campbell said. “We will find the best five, and we’re trying to find that before camp starts, but, look, if this goes into the season, it does. But at some point, we will find the best five and where they belong, and they’ll be ready.”
author: Erik Schlitt

title: Bubble Watch: Several Detroit Lions training camp battles heat up on offense
summary: The Detroit Lions aren’t even a full week into 2026 training camp, but we’ve already seen some surprises when it comes to the roster. The depth chart may not be exactly what we expected, and injuries have forced some roster reshuffling. For Week 2 of our Roster Bubble series, it’s not surprising that there have […]
full_text: Detroit Lions wide receiver Dominic Lovett (19) walks off the field after practice during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Thursday, July 30, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions aren’t even a full week into 2026 training camp, but we’ve already seen some surprises when it comes to the roster. The depth chart may not be exactly what we expected, and injuries have forced some roster reshuffling. For Week 2 of our Roster Bubble series, it’s not surprising that there have been some significant shifts—although most are on defense. Today, let’s re-examine the players on the roster bubble on offense. View Link Quarterback: Assumed in: Jared Goff NEW TO BUBBLE WATCH: Josh Dobbs: 9 “IN votes Luke Altmyer: 4 votes ( up 4 ) With Teddy Bridgewater’s retirement, the Lions suddenly have a very interesting backup quarterback competition. Most of us understandably have veteran quarterback Josh Dobbs winning the competition, but Erik Schlitt stands in sole defiance, picking rookie Luke Altmyer to win the battle. The other three Altmyer votes come from staffers who are choosing to carry three quarterbacks. Admittedly, Altmyer has done enough to warrant consideration, but his performance in the preseason will likely be the biggest determinant of his future. Running back: Assumed in: Jahmyr Gibbs, Isiah Pacheco NEW TO BUBBLE WATCH: Sione Vaki: 11 votes Jacob Saylors: 9 votes ( no change ) NEW TO BUBBLE WATCH: Jabari Small: 0 votes We downgraded Sione Vaki from “assumed in” to “on the bubble” simply because of his injury. At this point, it’s unclear if his broken nose and poked eye will warrant a trip to the short-term IR, but no one is taking the bait yet. Instead, this Bubble Watch is a debate over whether the Lions will keep a fourth running back. Not only do most of us agree (9 of 11) that they will, but everyone is currently picking Saylors over Small. Wide receiver: Assumed in: Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Isaac TeSlaa, Greg Dortch Cedrick Wilson Jr.: 7 “IN” votes (down 3) Dominic Lovett: 6 votes (up 4) Tom Kennedy: 0 vote (no change) The WR 5/6 battle is really heating up. After a strong start to camp, veteran Cedrick Wilson has cooled off a little and is currently sidelined with an unknown absence. Lovett, meanwhile, is on the opposite trajectory. He started camp with some familiar struggles, but has started to come on in the last few practices with some increased opportunities. The staff is about as split as they can get: 4 have Lovett over Wilson 5 have Wilson over Lovett 2 have the Lions keeping both (6 total WRs) Tight end: Assumed in: Sam LaPorta, Brock Wright OFF BUBBLE WATCH: Miles Kitselman (IR), Anthony Firkser (IR) Tyler Conklin: 11 “IN” votes (no change) Jackson Meeks: 5 votes (up 5) NEW TO BUBBLE WATCH: Thomas Gordon (0 votes) It’s been an injury-filled camp for the tight end position. Sam LaPorta is still working his way back. Tyler Conklin is just now seeing the field for the first time since camp opened. And last week, the Lions lost two tight ends to injuries that landed them on IR (Kitselman, Firkser). As a result, Conklin’s spot on the roster feels safer than ever, but Jackson Meeks is starting to get warranted consideration for Detroit keeping a fourth tight end. While Meeks has had an up-and-down camp, I’ve started to see some growth, and I do wonder if Detroit is still considering playing a high amount of 13 personnel, which would almost certainly require a fourth rostered tight end. Offensive tackle: Assumed in: Penei Sewell, Blake Miller, Larry Borom Colby Sorsdal: 0 votes (no change) Devin Cochran: 0 votes (no change) None of the staff believes Detroit would be warranted in keeping a fourth offensive tackle, and the top three are firmly set. Miles Frazier’s ability to kick outside will make it hard for Sorsdal or Cochran to warrant a spot on the 53-man roster. Interior offensive line: Assumed in: Tate Ratledge, Cade Mays, Christian Mahogany, Miles Frazier Ben Bartch: 11 votes (no change) Juice Scruggs: 11 votes (up 1) Seth McLaughlin: 0 votes Michael Niese: 0 votes We haven’t seen many changes to the interior offensive line predictions all camp, but I wonder if that could change soon. For one, Scruggs has been sidelined a few practices for undisclosed reasons. It remains unclear if he’s dealing with a serious injury or not. Then there’s Bartch. He missed nearly two weeks of training camp and is just now starting to get worked into some team drills. But coach Dan Campbell offered some mixed feelings on Bartch in his Sunday press conference. “I’d be lying to you if I said I wasn’t hopeful he would have been out there more than now, but I also know there’s no setbacks, anything like that and he’s a veteran guy,” Campbell said. “From what we know about him and the short time we’ve been around him, he’s a guy that, it means something to him. He’s smart, he’s conscientious, all those things.” “… There’s a reason he’s here, we think he brings outstanding competition. He’s got a shot, but certainly he’s behind the mark. I mean, he’s missed some days and that’s just part of coming off an injury. That’s the hand you’re dealt.” The problem is that there has not been a clear reserve beyond Bartch that has stuck out for good reasons.

title: Dan Campbell reveals Detroit Lions’ plan for starters in preseason opener vs. Bengals
summary: This offseason, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell has publicly played with the idea of playing starters in the preseason—a departure from the team’s standard strategy. But when it comes to the team’s preseason opener this upcoming Thursday against the Cincinnati Bengals, it appears most of the team’s starters will not be suited up. “I really […]
full_text: Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell reacts to a play against the New York Giants during the first half of a preseason game at Ford Field in Detroit on Friday, Aug. 11, 2023. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co This offseason, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell has publicly played with the idea of playing starters in the preseason—a departure from the team’s standard strategy. But when it comes to the team’s preseason opener this upcoming Thursday against the Cincinnati Bengals, it appears most of the team’s starters will not be suited up. “I really don’t see playing a lot of our guys,” Campbell said. “We’ll play some of them. We’ll play some of our guys that are in these, we’ve got some competitions going on at spots, but you ask about (Jared) Goff, I don’t see Goff playing. And we’ll kind of gauge it as we go here.” Goff won’t play, but the Lions certainly have an interesting quarterback situation brewing after Teddy Bridgewater’s retirement . Undrafted rookie quarterback Luke Altmyer has been getting second and third-team reps in training camp since Bridgewater’s departure, and he’s set to take a significant amount of snaps on Thursday. However, Campbell said they plan on also playing whichever veteran quarterback they sign— which turned out to be Josh Dobbs —despite joining the team just a few days before the preseason opener. “Certainly Altmyer’s going to take a heavy load and then anybody else we get, we’ll get them up to speed as fast as we can and give them some reps,” Campbell said. As for Campbell’s initial intentions on playing starters in the preseason, it appears the Lions coach will consider that in Week 2 of the preseason—their sole home exhibition game against the Commanders on Saturday, August 22. “I think more of mine are the questions will be coming next week, when we start getting into the Washington week, because that was kind of where I always targeted like, alright, this may be where we need to play our guys,” Campbell said. “That’ll be the first one is kind of where I was thinking.”

title: 8 standouts from Day 9 of Detroit Lions training camp
summary: The Detroit Lions returned to practice Sunday for an early afternoon session after taking Saturday off. After four padded practices in five days this past week, the Lions took things relatively easy, electing to practice in shells during a session that lasted under two hours. With nearly 25 players either sidelined by injury or receiving […]
full_text: ALLEN PARK, MICHIGAN - JULY 29: Skyler Gill-Howard #50 of the Detroit Lions looks on during Detroit Lions Training Camp at Detroit Lions Meijer Performance Center on July 29, 2026 in Allen Park, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions returned to practice Sunday for an early afternoon session after taking Saturday off. After four padded practices in five days this past week, the Lions took things relatively easy, electing to practice in shells during a session that lasted under two hours. With nearly 25 players either sidelined by injury or receiving veteran days after participating only in warm-ups and walkthroughs, there were also only a handful of full-team 11-on-11 periods. Given the more mild-mannered nature of practice, one skirmish aside, the list of standouts is limited and should be taken with a grain of salt. Below are my eight biggest standouts from the day. Defensive tackle — Sykler Gill-Howard With several players along the defensive front mostly inactive Sunday, the sixth-round rookie took advantage of the additional opportunities and was a bit of a shop wrecker, emerging as the definitive biggest standout of the day. Gill-Howard told Pride of Detroit after practice that he’s starting to feel like himself again after an injury ended his last college season in October. “The first half of training camp went very poorly. I hold myself to a high standard and it took a while for me to click, having (not) been playing since October, my injury,” Gill-Howard said. “So when I got back out there in pads, it was kind of like, ‘Ah, do I still got it?’ in a sense. My body just doesn’t feel right. But as the days went on, I started giving myself grace, like, ‘Man, you haven’t been out here. Take some time. Take some time. Give yourself grace.’ And now it’s starting to click. I’m not where I want to be yet, but I’m definitely on the right path.” He credited veterans Alim McNeill and Levi Onwuzurike as two voices who helped pick him back up after he was feeling down following those first few days in pads. During the first team period with the second-team defense, Gill-Howard recorded a would-be sack of Luke Altmeyer after beating Melvin Priestly. On the very next play, he combined with Chris Smith for a submarine-sandwich tackle for loss on the running back. Later, during one-on-one pass-rush drills, Gill-Howard took losses against Tate Ratledge and Christian Mahogany but gained valuable reps against the first-team guards. He followed those up with two wins of his own, using a powerful punch to beat Priestly before recording another victory against Michael Niese. Gill-Howard saved his best work for the end-of-game one-minute drill, when he found himself on the field with the first-team defense and made the most of the opportunity. On back-to-back snaps against Mahogany, Gill-Howard generated clean pass-rush wins. The first resulted in immediate pressure and a would-be sack that forced Jared Goff to dirt the ball. On the next snap, Gill-Howard generated pressure again. Goff likely still gets the throw off in a full-contact setting, but the play resulted in a hurried incompletion after what appeared to be miscommunication with Greg Dortch. For a rookie who admittedly wasn’t pleased with how he opened training camp, Sunday was an encouraging example of Gill-Howard making the most of increased opportunities and showing tangible development. Running back — Jahmyr Gibbs The player with $67.5 million worth of game-breaking ability looked exactly like the type of player who keeps defensive coordinators up at night. While evaluating the run game during a practice in shells lacks some clarity without full contact, Gibbs had a handful of plays that showcased his warp-speed ability. On two potential explosive runs, Tyleik Williams was standing in the backfield on plays that could have resulted in no gain, but Gibbs still found a way to create. During the first-team session, Gibbs rapidly hit the hole off a combo block and second-level seal from Tate Ratledge and Blake Miller. Later, Gibbs cut backside behind left tackle Miles Frazier and appeared to have an off-to-the-races potential 90+ yard acceleration touchdown. Earlier in that same period, with the offense backed up at its own 1-yard line, Gibbs made a decisive cut to get upfield, escape dangerous territory, and pick up more than five yards. Gibbs showed out in the passing game as well, starting with a crossing route where he beat Devin White during seven-on-seven drills. Playmaker. pic.twitter.com/arbt66eC9R — Detroit Lions (@Lions) August 9, 2026 Then came arguably his play of the day. During the end-of-game scenario, the offense faced a must-have third-and-10. Gibbs hauled in a miraculous 17-yard catch on a wheel route amid a sea of defenders, securing the ball over White’s outstretched hands to move the chains. Gibbs added another short reception in the flat a few plays later. For anyone concerned about Gibbs potentially returning rusty, Sunday’s practice was a reassuring step in the right direction. Quick Hitters WR Dominic Lovett — With St. Brown and Williams mostly inactive, Lovett took advantage of the additional opportunities. He made a vice-grip, full-extension contested catch over the middle, showcasing a skill set we haven’t often seen from him. Later, during the get-out-of-the-end-zone period, Lovett found himself wide open as a safety valve on a deep dig from Altmeyer with plenty of catch-and-run potential ahead of him. WR Greg Dortch — Dortch made a short curl reception when the offense was backed up near its own end zone, but his biggest play came during the end-of-game scenario. He hauled in a 30-plus-yard post over the middle after beating Roger McCreary in coverage. Dortch continues to look like the WR4, although he did drop a punt during special teams drills. CB Nick Whiteside — Another practice where Whiteside repped ahead of Ennis Rakestraw and continued to look like the team’s No. 3 outside cornerback. He ended practice with an interception near the goal line on a 20-yard desperation heave from Jared Goff during the end-of-game scenario. DE Anthony Lucas — With several defensive ends out, Lucas received valuable first-team reps throughout practice, from the opening full-team periods through his work as the rush end during the end-of-game scenario. Lucas wasn’t overly notable during one-on-one drills but did record a pull-and-rip win against Blake Miller. LB Troy Reeder — After moving around to different linebacker spots during his first few days of camp, Reeder received valuable work as the second-team MIKE linebacker. His best rep came on a stuff of Jabari Small, when Reeder diagnosed the run quickly, beat the blocker to the hole, and delivered a downhill thump at the line of scrimmage. S Avonte Maddox — After a full week of practice, Maddox remains entrenched as a first-team safety and showed off his range throughout Sunday’s practice. He stayed over the top of an early deep shot from Goff to Lucky Jackson and twice quickly closed to the sideline on passes to the flat—one to Jahmyr Gibbs and another to Jacob Saylors.

title: Discussion: Should the Detroit Lions trade for a backup quarterback?
summary: To the surprise of many, quarterback Teddy Bridgewater stepped away from professional football, leaving the Detroit Lions in need of further depth. They filled that vacancy with haste, signing veteran Joshua Dobbs mere hours after Bridgewater’s departure was announced. While the quarterback room has returned to three-players deep, is that deep enough? Jared Goff is […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 01: Joshua Dobbs #9 of the Arizona Cardinals passes the ball during the third quarter against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on October 01, 2023 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images To the surprise of many, quarterback Teddy Bridgewater stepped away from professional football , leaving the Detroit Lions in need of further depth. They filled that vacancy with haste, signing veteran Joshua Dobbs mere hours after Bridgewater’s departure was announced. While the quarterback room has returned to three-players deep, is that deep enough? Jared Goff is the starter and key cog of the franchise. Now that Dobbs enters the fold, the backup quarterback position becomes a true battle between him and undrafted rookie Luke Altmyer. Altmyer was signed by the Lions after the 2026 NFL Draft, meaning he has an extra few months of familiarity with the Lions, but Dobbs’ familiarity with the NFL could give him the edge down the road. Neither Dobbs nor Altmyer are among the elite backups in the league—after all, there is a reason why Dobbs remained unsigned and Altmyer went undrafted. If something were to happen to Goff atop the depth chart, are the Lions really comfortable with either of these players stepping into the lineup? Today’s Question of the Day is: Should the Detroit Lions trade for a backup quarterback? My answer: No. When news of Bridgewater’s retirement was first revealed, there were two thoughts at the forefront of my mind. Firstly, this was an excellent opportunity for Altmyer to stake a claim at a roster spot, regardless of whom else the Lions sign. The second is that Goff is so integral to this offense that almost no available quarterback can replace his production—what really matters is finding a quarterback that can lend a hand in the film room. With Dobbs in the fold, I think that the Lions have all they need in their quarterback room. Dobbs checks a lot of boxes for the Lions. He has familiarity with Drew Petzing from their time in Arizona, including eight starts. Although the Arizona Cardinals went 1-7 in those games started by Dobbs, it is worth remembering that their roster was subpar at best, a supporting cast including James Conner, Trey McBride (before his ascension to elite tight end), Marquise Brown, and a rookie Michael Wilson. Dobbs himself was not awful in those games either, throwing for eight touchdowns, five interceptions, and 1,569 yards across those eight games, as well as scrambling for 258 yards and three touchdowns. When you examine the other free agent quarterbacks still available on the market, only players like Jimmy Garoppolo, Russell Wilson, and Trevor Siemian have more starts than Dobbs. When you factor in Dobbs’ intangibles (he is known as “the Passtronaut” for a reason), he is about as good of a backup as you can sign in the middle of August—experienced, athletic, smart, and, best of all, inexpensive. Via trade, you might be able to get an upgrade, but not without a larger price tag. Looking around at NFL rosters, there is a bevy of veteran backups with starting experience, such as Marcus Mariota, Carson Wentz, or Andy Dalton. However, are any of these players such an upgrade over Dobbs to warrant trading away assets? I personally do not think so. You can also consider former draft picks that have fallen out of favor. Players like Will Levis, Spencer Rattler, and Anthony Richardson are no longer viewed favorably for their respective teams, so a change of scenery would make sense. Yet these players have fallen down the depth chart for a reason—would it truly benefit Detroit to take on a reclamation project at an important position during a pivotal season? If Goff gets hurt, I personally would not want a player like Levis or Richardson stepping in. For as high as their ceilings are, I want a backup to have a safe floor. With Dobbs and Altmyer on the roster, I think the Lions are in a decent position. At the end of the day, Goff is irreplaceable to this team, and any injury replacement would be treading water at best—good quarterbacks are hard to find in this league. Preseason has not yet started. Let us give Dobbs and Altmyer some time to show if reinforcements are truly needed. Join the conversation! title: Green Bay Packers announce 1st ‘unofficial’ depth chart of training camp
summary: The Green Bay Packers have announced their first depth chart of training camp. While it’s “unofficial,” it’s our first look at how the Packers (or at least their PR team) want us to think about this roster. You can give it a look for yourself below, and I’ll add some of my thoughts. Offense The […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - JANUARY 10: Anthony Belton #71 of the Green Bay Packers looks on from the field during an NFC Wild Card Playoff game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on January 10, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers have announced their first depth chart of training camp. While it’s “unofficial,” it’s our first look at how the Packers (or at least their PR team) want us to think about this roster. You can give it a look for yourself below, and I’ll add some of my thoughts. Offense The skill positions are pretty chalky. The trio of Christian Watson, Jayden Reed and Matthew Golden is “starting,” with Davion Williams, Bo Melton and Skyy Moore backing them up, and Isaiah Neyor and J. Michael Sturdivant are on the outside looking in on the two-deep. Chris Brooks getting the nod over MarShawn Lloyd as the second-string back is semi-interesting, but Brooks has never really been given full drives before, like other Packers backs, as he’s been more of a situational blocker than a ball-carrier in Green Bay. Where it’s actually newsy is on the offensive line, where Anthony Belton remains as the starting right guard, despite Jager Burton, Jacob Monk and Donovan Jennings pushing for his job. Jennings and second-year lineman John Williams, who is playing all five positions for the Packers in camp, got the nod on the two-deep over Travis Glover, who at this point last year was considered to be a near-roster lock before he suffered a season-ending shoulder injury. Defense The big thing that stands out on the starting line of the depth chart is that it’s Devonte Wyatt and Karl Brooks starting on the defensive line, not Javon Hargrave. Hargrave is a second-stringer here, along with Warren Brinson. On the edge, Barryn Sorrell appears to have a lead to be the Packers’ starter opposite Lukas Van Ness, which isn’t surprising considering that the duo is pretty much getting first-look opportunities every day in camp. Slightly interesting: rookie Dani Dennis-Sutton is being listed as a third-stringer behind Collin Oliver and Brenton Cox Jr., but the whole group will rotate heavily. Cornerback is another position of intrigue, as Keisean Nixon and Carrington Valentine are listed as starters over Brandon Cisse and Benjamin St-Juste, despite all four corners getting significant reps with the first-team defense in camp (when healthy). Kamal Hadden, who recently returned to practice, is also listed as the team’s number two slot defender, despite safety Kitan Oladapo playing the role of Javon Bullard’s replacement in practice. Hadden hasn’t played the slot in Green Bay in regular-season action before, so it’ll be interesting to see if he gets some of those looks in the preseason or if the Packers’ two newly signed safeties mean that Oladapo is freed up to play the slot this summer. Special Teams Matt Orzech, who is still on the PUP list with a short-term calf issue, is still ahead of veteran Cal Adomitis on the long snapper depth chart. Adomitis was signed at the start of camp due to Orzech’s injury. Skyy Moore is listed as the starting punt returner and kick returner for the Packers, with Savion Williams and Pierre Strong Jr. backing him up on kicks and Will Sheppard and Jaden Nixon backing him up on punts. My guess: Strong, Sheppard and Nixon don’t make Green Bay’s initial 53-man roster , barring injuries at their offensive positions.

title: Packers Training Camp Recap: Javon Bullard’s foot injury revealed
summary: During Sunday’s practice, Green Bay Packers safety and starting slot defender Javon Bullard dropped out with an apparent foot injury. Going into Monday, we did not know the severity of the injury until the after practice locker room availability. While he wore a boot while being sidelined on Monday, Bullard claimed that he has a […]
full_text: ASHWAUBENON, WISCONSIN - JULY 31: Javon Bullard #7 of the Green Bay Packers rides a bike during the Green Bay Packers training camp at Ray Nitschke Field on July 31, 2026 in Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images During Sunday’s practice, Green Bay Packers safety and starting slot defender Javon Bullard dropped out with an apparent foot injury. Going into Monday, we did not know the severity of the injury until the after practice locker room availability. While he wore a boot while being sidelined on Monday, Bullard claimed that he has a bone bruise, with the biggest symptom being swelling, and that the team is just being precautionary. He told the press after practice, with the boot off, that “ If we had a game tomorrow, I’d play .” So there’s some (relatively) good news, especially after Bullard’s preferred backup in the slot, Johnathan Baldwin, was waived with an injury designation yesterday to make room for the team adding two new receivers . Beyond the Bullard news, here’s what you need to know from practice today. Injuries Both Edgerrin Cooper (foot) and Zaire Franklin (excused travel) returned to practice today after the starting linebackers weren’t participants in camp on Sunday. Tight end Luke Musgrave (neck), edge defender Micah Parsons (knee), defensive lineman Jordon Riley (Achilles) and long snapper Matt Orzech (calf) remain on the PUP list. Orzech should be the next man off the PUP list, based on how the Packers’ decision-makers have talked about that group of players’ injuries. The non-participants in practice, beyond the PUP list, were Bullard, running back Josh Jacobs (groin), receiver Matthew Golden (toe), receiver Jayden Reed (foot), tight end Josh Whyle (neck), cornerback Domani Jackson (undisclosed) and cornerback Carrington Valentine (hamstring). The only new injury added to the list was Bullard’s. Offense Starters: Love Lloyd Swinson – Dabney Williams – Neyor Morgan – Burton – Rhyan – Monk – ZBB LVN – brooks – Wyatt – Brinson – Sorrell Zaire – Coop Nixon – Cisse Williams – X Oladapo was the nickel. — Andy Herman (@AndyHermanNFL) August 10, 2026 On offense, the Packers continue to play around with their offensive line, as Jager Burton and Jacob Monk have been “starting” guards on the team (with Aaron Banks still sitting out team drills) since Zach Bako-Bewele returned to the lineup at right tackle. Previously, Anthony Belton was a pretty consistent starting right guard throughout the spring and summer. Instant win for Warren Brinson vs Jacob Monk pic.twitter.com/MT6MRaTGMM — Justis Mosqueda (@JuMosq) August 8, 2026 Head coach Matt LaFleur and general manager Brian Gutekunst have both praised the mentality that Monk brings to the interior line, even though Monk didn’t look great in Green Bay’s Family Night practice at Lambeau Field on Friday. At this point, though, it seems we’ve reached full-blown camp battle status for the right guard position. Keep an eye on it throughout the preseason, as that’s really the one spot open on the Packers’ depth chart on that side of the ball. Even Donovan Jennings is getting in the mix at the right guard spot. Belton also apparently had an elbow injury in practice today, as he visited a trainer and returned with a brace on his left arm. Miles Bokeem Melton. Might be the catch of camp. Line gave Love time and he fires up a deep 50/50. Melton skies and comes down with it. — weston hodkiewicz (@WesHod) August 10, 2026 Lloyd with the backward pass to Love, who throws a bomb to Melton for six. — Bill Huber (@BillHuberNFL) August 10, 2026 Yesterday, it was Bo Melton and Christian Watson starting on offense while Savion Williams had his best day of camp. Today, it was Williams and Isaiah Neyor as the team’s “starting” receivers while Melton made the two biggest plays during team periods. It’s nice that the backups are stepping up while Golden and Reed are rehabbing. Defense Kamal Hadden is back in team — weston hodkiewicz (@WesHod) August 10, 2026 Practice ends with Jaylin Simpson an INT off Drones on a goal line out. Likely pick six. — weston hodkiewicz (@WesHod) August 10, 2026 The cornerback competition for the final couple of spots on the team is starting to turn up, as Kamal Hadden returned to team drills for the first time this camp. Hadden played in 10 games last regular season and was actually poised to replace Valentine on non-obvious passing downs before an injury ended his 2025 campaign. Meanwhile, the player who has benefited the most from Hadden and Jackson being sidelined has been Jaylin Simpson, who was mostly a practice squadder for the 2025 Packers. He had been working with the second-team unit this camp and ended practice today with a 99-yard pick-six of fourth-string quarterback Kyron Drones. On the starting level, Keisean Nixon, Brandon Cisse and Benjamin St-Juste continue to split reps. Early on in camp, the Packers had a clear pecking order of Nixon, Valentine, Cisse and St-Juste, but it seems like they’re opening up reps with the first-team unit more as we progress closer to the preseason. For what it’s worth, Bullard’s replacement in the slot today was safety Kitan Oladapo, which was expected. Oladapo was the team’s third slot option in 2025 behind Bullard and Nate Hobbs, who was a cap casualty this offseason. Defensive lineman Javon Hargrave, who was recently activated off the PUP list, remains out of team drills at this point in time. The “starting” defensive line today (without Hargrave) was Devonte Wyatt (who also just recently returned to team drills), Karl Brooks and Warren Brinson. Special Teams LVN now on punt coverage unit today as well. That’s at least 3 special teams units for their top edge. — Andy Herman (@AndyHermanNFL) August 10, 2026 This is very niche, but one of the bigger questions the Packers have to answer this season is how they’re going to replace Lukas Van Ness on special teams (if at all) as he steps into a full-time starting role on defense. With the loss of safety Zayne Anderson in free agency, linebacker Nick Niemann has stepped up as the personal protector on the punt team. Generally, the “offensive line” of the punt team is made up of linebacker/edge rusher bodies, a role that Van Ness has played throughout the duration of his rookie contract. On Family Night, the Packers’ top punt team “offensive line” was made up of Barryn Sorrell, Arron Mosby, Isaiah McDuffie and Ty’Ron Hopper. Those players have all played those positions before, so that was sort of expected, but the big question is whether or not Mosby’s special teams ability warrants a spot on the 53-man roster when the season begins. As a vested veteran, Mosby’s entire 2026 season’s worth of game checks would become fully guaranteed if he’s on the roster in Week 1. If Mosby doesn’t make the team, it would make sense for Van Ness to be his replacement, as long as the Packers can stomach running both of their starting edge defenders 40 yards before starting defensive drives (until Parsons returns to the lineup). Green Bay’s other edge defenders, the only other backup options for the Mosby/Van Ness position — assuming that the team rosters only five off-ball linebackers, are likely to be Brenton Cox Jr., Dani Dennis-Sutton and Collin Oliver. We haven’t seen either Dennis-Sutton or Oliver play the “line” spot on punt team yet, and Cox has famously struggled on special teams during his time with the Packers.

title: Micah Parsons says his ‘most optimistic’ return target is Week 6 vs. Cowboys
summary: According to the NFL’s new rules around the Physically Unable to Perform list, players who start the regular season on that list will be eligible to return as early as their team’s fifth game of the season. For the Green Bay Packers, that takes on outsized importance — their week 5 contest is a massive […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - SEPTEMBER 28: Micah Parsons #1 of the Green Bay Packers looks on before kickoff against the Dallas Cowboys during an NFL football game at AT&T Field on September 28, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to the NFL’s new rules around the Physically Unable to Perform list, players who start the regular season on that list will be eligible to return as early as their team’s fifth game of the season. For the Green Bay Packers, that takes on outsized importance — their week 5 contest is a massive one with the Chicago Bears coming to Lambeau Field. That Packers-Bears game theoretically could have been a target for Micah Parsons to return from his torn ACL. However, recent comments from Parsons have heard him mention the following week’s game against the Dallas Cowboys as his primary target. On Monday at training camp, he made that more explicit, revealing to NFL Network reporters that the Week 6 contest against his old team is in fact his “most optimistic” return date. Interestingly, Parsons was not expected to make an appearance on the Inside Training Camp show, as reporter Stacey Dales noted that he “crashed our set .” That timeline may be a bit of a disappointment for Packers fans, given that Parsons returning against the Bears could have been a significant shot in the arm for the pass rush and team morale. Still, Parsons has work to do before he will be able to return to the field. Because his knee injury required a bit more work to repair than recent ACL tears to Tucker Kraft and Christian Watson — there was reportedly more meniscus damage than those players suffered — his recovery timeline may be a bit slower than theirs. Kraft, of course, is already back at practice and appears on track to return for week one. Last year, Watson returned to game action just shy of 10 months after his injury late in the 2024 season; a similar timeline would have Kraft ready for game action right about September 1st, and with the Packers playing their Week 1 game on September 13th, that looks well within reason for the star tight end. Perhaps that is why Parsons appears to be targeting Week 6 as the earliest possible return date for game action. His injury occurred last December 14th in Denver, and the date of the Cowboys game (October 18) comes just after that 10-month mark. Fortunately, early returns from training camp indicate that the Packers’ defensive front has been making plays without Parsons, and they will evidently need to do just that through at least the first five games of the regular season in 2026.

title: Green Bay Packers News: Savion Williams pounces on opportunities
summary: Sunday was a big day for a young wide receiver going into his second season in the NFL. The Green Bay Packers drafted Savion Williams in the third round of the 2025 NFL Draft, seeing plenty of untapped potential and athletic ability in the big wideout. However, his impact on offense was limited as a […]
full_text: Savion Williams #83 of the Green Bay Packers runs with the football during training camp at Ray Nitschke Field in Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin, on August 2, 2026. (Photo by Ross Harried/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Sunday was a big day for a young wide receiver going into his second season in the NFL. The Green Bay Packers drafted Savion Williams in the third round of the 2025 NFL Draft, seeing plenty of untapped potential and athletic ability in the big wideout. However, his impact on offense was limited as a rookie, as he was buried deep on the depth chart and had a long way to go to learn how to be an NFL receiver. The Packers’ practice on Sunday showed signs of how far he has come in recent months. Williams was responsible for multiple highlight-reel plays during Sunday’s closed practice, according to beat writers, as he took advantage of more reps with the starting offense. Unfortunately, those reps came as a result of knocks to two of the Packers’ top three wideouts, as Jayden Reed and Matthew Golden both sat out the practice session. Still, those injuries opened the door for Williams to make some plays, which he did. From a deep score on a go route to taking a slant to the house at the very end of practice, it was Williams’ time to shine. With the injured players likely to sit out longer this week, look for Williams to get a decent amount of run in the first half of Thursday’s preseason opener, and hopefully he can open some more eyes in game action against the Pittsburgh Steelers. 5 things learned at Packers training camp – Aug. 9 | Packers.com Chris Brooks and Javon Hargrave being back will help both sides of the football, but the bigger concerns surround the offense, with Jayden Reed, Matthew Golden, and Josh Whyle all sitting out on Sunday due to some injuries. Packers shake up O-line, cornerback depth charts as competition grows | Packers Wire Zach Bako-Bewele (we’re still getting used to the name) was finally back taking team reps for the first time in camp, but the line looked different with Jager Burton and Jacob Monk manning the guard spots. Meanwhile, Benjamin St-Juste got some reps with the top defensive unit while Keisean Nixon got dropped down to the twos. 2026 Green Bay Packers training camp: Latest intel, updates | ESPN Savion Williams stepped up with the team running a skeleton crew at wide receiver, hauling in a 60-yard bomb from Kyle McCord for a score.
