title: Groupthink: Texans Training Camp’s Most to Gain and Lose
summary: Houston has been at camp for over one week. Plenty has been learned about this offense and defense. New faces adorn the roster, battles have taken place, and stocks are beginning to rise and fall. It hasn’t been perfect, but this training camp and preseason represents an amazing opportunity for players to further their career. […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - NOVEMBER 09: Blake Fisher #57 of the Houston Texans looks on from the field during an NFL football game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at NRG Stadium on November 9, 2025 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Houston has been at camp for over one week. Plenty has been learned about this offense and defense. New faces adorn the roster, battles have taken place, and stocks are beginning to rise and fall. It hasn’t been perfect, but this training camp and preseason represents an amazing opportunity for players to further their career. Conversely. there’s plenty of chances for players to lose their roster spots. With that, I posed the following question to the writers. Training camp is upon us! Which player has the most to gain from a good training camp and which has the most to lose? L4Blitzer Most to gain: Every single LB in camp not named Azeez Al-Shaair or Henry To’oTo’o. Those two are your starters in a base 4-2-5. However, with EJ Speed and Jake Hansen out due to injury, all seven other LBs on the roster (Fisher, TakiTaki, Hill, Hummel, Mapu, Ossai, Woodaz) have a chance to lock down the LB3 spot, assuring themselves more playing time and perhaps, more money. Especially when the team needs to move to a base 4-3, that LB3 is going to be critical. Likely, said LB3 will need to play special teams, but then again, E.J. Speed logged over half of the special teams snaps. Overall, a huge chance for all seven of those LBs. Most to lose: Between Jake Andrews and Jarrett Patterson at the C/G spots. Both logged time on the O-line last season. However, Houston still went heavy (literally and figuratively) on the interior O-line in free agency and the draft. Both are in the last season of their respective contracts. If Houston decided to cut bait, neither would be huge cap or roster loss per se. Camp is likely going to be massive for both as far as their future with the Texans, if not in the NFL, is concerned. Neither locked down their spots at the end of last season, and are going to be in a dogfight for their spots this year. VBallRetired In terms of camp, I’m looking at Blake Fisher. I think he is one bad camp away from being cut and one good camp away from potentially being the swing tackle. Others players such as WR Xavier Hutchinson could be fighting for their job as well. The rest kind of sort their way out through the season but I’m looking at guys on the cusp. Fizzy Joe Out of the many players entering this training camp with a lot to gain (like L4Blitzer said, all of the backup LBs), I think TE Brevin Jordan can make a case for biggest upside. He hasn’t been in a real football game since September of 2024 after back-to-back season-ending injuries derailed his NFL career. Now, he’s fully recovered and motivated to keep his spot over rookie second-round pick Marlin Klein and/or veteran signing Foster Moreau. I think Jordan has a chance to explode onto the scene this training camp. My expectation going into last season with then-new offensive coordinator Nick Caley was that Brevin Jordan would be his X-factor tight end that could excel as both a blocker and receiver, not unlike Rams TEs Tyler Higbee or Colby Parkinson. Granted, Dalton Schultz was a far better run-blocker last year than I expected, but Jordan could have been the missing puzzle piece to that whole group last year. He has chance not only to become the #2 tight end this training camp, but I also think Jordan has a chance to push Schultz for playing time if he really gels with Caley’s offense. As for the player that has the most to lose, I have to agree with L4Blitzer that Jake Andrews and/or Jarrett Patterson are in trouble. And argument can be made for someone like S Jaylen Reed or WR Xavier Hutchinson because of the competition surrounding them, but I expect both of those players to at least be on the roster by the end of the preseason, whereas I cannot say the same for Patterson or Andrews. There are probably five or six interior linemen currently on this roster with a solid chance of starting or making the roster. Patterson nor Andrews can’t claim they’re better than any guard or center except Eli Cox. Evan Brown, Febechi Nwaiwu, and Keylan Rutledge all have reason to be chosen over the two former starting centers. If Andrews or Patterson can’t out duel one of the newbies this month, both could end up traded or cut. If I had to pick one that’s in the most danger, I’d pick Jarrett Patterson since he started fewer games last year than Andrews, who was, for better or worse, a rock at center in 2025. It would be heartbreaking to see Patterson go after he he was thrown into the fire his rookie season in 2023, but he might just be the worst center on the roster Kenneth L. Let me start off by ruling out any of the rookies as they have significant opportunity to gain and lose relative to other players on the roster. However, they have the luxury of a cheap, four-year salary on their side. Most to gain: I like the Brevin Jordan shout. It’s hard to disagree that a player who could go from fifth to second at his position, on a contract year, and off two injuries doesn’t have a lot to gain. However, I think Tank Dell for obvious reasons has the most to gain. Even if he starts the season on Injured Reserve, he has the opportunity to reintegrate himself back into this offense. His relationship with C.J. Stroud could propel him over the 709 yard mark from his rookie season. Another player with a lot on the line is nickel Alijah Huzzie. I am keenly aware of my over-infatuation with the second-year defensive back from UNC. I love his gritty play, but mainly shutter to think who takes over for Jalen Pitre in the slot if he is injured. From UDFA to key piece on the defense is plenty to earn to make this list. Last name I’ll throw out for gain is veteran Logan Hall. Nick Caserio loves to roll the dice on a traits-y, semi-underdeveloped veteran with flashes of performance. Hall could be the unlock for this defense that takes it to another level up front. Most to lose: veteran Tremon Smith must feel the walls closing in around him. From Jaylin Smith’s return and hype to undrafted rookie Collin Wright balling out at camp, his role on defense and specialization on special teams is dwindling. Smith makes more than twice as much as both Wright and Huzzie combined. I also believe WR Jaylin Noel has a lot to lose with this injury. Sure, he’s practicing again, but he was on the outs with the staff last year. There are seven WRs vying for six spots and Noel keeps giving them reasons to drop him on the depth chart. Noel should be fine for now, but he’s left the door open for Justin Watson, Tank Dell, Lewis Bond, and even Jared Wayne to steal not only his role but roster spot.

title: Value of things: Revisiting the C.J. Stroud question
summary: The C.J. Stroud question is actually three questions. We have hashed and rehashed this before, but important events that seem unrelated have converged to bring the question back to the forefront. The first is that preseason publications have begun to do their quarterback rankings. One in particular (PFF) had Davis Mills ranking higher than Stroud. […]
full_text: The C.J. Stroud question is actually three questions. We have hashed and rehashed this before, but important events that seem unrelated have converged to bring the question back to the forefront. The first is that preseason publications have begun to do their quarterback rankings. One in particular (PFF) had Davis Mills ranking higher than Stroud. That obviously raised some eyebrows. The second event was the contract extension for Henry To’o’to’o. Obviously, eight million dollars a year for a linebacker may not have much to do with a quarterback contract by itself, but when taken in concert with the Will Anderson extension, Danielle Hunter contract, Azeez Al-Shaair contract, Derek Stingley contract, and the looming contracts for Calen Bullock and Kamari Lassiter things start to come into focus more. Can the Texans outfit the best defense in football AND pay a quarterback top quarterback dollars? Moreover, does Stroud deserve the money? I try to approach things analytically as much as possible. So, I am doing this in a specific order. The first question is where do the various experts rank Stroud? We referenced PFF, but it is always better to get a cross-section of different experts and pundits to see if we can get a handle of where the consensus ranks him. The second question is do we agree with the consensus? Obviously, that is a yes or no answer, but all answers deserve qualification. The final question is whether we think he is the long-term quarterback of the future and what he needs to do to solidify that answer. Where does Stroud rank? Ranking ESPN 18+ NFL.com 24 Fox 22 Bleacher Report 20 PFF 31 I think we can all agree that PFF is an outlier and that was based purely on last season. I am sure if they did a multi-season analysis then the rankings would come out differently. I should note that ESPN.com only listed the top ten quarterbacks according to them, but listed seven different honorable mentions. Stroud came up in the category of others receiving votes, so he could be no better than 18th according to them. Statistically, what I would normally do is first look for outliers in the groupings. I obviously could include additional sources, but once we remove PFF from the group we get a pretty tight group of where people see Stroud. He ranks between 18th and 24th according to the four sources. Of course, the NFL.com one deserves some further explanation, but I imagine that most of these sources have some of the same biases built in. Do we trust the rankings? This is not s simple yes or no proposition. So, as much as it is a cop out, I will say they are both right and wrong. For instance, the NFL.com is more of a fantasy ranking. Fantasy rankings are based on expected production and not necessarily pure ability. The Texans will likely be more conservative this season as they hope to establish a running game and minimize negative plays. That distinction alone comes with a number of caveats that impact the third question in our piece. It looks like the overall consensus is that he fits in around 20th. I am sure all of them are at least partially basing that on the numbers they expect him to produce. Would Stroud produce better numbers on a different team and in a different system? That’s a fair question. I imagine he might go a little higher than 20th if teams were starting from scratch, but that is never the reality. So, I don’t think he is literally the 20th best quarterback in football when simply looking at skills and ability. However, that is what his production says at this point. So, as a statistician on the interwebs, I cannot ignore what has been done and what goes into those rankings. The decision to sign or not sign Stroud is the most consequential decision this organization will make. Of course, that spills us into the third question. What does this mean for Stroud’s future? My position on Stroud has always been nuanced and complicated, but it really has not fundamentally changed in the last year. He is a solid NFL quarterback. There is a grouping of guys that are consistent MVP threats every year. There is another tier of guys that are always very good. Then there is a third tier of guys that can put up numbers in the right circumstances, but probably cannot carry a team on their own to the championship. Stroud is in that third group. Make no mistake, they can win one. Sam Darnold is in that group. If you put a good enough team around them, they are capable of making enough plays to win enough games to get to the Super Bowl. Stroud is not Josh Allen, Patrick Mahomes, Lamar Jackson, or Matthew Stafford. He never will be those guys. He isn’t Joe Burrow, Dak Prescott, or Justin Herbert. He might be in that next group, but I have already listed seven quarterbacks that he isn’t. Is he better than Caleb Williams? Jordan Love? Jared Goff? Jalen Hurts? Drake Maye? Now all of the sudden we are pushing him into the teens. We get another group of guys that have sometimes been great and sometimes been meh. That group includes Trevor Lawrence, Baker Mayfield, Sam Darnold, and Brock Purdy. I haven’t even included the group of young quarterbacks that haven’t established themselves like Bo Nix, Jayden Daniels, Jaxson Dart, Tyler Shough, and Cam Ward. This also doesn’t include journeymen like Daniel Jones who have shown glimpses of good play in the past. I think everyone is starting to get the idea. The Seattle Seahawks showed you can win without one of those top ten guys. I would dare say that more championships have been won by players outside the top ten than we might believe. After all, Burrows, Stafford, Allen, and Jackson have combined for one title. If you are asking a quarterback to play conservatively, take care of the football, and give his team a chance to win with their defense, you don’t need to pay a guy 55 to 60 million dollars to do that. This is where the nuance comes in. Saying I don’t want to pay Stroud is not just a reflection on Stroud. It is a reflection of how DeMeco Ryans wants to win football games. If you are going to win with your defense then paying a quarterback 20-30 million affords you the ability to pay one or two additional defenders you can’t afford to pay if you are paying your quarterback 60 million. That means keeping Lassiter and Bullock. That means having the best secondary in football versus having a solid one and hoping you fill the holes in the draft. Saying I don’t want to pay Stroud is not me disliking Stroud. It is just an acknowledgment that he might not be the right fit for what Ryans wants to do.

full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, IN - JUNE 11: Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Alec Pierce (14) watches a drill during the Indianapolis Colts Minicamp on June 11, 2026 at the Indiana Farm Bureau Football Center in Indianapolis, IN. (Photo by Zach Bolinger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images According to The Athletic’s James Boyd, Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Alec Pierce had another PRP injection during late June in his rehabbing left ankle, which underwent minor cleanup surgery earlier this offseason: #Colts WR Alec Pierce received another PRP injection in his left ankle, a league source confirms to @TheAthleticNFL . Pierce underwent left ankle surgery in March. This is the second time he’s received a PRP injection this offseason. @AdamSchefter and @By_NathanBrown were on it. — James Boyd (@RomeovilleKid) August 11, 2026 The second PRP injection wasn’t publicly disclosed by the team. That being said, Boyd later noted that the second PRP injection wasn’t considered a setback by a team source. FOX59/CBS4’s Mike Chapell also confirmed that the second injection “wasn’t abnormal and helps healing.” However, there’s still no clear timetable for his return to the football field. For those not in the medical field, a PRP injection is a ‘platelet-rich plasma’ injection to help repair damaged tissues and ease joint pain as a form of medical treatment. The last public update we had received was from Pierce himself, when in early June, he indicated to the local media that there was a four-to-six month recovery timeline from his minor ankle surgery in late March. However, the hope was that he’d realistically return by late team training camp. For what it’s worth, ESPN NFL Insider Adam Schefter said on ‘The Pat McAfee Show’ on Monday that the Colts maintain that Pierce will be ready for the regular season opener. It’s of key concern for the Colts because not only did Pierce recently ink a once historic 4-year, $114 million contract (with $84 million guaranteed) , but given the trade of longtime veteran Michael Pittman Jr. to the Pittsburgh Steelers, and it’s an Indy wide receiver corps that looks a lot less formidable without him along the outside. There’s Josh Downs, who’s injured himself right now, manning the slot, and then his wide receiver teammates such as Ashton Dulin, Nick Westbrook-Ikhine, and rookie 7th round pick Deion Burks are the ‘next men up!’

Shane Steichen’s plan is for Riley Leonard and Anthony Richardson Sr. to split reps against New England, and the depth chart reflects that competition by listing both players as the No. 2 quarterback for now. That is probably the right way to frame the battle. Jones is the starter, while Leonard and Richardson are still fighting for the backup job. On offense, Alec Pierce is still listed as a starting receiver despite his ongoing ankle situation, alongside Josh Downs and Ashton Dulin. The offensive line has Bernhard Raimann at left tackle, Quenton Nelson at left guard, Tanor Bortolini at center, Matt Goncalves at right guard and Jalen Travis at right tackle. The right side is worth watching, with rookie Jalen Farmer listed behind Goncalves and Luke Tenuta behind Travis. Tyler Warren is listed as the top tight end, ahead of Mo Alie-Cox, Drew Ogletree and Will Mallory. At running back, Jonathan Taylor is unsurprisingly listed first, with DJ Giddens ahead of Seth McGowan for the backup job. That is one of the more interesting camp battles because the Colts have talked about wanting to manage Taylor’s workload, and whoever wins the No. 2 role could have a real weekly job. Giddens getting the first nod makes sense based on experience and draft slot, but McGowan has generated enough camp buzz that this one should not be treated as settled yet. Defensively, CJ Allen is listed as the starting middle linebacker, which is notable even on an unofficial depth chart, although he is currently injured and I doubt will play. Akeem Davis-Gaither is listed at weakside linebacker, while the defensive line features Arden Key, DeForest Buckner, Grover Stewart and Laiatu Latu as the listed starters. In the secondary, Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward are the outside corners, Camryn Bynum and AJ Haulcy are the starting safeties, and Justin Walley is listed as the nickel. Special teams also has one unresolved battle, with Blake Grupe and Spencer Shrader listed as co-starters at kicker. Anthony Gould is listed as both the top kick returner and punt returner, which gives him a clear early path to roster value even if his offensive role remains uncertain. The depth chart should not be treated as final, especially before the first preseason game and Tuesday’s joint practice with the Patriots. Still, it confirms the main early storylines: Leonard vs. Richardson for QB2, Giddens vs. McGowan behind Taylor, the kicker battle, Allen’s early defensive role, and how the Colts are lining up a new-look secondary. For an unofficial August depth chart, that is enough to make it worth paying attention to.

title: What’s going on with Alec Pierce?
summary: The Colts are now at the point where Alec Pierce’s ankle situation deserves more than the usual “he’s doing a great job in rehab” answer. Pierce had ankle surgery in March after playing through the injury last season, and the expectation from the organization was that he would return at some point during training camp. […]
full_text: The Colts are now at the point where Alec Pierce’s ankle situation deserves more than the usual “he’s doing a great job in rehab” answer. Pierce had ankle surgery in March after playing through the injury last season, and the expectation from the organization was that he would return at some point during training camp. Chris Ballard said earlier in the offseason that Pierce was on roughly a three-month recovery timeline, which put him on track to return around camp, while Shane Steichen later said the team expected him back “at some point in training camp.” That timeline has now become much less clear. Pierce opened camp on the active/PUP list, which by itself was not a massive concern because players can be activated at any point. The issue is what has happened since. Ballard reportedly said Pierce was “a week or two away” from returning near the start of camp, yet Steichen was asked this week whether there was a timetable and answered, “No, not right now.” He added that Pierce’s rehab is going well and that he is doing a “hell of a job,” which sounds nice but does not actually say much. Nobody needs the Colts to hand out every medical detail, and nobody is asking them to rush Pierce back before he is ready. The problem is that this organization has lost the benefit of the doubt when injury updates start getting vague. Andrew Luck is the obvious example, but Shaq Leonard is the cleaner recent one. His back issue was talked about with optimism, then came the PUP list, the unclear timetable, the brief return, another procedure and eventually a lost season. That does not mean Pierce’s ankle is headed anywhere close to that territory, but it explains why Colts fans do not hear “he’s doing a great job in rehab” and automatically relax. When Ballard says Pierce is close and Steichen says shortly after that there is no timetable, people are going to wonder what is actually going on. That does not mean Pierce is definitely in danger of missing Week 1. It also does not mean the team is hiding some catastrophic setback. However, the whole point is that the Colts have not given anyone enough clarity to feel confident either way. Pierce had surgery in March, the original messaging pointed toward a return during training camp, he opened camp on PUP, Ballard recently made it sound like he was getting close, and now Steichen is back to saying there is no timetable. That sequence is not reassuring! Maybe he returns next week and this all disappears, but until he is actually back on the field, the concern is completely reasonable. With Michael Pittman Jr. gone, he is one of the key pieces in the passing game, and his vertical ability changes how defenses have to play Indianapolis. Daniel Jones is trying to rebuild timing in this offense, Josh Downs is taking on a bigger role, and Tyler Warren is entering his second season as a major weapon, so losing practice reps with Pierce is not nothing. The Colts need their passing game to be sharper this year, and that becomes harder when one of their main receivers is still rehabbing with no clear return date. It is exhausting dealing with an organization that treats clarity like it is too much to ask.

title: Chiefs training camp notebook Day 11: Eric Bieniemy makes presence heard in return
summary: The main headline from the 11th practice of the Kansas City Chiefs’ training camp on Monday was the return of offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy. Head coach Andy Reid spoke to local media after practice and officially welcomed him back. He was ready to go from the jump on Monday morning, yelling orders of attention to […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - JUNE 09: Eric Bieniemy, offensive coordinator of the Kansas City Chiefs, reacts during mandatory minicamp at The University of Kansas Hospital Arrowhead Training Complex on June 09, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Aaron M. Sprecher/Getty Images) | Getty Images The main headline from the 11th practice of the Kansas City Chiefs ’ training camp on Monday was the return of offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy. Head coach Andy Reid spoke to local media after practice and officially welcomed him back. He was ready to go from the jump on Monday morning, yelling orders of attention to detail before the first-team offense even took its first snap together on air. “Get the [expletive] out of the huddle,” Bieniemy barked loudly enough to be heard from the bleachers on the far field. Later in a nine-on-seven run period, Bieniemy alerted his unit to its body language a few plays in. “Hands off your [expletive] hips!” Before the first-team offense lined up against the starting defense for a red-zone period, Bieniemy had a simple instruction for the group. “Every [expletive] play!” Throughout the day, the word “finish” was yelled loudly and aggressively as ball carriers worked through the whistle. If you attended camp without seeing the notification that Bieniemy was back with the team, you certainly heard of his return by the end of the day. K9 vs. Bolton in pass pro. EB coaching up the lead back afterwards pic.twitter.com/oQ78LhyWRp — Ron Kopp Jr (@RonOnChiefs) August 10, 2026 His return was also seen during a pass-protection drill. He was hands-on with the running backs, coaching up Kenneth Walker and Brashard Smith with intensity after each player finished with reps. During this one-on-one period, undrafted rookie running back Jaydn Ott whiffed against undrafted rookie linebacker Wesley Bissainthe. Bieniemy loudly critiqued the rep before making the two do it again. “Having a guy like that come back on the field, a competitor, it brings the best out of us also on defense,” Chiefs linebacker Nick Bolton told reporters after practice on Monday. “If we win a rep, he doesn’t really care about winning a rep, a ‘do it again’ type of deal. Great to have him back in the building.” Bieniemy has been away from Kansas City since the 2022 season, meaning there are plenty of starters on offense who are unfamiliar with Bieniemy in-season. Left guard Kingsley Suamataia is one of them. He was asked about his experience so far with his new offensive coordinator. “Coach EB, he’s crazy,” Suamataia said with wide eyes before cracking a smile. “He’s a great guy, very vocal,” Suamataia continued. “He pushes us to our limits every day so we can be the best offense out there.” “To be able to have his voice, his coaching points, and his energy, it’s infectious,” Second-year tight end Jake Briningstool said at the podium on Monday. “It’s great to have him back out here.” Other notes from practice State of the receivers While wide receiver Xavier Worthy walked down the hill in pads on Monday, he did not participate in team periods for the most part. The starting three receivers for the offense were Rashee Rice, Tyquan Thornton and Jalen Royals. Royals, the second-year wideout from Utah State, has had an up-and-down camp. He flashed with the starting offense on Saturday, but was quieter on Monday; Andy Reid was asked about Royals’ camp so far at the podium. “He’s getting better every day, faster every day,” Reid shared. “Had some nice catches today. Just have to keep going, you have to stack the days; it’s not what you did today, you have to do well tomorrow, so you can’t drop back off. That’s the challenge.” Rookie wide receiver Cyrus Allen was back in the mix with the starting offense in team periods, scoring a touchdown in a seven-on-seven red zone period that showed chemistry with quarterback Patrick Mahomes in the scramble drill, even if the extended play may have been a sack in live action. Mahomes to Tyquan strikes again pic.twitter.com/mDO8Tvdq4j — Ron Kopp Jr (@RonOnChiefs) August 10, 2026 However, it was Tyquan Thornton who had the biggest day of all the team’s receivers on Monday. Mahomes made two beautiful passes to Thornton streaking downfield in seven-on-seven periods, both finishing as deep touchdowns. Tight end rotation Reid was asked about the tight ends after practice, a group that may have one of the biggest battles for positioning in the preseason. Behind star tight end Travis Kelce, incumbents Noah Gray and Jared Wiley are jockeying for snaps. “You’re seeing the challenge between the two of them. They’re competing as that whole group is,” Reid told reporters. Reid also pointed to reserve tight ends Tre Watson and Jake Briningstool when talking about competition in the tight end room. “Tre’s right in the mix there too; it’s a good group of young guys. Big, strong guys. Briningstool’s whole thing was if he could stay on the field, and he has been doing that.” The head coach also noted that Kelce, in his 14th camp, isn’t making it easy on the coaches to get a look at his backups. “You gotta pull Travis off the field,” Reid said with a smile. “If he hears the next play and it’s one he kind of likes, you have to fight him to get him off. I love that part of him.” And it’s great for the young guys; that’s the best part,“ Reid elaborated. ”He shares that energy with them; he’s not afraid to get on guys and challenge them, then he walks his part of it.” Kahlil Benson at right guard again With starting right guard Trey Smith still recovering from a hip injury, rookie Kahlil Benson manned the right guard position for the third consecutive day alongside veteran right tackle Jaylon Moore. Reid commented on the look at Benson inside after he spent the first week of camp at right tackle. “I think it’s good for him to have some flexibility in there to do both,” Reid said. “We worked him a little bit in there in OTAs, we liked what we saw, so this gives him real competition in there now where Spags is throwing a lot of different things at you; you have to be able to adjust. It’ll do nothing but help him,“ Reid emphasized. ”Even at the tackle spot, it will help him once he jumps back there.”

title: Andy Reid talks injuries, Bieniemy’s return after Monday’s Chiefs practice
summary: After a day of rest for the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday, the full team was back on the fields at Missouri Western State in St. Joe for the 11th practice of this year’s training camp. It was another mild day compared to the typical August mornings in Missouri. Head coach Andy Reid stepped up […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - JUNE 09: Andy Reid (right) talks with Eric Bieniemy of the Kansas City Chiefs during mandatory minicamp at The University of Kansas Hospital Arrowhead Training Complex on June 09, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Aaron M. Sprecher/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a day of rest for the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday, the full team was back on the fields at Missouri Western State in St. Joe for the 11th practice of this year’s training camp. It was another mild day compared to the typical August mornings in Missouri. Head coach Andy Reid stepped up to the podium to recap the day before going over important updates pertaining to the Chiefs. “A lot of red-zone work today, short field,” Reid shared. “Things are a little faster in that area, and I thought the guys competed against each other… we worked a lot of third downs in the red zone, which will help us down the road, too.” Injury report Right guard Trey Smith The starting offensive lineman missed his third consecutive practice due to a hip injury that caused him to see a specialist. He could be seen off to the side on Monday. “Trey didn’t practice, but improving,” Reid said. When asked if it was a short-term injury for Smith, Reid put it bluntly to an old friend of the site and Kansas City Star beat writer Pete Sweeney. “Yes,” Reid quickly said. Others who didn’t practice Cornerback L’Jarius Sneed (Knee) Linebacker Drue Tranquill (Back spasm) “They’re all improving as we go,” Reid said of the players unable to participate in Monday’s practice. Returning to the field on Monday in a limited fashion Linebacker Jeffrey Bassa (Groin) Defensive end Ashton Gillotte (Hamstring) Wide receiver Xavier Worthy (Shoulder) Increased participation in practice on Monday Wide receiver Cyrus Allen (Shin bruise) Wide receiver Rashee Rice (Knee) Cornerback Mansoor Delane (Shoulder) “Cyrus got some good work in today,” Reid said. “Bassa is back out there and did good. Delane did up through seven-on-seven, did a nice job with that with the pads on. Rice did most of the practice.” The return of Eric Bieniemy To the surprise of media and fans, Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy walked down the hill on Monday morning to attend his first full-team practice of camp since leaving to care for his wife, Mia, after she was hospitalized due to a gunshot wound. Reid said it was good to have his long-time assistant coach back on the field, for many different reasons. “He’s back in the fold, and I don’t think he missed a step,” Reid said. “He was out there getting after it, and that’s a positive for the offensive side.” “I talked to him several times a day, so I knew he was coming back if everything worked out the way it had been,” Reid revealed. “The primary thing is that Mia’s stable and in good hands; she’s doing well, so that was the primary thing,” Reid emphasized. “That’s where we stand with it.” Some EB greetings for the TL pic.twitter.com/9yIUiEaomn — Ron Kopp Jr (@RonOnChiefs) August 10, 2026 Early and often during Monday’s practice, Bieniemy could be heard barking at his unit and doing it with expletives. As Reid said, he didn’t miss a step, and that instantly raised the intensity level of practice, anecdotally. “It was great back to have him back out there, everybody was glad to see him,” Reid reiterated. “I think once you start going, then you’re going; it’s a little bit like a game. Once you’re in the game, you’re in the game. He always brings great energy.” The Chiefs, and Bieniemy, will be back at it on Tuesday morning at 9:15 a.m.

The first-round DT could be massive for K.C.’s defense. Undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson seems poised to swipe the starting right tackle job. This feels like it warrants more attention. Five Observations from Saturday’s Practice | Chiefs Training Camp 8/8 | The Mothership 3. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes made a handful of classic throws. Mahomes showed off a handful of the off-balance throws for which he’s synonymous on Saturday, firing a pair of near identical passes across his body while on the run to a receiver in the middle of the field. Mahomes found Andrew Armstrong on the first instance, followed by a throw to Nikko Remigio a little bit later. The three-time Super Bowl MVP, who has participated in every 11-on-11 segment of training camp so far, spoke following practice about his progress as he continues to work his way back from last season’s knee injury. Three Chiefs Players With the Most to Lose in Preseason Opener vs Rams | Sports Illustrated 3. Garrett Nussmeier Now that he has an extended opportunity, Nussmeier’s performance could have massive implications for his chances of securing the QB3 job. It will be his first real opportunity to play with the rest of the squad, and it’s possible that he receives snaps with some of the first-team starters as well. While it’s highly unlikely that Chris Oladokun jumps him up the depth chart, K.C. is in a tricky situation with Nussmeier. If he plays poorly in the preseason, the Chiefs could decide to run with two quarterbacks on the active 53-man roster to open the campaign and leave Oladokun on the practice squad. Nussmeier cannot simply be placed on the practice squad like Oladokun as a drafted rookie, as he would first have to clear the NFL waiver wire. Patrick Mahomes supports hometown schools with T-Mobile | Chiefs Wire Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes returns for his second season alongside Rob Gronkowski to inspire fans and rally communities throughout T-Mobile’s Friday Night 5G Lights competition. Mahomes and Gronkowski are joined by standout college athletes Dante Moore, Ashlea Klam, CJ Carr, Rocco Becht and Kewan Lacy, representing divisions across the country and encouraging fans to support their hometown schools in the race for game-changing prizes. Chiefs Predicted to Part Ways With Fan-Favorite WR After Offseason Return | Heavy Sports “With the uncertainty at the top of the depth chart, it seems like the team needs to keep more than five receivers. There’s more to find out about Royals and Armstrong, but that’s more than can be said about Remigio. He has maximized his role in Kansas City, and the return job should be handed off to Brashard Smith. Allen has lined up and caught punts and kicks as well.” Remigio was an exclusive-rights free agent this winter, returning to the team with a new contract extension on the day the free agent market officially opened in March. Remigio made a strong impression in training camp in 2024, averaging 33.25 yards on kick returns and 21.0 yards on punts, though the numbers leveled off during the regular season. Around the NFL Commanders moving Brandon Coleman back to LT after Laremy Tunsil injury | The Athletic Only 72 hours after celebrating the signing of veteran receiver Stefon Diggs, the Washington Commanders lost five-time Pro Bowl left tackle Laremy Tunsil to a torn triceps, an injury that will keep him out for a good portion of the season, if not its entirety. Replacing a player of that caliber is a tall task, especially this late in the offseason. Washington may add to its offensive line — for depth, if not more — but for now, the plan is to turn to Brandon Coleman at left tackle, according to a team source who spoke on condition of anonymity because they are not authorized to speak publicly on the matter. Teddy Bridgewater leaves Lions to retire again, coach says | ESPN Head coach Dan Campbell said he believes that this retirement could stick for Bridgewater, who had previously retired after the 2023 season only to return to the Lions the next season. “I think he can only truly answer that, but I feel like this is where it’s at for sure right now. This is where it needs to be and where he felt,” Campbell said. “And his biggest worry was letting us down. That’s the type of guy he is, and he’s not. “That’s as far as it can get. He meant a lot.” Safety Plan: Defensive Back Brandon Jones fills in as Broncos kicker, makes three field goals in scrimmage | NFL.com Jones did not kick in high school or college. “I just have some history in playing soccer,” he said. “I don’t know how I even got to kick. Me and I guess, I can’t remember… I think I just was joking with ‘Riz’ like, ‘Yo, I can kick if you ever need an emergency-kicker-type of situation.’ Then he called my bluff and put me to the test one day, I think it was some time last year. I made an extra point. Apparently, there are a lot of guys on the team that can also kick, but I guess I just got the opportunity today. [I] went three-for-four, so not too bad.” In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Chiefs training camp: 5 observations from the second week of practices 3. R Mason Thomas should see more snaps as time goes on With second-year defensive end Ashton Gillotte missing nearly all of the second week of camp with an injury, the primary workload for the first team went to Felix Anudike-Uzomah, while rookie R Mason Thomas mostly took snaps with the second team and a few rotational situations with the first team. The team appears to be willing to give Anudike-Uzomah every chance to earn playing time after struggling through the first three seasons of his career, but on Friday during the two-minute drill, it was Thomas who walked on to the field when the first-team defense took on the starting offense. The two-minute drill can be where games are won and lost, and the team did not hide the fact that the rookie is already one of the defense’s best pass-rush options. title: The key to the Chargers making a deep playoff run
summary: The Los Angeles Chargers have made the playoffs in each of the last two seasons, but they found themselves losing in the first round in consecutive years to the Houston Texans and New England Patriots. The Chargers are hoping for different fortunes in the 2026 season, but it will likely come down to the health […]
full_text: ORLANDO, FLORIDA - FEBRUARY 02: Rashawn Slater #70 of the Los Angeles Chargers and AFC looks on prior to the 2025 NFL Pro Bowl Games at Camping World Stadium on February 02, 2025 in Orlando, Florida. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Chargers have made the playoffs in each of the last two seasons, but they found themselves losing in the first round in consecutive years to the Houston Texans and New England Patriots. The Chargers are hoping for different fortunes in the 2026 season, but it will likely come down to the health of their offensive line, which struggled last season. “Los Angeles’ offensive line should be a strength of the team in 2026 after disaster struck last season. Left tackle Rashawn Slater suffered a season-ending patellar tendon tear in August, while right tackle Joe Alt played just six games before requiring season-ending ankle surgery,” NFL.com contributor Bobby Kownack wrote. “Herbert took a career-high 54 sacks behind a patchwork offensive line, leading the league with 268 pressures taken and a 43.3 pressure rate. Slater and Alt are back, but they’ll also be joined on the line by free-agent signings Tyler Biadasz and Cole Strange, as well as second-round rookie Jake Slaughter. Assuming the group stays healthy, Herbert should be well protected. First, though, the Bolts blockers have to jell together as a unit in August.” The Chargers are healthy in that area for the most part, which is all they can ask for at this point in the year. Slater did leave practice last week with a brief injury, but he was able to get some work in later in the day. The team wants to be extremely careful with him coming back from such a major injury, especially considering he signed a $114 million contract last offseason. If the Chargers proceed with caution, they have a better chance of having Slater healthy for the long haul, which is what’s going to be needed in order for the Chargers to truly take that next step forward. BFTB community, how do you feel about the offensive line going into the season? How concerned are you if the offensive line struggles with injuries like they did last year? Let us know in the comment section below.

title: George Kittle on track to play against Rams in Week 1
summary: There is a “high level of confidence” that the San Francisco 49ers will have George Kittle available when they play the L.A. Rams in Week 1, according to CBS Sports reporter Matt Zenitz. But will the 49ers have anyone else? Kittle tore his Achilles in a playoff loss to the Seattle Seahawks in January, indicating […]
full_text: Oct 30, 2022; Inglewood, California, USA; San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle (85) reacts against the Los Angeles Rams during the second half at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-USA TODAY Sports There is a “high level of confidence” that the San Francisco 49ers will have George Kittle available when they play the L.A. Rams in Week 1, according to CBS Sports reporter Matt Zenitz. But will the 49ers have anyone else? Kittle tore his Achilles in a playoff loss to the Seattle Seahawks in January, indicating a remarkable turnaround if he is able to suit up nine months later for a game. However, the 49ers have a growing list of injury concerns , including placing receiver Ricky Pearsall on season-ending injured reserve, and starters such as Christian McCaffrey, Mike Evans, Christian Kirk, Nick Bosa, Kyle Jusczcyk, Malik Mustapha, and Mykel Williams missing time in training camp. #49ers star tight end George Kittle continues to make terrific progress working back from the torn Achilles he suffered in January and there’s a high level of confidence at this point that he’ll end up being able to play Week 1 vs. the #Rams , sources tell @CBSSports pic.twitter.com/UK7cBEzs24 — Matt Zenitz (@mzenitz) August 10, 2026 Williams is on PUP while recovering from a torn ACL, and running back Isaac Guerendo is also on PUP, as is Kittle. The running back position exemplifies injury concerns related to San Francisco’s depth, as not only is McCaffrey banged up, so is backup Jordan James, and so is rookie third-round pick Kaelon Black, and so is Guerendo. Without those four, the Niners are down to Patrick Taylor, Sincere McCormick, and Khalil Herbert. 49ers worked out 2 vet RBs, hosted another… Zamir White Nyheim Miller Blake Watson (visit) SF likely to sign one of them ahead of Tuesday's joint practice with Tennessee. Numbers will be needed for that and Thursday's game. Worth noting Miller has punt returner experience — David Lombardi (@LombardiHimself) August 10, 2026 The 49ers also added receiver depth by signing Deebo Samuel, as backup Jacob Cowing is also missing time in training camp, in addition to Evans and Pearsall. Black isn’t the only third-round rookie out, as defensive end Romello Height is also injured. The San Francisco 49ers had as many as 27 injured players as of Monday . When the Rams face the 49ers in Melbourne in one month, San Francisco is likely to get most of the players back. Some key players have avoided the injury bug so far, including Brock Purdy, Fred Warner, Trent Williams, and Alfred Collins. Bosa, McCaffrey, and Evans could all turn out “fine” by September, although it’s not a guarantee. Nick Bosa not seen at 49ers practice for almost a week feels like a problem — Gregg Rosenthal (@greggrosenthal) August 11, 2026 The Rams can’t expect the Niners to just be injured when they face off in Australia. L.A. has to prepare as if this is the full-time 49ers, which could include George Kittle. However, as things stand it’s not clear how many 49ers can actually make that trip.

title: Winners & Losers: Who stood out in Rams training camp?
summary: Los Angeles Rams training camp at Loyola Marymount University came to a close on Friday. The team now returns to their practice facilities at Woodland Hills. A change of scene could bring the addition of Aaron Donald, who is expected to make an announcement in the coming weeks whether he will return to football. The […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 23: Cornerback Cam Lampkin #33 of the Los Angeles Rams celebrates after a play during the fourth quarter of an NFL Preseason 2025 game against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on August 23, 2025 in Cleveland, Ohio. The Browns defeated the Rams 19-17. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Los Angeles Rams training camp at Loyola Marymount University came to a close on Friday. The team now returns to their practice facilities at Woodland Hills. A change of scene could bring the addition of Aaron Donald, who is expected to make an announcement in the coming weeks whether he will return to football. The Dallas Cowboys are also set to face LA in a joint practice session on Tuesday. But before we turn our attention to the preseason, which players showed out at Loyola Marymount? Roster battles are won or lost in camp. Let’s check in on those with rising and falling stocks. Winners Receiver & corner battles Nothing steals the show quite like two strengths going head-to-head. Puka Nacua and Davante Adams battled every day against Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson. They each had their own victories on certain days, but the Rams won from the competitive bar being raised. Nacua and Adams seem to be picking up where they left off in 2025. A clean bill of health is of the upmost importance for each. McDuffie and Watson seem as advertised. There are no signs of buyer’s remorse for the Rams so far. This is the TD pass from Matthew Stafford to Davante Adams I was referring to earlier. Hard for any CB/DB to beat that ball placement by Stafford and the late hands by Adams pic.twitter.com/FOyc3umDzz — Stu Jackson (@StuJRams) August 3, 2026 Blake Corum, RB Is it a stretch to think that Corum can overtake Kyren Williams as the primary running back this season? Corum appears slimmed down and was already the more explosive player a year ago. This could realistically be Williams’ last season in Los Angeles . It may not happen as early as Week 1, but Corum seems on the path to earning LA’s RB#1 job in 2026 and beyond. Cam Lampkin & Emmanuel Forbes, CB While McDuffie and Watson were the shiny new additions that were met with more anticipation, Cam Lampkin and Emmanuel Forbes both consistently drew praise across camp practices. Fans may see Forbes more often than they expect depending on how much McDuffie plays in the slot. The Rams plan to deploy McDuffie in a variety of ways, and someone must play outside if McDuffie aligns elsewhere. It’s an encouraging sign for LA that Forbes has performed well when given the opportunity. For that same reason, the Rams need as many outside corners as possible. They are short on numbers. Lampkin is an outside corner, and he entered camp with an advantage over the likes of Josh Wallace and others because of positional value. Lampkin has been a ballhawk. He’s someone to watch in the preseason. Cam Lampkin has had a solid camp. pic.twitter.com/jsRCgZNKqd — Allen Sales (@AllenSales) August 7, 2026 Terrance Ferguson, TE Ferguson reportedly knows all receiving positions within the offense and is aligning all over the field . The Rams would like to utilize his run after the catch ability more often—something he consistently flashed at Oregon. It’s not exactly bold to predict a breakout campaign for last year’s top draft pick; however, things seem to be trending in the right direction for Ferguson. Max Klare has recently received first-string snaps as well. Could 2026 be the year of the tight ends? Losers Kyren Williams, RB Deploying Williams as the primary punt returner at the minimum is peculiar. Perhaps the Rams are simply biding time until cutdown day when they acquire an alternative. Still, with Corum’s emergence and Williams’ strange usage, it only seems like the veteran is trending downwards with the team. LA has several key players that need re-signed in the next year or two. There may not be enough salary cap space to keep around an expensive running back. Enjoy him in Los Angeles while you can. Xavier Smith, WR How bad is Xavier Smith as a punt returner for the team to hand the reins to Williams? It would be increasingly difficult for Smith to stick on the roster if he loses his value as a special teams player. He also hasn’t had many breakout moments in camp as a receiver. Smith may never live down his muffed punt in last year’s NFC Championship game. Stetson Bennett, QB It may seem odd that Bennett is included on the “losers” list. He’s drawn praise in camp for his performance so far, although in recent days he’s seemed to have taken a step back and saw an uptick in turnovers. It’s telling that Sean McVay said Ty Simpson would play in the preseason but is still mulling the idea of whether Bennett will join him. That tells me the backup quarterback spot is not yet won. And if the quarterback competition is even remotely close, Simpson will have the upper hand in terms of sticking on the roster. Bennett had to win in convincing fashion. I’m not sure he did. Pick 6 here by Sean Dolac. pic.twitter.com/LtzvpAEu4j — Allen Sales (@AllenSales) August 7, 2026 Jarquez Hunter, RB Jarquez Hunter needed to stand out in training camp in order to find a role in 2026 . It’s been quiet on that front so far, which aligns with his first year in the NFL. But training camp can be a tough environment for running backs. Hunter is battling with Ronnie Rivers for what is likely the third and final spot on the roster at the position. Their real battle does not begin until the preseason. Both should be expected to see significant work and make their case. It hasn’t been ideal for Hunter so far. There is still time to salvage his second season.
author: JB Scott

title: The Rams must be careful with big contracts next year
summary: Teams with top-heavy payrolls, which could be any team with 50-percent of their cap space allocated to 12 or fewer players, tend to disappoint their fans come playoff time and the L.A. Rams could be headed in that direction. With 29 pending free agents heading into next year, the Rams need to avoid spending too […]
full_text: HOLLYWOOD, FL - MARCH 18: Stacks of money are seen in what is being called a first-of-its-kind exhibit of five million dollars in cash at the Seminole Hard Rock Hotel & Casino on March 18, 2009 in Hollywood, Florida. The display consists of $100 bills encased in a 1,300-pound, custom-made $90,000 bullet-resistant Lexan showcase. (Photo by Joe Raedle/Getty Images) | Getty Images Teams with top-heavy payrolls, which could be any team with 50-percent of their cap space allocated to 12 or fewer players, tend to disappoint their fans come playoff time and the L.A. Rams could be headed in that direction. With 29 pending free agents heading into next year, the Rams need to avoid spending too much of their budget on too few players, setting themselves up for failure in 2027 and beyond due to injury or a lack of funds for their supporting cast. The Rams will be paying the price next year. The only question will be: who do they keep? The Methodology I put together a list of 12 teams, six each from the NFC and AFC, to get a mix of teams that, in my opinion, performed well and those that disappointed last season to see if there was any correlation between spending too heavily on a small number of players and the teams’ overall performance. It would appear that teams that spent upwards of 50% of their budget on 12 or fewer players were susceptible to severe consequences from injury to any of those players (for example, Cincinnati) and also lacked the necessary funds to build a strong foundation throughout the team. The Dallas Cowboys lacked the funds to field a decent defense for this very reason. Not surprisingly, the top four teams in terms of managing their budgets—Patriots, Broncos, Seahawks, Eagles—had the best records last year. By spending less at the top, teams can build a superior supporting cast. The Seahawks, for example, had 25 players inside the top 50-percent of their 2025 cap and were widely regarded as one of the most balanced teams in the league. The Rams 2025 Cap Please understand I am far from a ‘cap specialist’. For simplicity, the list is made up of the cap hits listed by Spotrac and I listed each team from top to bottom and added the percentages until it was approximately 50%. Here’s how the 2025 L.A. Rams allocated their top 50-percent of the budget: Notice how a player like TuTu Atwell takes up 3.6-percent, just ahead of players like Tyler Higbee and Darious Williams. Think of how much better L.A.’s cap could be without so much cap tied up in players who contribute little-to-nothing for the team. Often, the worst spending is on players who get injured, especially when they take up 3 percent of the cap or more. Look at the Cincinnati Bengals, for example: Of the 6 players who made up the top 50%, a significant amount of time was spent on the IR. Joe Burrow and Trey Hendrickson spent 18 games on the IR between them, meaning 13% of the cap was unavailable. The breakdown How many top players eat up 50 percent of each team’s salary cap? Here are the six teams in each conference that I mentioned earlier and how many players fit inside their top 50 percent of the cap, as well as the effects of players who ended up on IR: 2025 NFC: Seattle, 25 players with minimal IR hit Philadelphia, 15 players minimal IR hit Dallas, 12 players, minimal IR hit Detroit, 10 players, minimal IR hit * Los Angeles Rams, 9 players, large hit on IR Chicago, 9 players, minimal IR hit * Detroit had 15 players on IR, representing a large hit 2025 AFC: New England, 15 players, 4% on IR (14 players) Denver, 13 players, medium hit on IR Buffalo, 11 players, large hit on IR Baltimore, 8 players, large hit on IR Kansas City, 8 players, large hit on IR Cincinnati, 6 players, huge hit on IR The teams with the fewest players comprising 50% of the cap, like the Bengals, Chiefs, and Ravens for instance, Cincinnati, were disappointments. Cincinnati rolled the dice with only six players taking up 50% of their cap space and the season was a disaster, ending 6-11. The Chiefs also finished 6-11. The Lions and Patriots had a significant amount of their payroll end up on the IR, which really hurt their supporting casts, but these were players outside of those making up 50 percent of their teams’ cap space. Detroit fell short of expectations and missed the playoffs with a 9-8 record, whereas New England overcame their faults and reached the Super Bowl, thanks in large part to Drake Maye’s relatively cheap rookie salary. Already the Lions are suffering the injury bug in camp as they could lose center Cade Mays, a $25 million signing in the offseason, for over two months. #Lions center Cade Mays fractured a small bone in his wrist, an injury that will keep him out roughly 8-10 weeks, source said. Coach Dan Campbell called the injury “significant.” But Mays should be back by midseason, at least. pic.twitter.com/BGhztyidRw — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) August 10, 2026 Injuries happen in the NFL, it’s unavoidable. But can the Rams avoid tying too much of their cap in too few players and then getting hammered by the injury bug like they were in 2022? The Rams cap situation With only nine players’ salaries accounting for 50-percent of the cap, the Rams were able to buck the trend and perform at a high level in 2025 thanks to some really talented players still on rookie contracts. That window closes at the end of the 2026 season. The Rams have an incredible 29 players eligible for free agency in 2027 . Looking over the group, I count at least 20 that had snaps last year, and a significant number of major contributors. Here are seven who will be looking for large salary increases, along with their current salary and Spotrac estimates for their market value: Puka Nacua, increase $5.8m to $50 million Kevin Dotson, $17.4m to $19.5m Steve Avila, $4.6m to $13.6m Byron Young, $6m to $30m Kobie Turner, $4.1m to $32.5m Warren McClendon, $1.2m to $19m (My estimate) Omar Speights, $1m to $4m (My estimate) These are only seven of the 29, and I intentionally left Davante Adams off the list because his contract, if he even comes back, should not be as expensive as it was to originally sign him in 2025. The 2027 salary cap should be in the $325 million range, according to Spotrac, an increase of $24 million, but several players are getting increases in their existing salaries. Trent McDuffie’s salary alone increases by $20 million next year, although L.A. has options to restructure it if they need to. So who do the Rams keep? Who the Rams can pay It’s difficult to even go down this road without knowing if Matthew Stafford intends to return in 2027 and/or 2028, as well as the potential cost of Aaron Donald if he decides to return in 2026. Even if Donald only plays in 2026, that will impact L.A.‘s spending ability in the future. It’s either less money they can roll over into 2027 or his contract terms could be spread out over multiple years into the future in order to afford him now. So with that many variables, nobody can predict what the Rams can and should do moving forward. What is for certain is that some will stay and should be paid accordingly. When we get into the players lower on L.A.’s priority order that’s when the decisions really get tough. What’s for certain? It’s better to have more talent than less talent, and with a team as talented as the L.A. Rams, it’s important to find values in the draft for when the talent breaks down.
author: John Newman

title: Matthew Stafford could have ‘3 to 4 of his best years ahead’
summary: While most people believe that Matthew Stafford could be entering the last season of his career, one Hall of Fame quarterback thinks that the L.A. Rams’ MVP has yet to reach his prime. Last week, Drew Brees told the media that in his experience, the later seasons of his career were the best, because that’s […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - OCTOBER 15: Drew Brees #9 of the New Orleans Saints and Matthew Stafford #9 of the Detroit Lions talk after a game at the Mercedes-Benz Superdome on October 15, 2017 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Jonathan Bachman/Getty Images) | Getty Images While most people believe that Matthew Stafford could be entering the last season of his career, one Hall of Fame quarterback thinks that the L.A. Rams’ MVP has yet to reach his prime. Last week, Drew Brees told the media that in his experience, the later seasons of his career were the best, because that’s when the mental part of the game was peaking at a time when he was still physically capable of making all the throws and withstanding the rigors of a 17-game NFL schedule. Brees specifically called out Stafford as a player who he has told directly could have “3 to 4 of his best years” ahead of him. “That’s when you’re riding at the level of elite. That’s where Stafford is. I told Matthew Stafford directly, ‘You could have 3 or 4 of the best years of your career coming up.’ He’s been dealing with the back that he had last offseason, so this is all barring injury. Something comes up, you’re dealing with that…You don’t want that to effect or force you to overcompensate to develop bad habits, these are all the things you’re constantly thinking of. That’s where the veteran guys have an advantage over the young gunslingers.“ That’s great news for the Rams. Not so great for Ty Simpson. Stafford won his first MVP last season at age 37, and next season he could be even better. That would align with Brees’s career arc, the former Saints quarterback who finished second in MVP voting when he was 39. Brees led the NFL in completion percentage every season from age 38-40. The Rams drafted Simpson in the first round this year, meaning that he is under contract through 2029, with a fifth-year option for 2030. However, Simpson only played one season of college football, so getting him on the field as soon as possible would be ideal for his development. On one hand, Stafford could lead the Rams to a Super Bowl victory and decide to play into his 40s, but that would keep Simpson on the bench. On the other hand, Stafford could decide the NFL is taking a toll on his body and he’d like to spend more time at home with his family after this season, which would usher in the Simpson era sooner. But that would mean no more Matthew Stafford. Brees thinks Stafford is only entering his prime. For now, the only thing we can guarantee is that he’s entering the 2026 season.

title: Cobie Durant sets tone for Rams-Cowboys joint practice
summary: The Los Angeles Rams and the Dallas Cowboys are set to clash in a joint training camp practice on Tuesday. Former Rams corner Cobie Durant set the tone ahead of time. Durant said he was “overly excited” to take on his old teammates and told reporters “Now you actually get to see what the guy […]
full_text: OXNARD, CALIFORNIA - JULY 30: Cobie Durant #2 of the Dallas Cowboys walks off the field during training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields on July 30, 2026 in Oxnard, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams and the Dallas Cowboys are set to clash in a joint training camp practice on Tuesday. Former Rams corner Cobie Durant set the tone ahead of time. Durant said he was “overly excited” to take on his old teammates and told reporters “Now you actually get to see what the guy next to you is really about going up against another offense.” Durant has spent much of his training camp with his new team covering CeeDee Lamb. As Dallas’ penciled in starting corner, he’ll face Puka Nacua and Davante Adams on Tuesday. Cobie Durant may be the first player to rip a ball away from George Pickens in camp pic.twitter.com/ruR2b8HVFA — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 9, 2026 It will be a full circle moment for the Rams. The secondary become a liability last season that derailed a hopeful Super Bowl run. LA heavily invested in the position group this offseason and acquired Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson from the Kansas City Chiefs. The revamped secondary has been the MVP of training camp according to reports from practice. So do the Rams miss Durant? Probably not. In fact, they may be better off without him. That could very well cause some hard feelings in joint practices that always seem to carry elevated temperatures. The Rams are no strangers to emotions getting a little too high in this shared practice environments. McDuffie and Watson will also have their work cut out for them. Lamb and George Pickens are among the most formidable wide receiver duos across the NFL. It’s a real test and a healthy measuring stick for a secondary that has earned sky-high expectations based on their results so far. Tuesday will be telling in terms of which receivers perform best. Durant has something to prove against his former teammates. The Rams will want to demonstrate that they are significantly improved in coverage in life after Durant. Stay tuned at Turf Show Times for a recap of practice and for all things Rams training camp.

title: Byron Young wants a new contract
summary: Byron Young is entering a contract year with the Los Angeles Rams, and he’s either going to be rewarded for his efforts or a victim of the team’s success. The Rams must decide which players they can afford to keep from a long list of impending free agents and Young, who had 12.5 sacks last […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - JANUARY 13: Linebacker Byron Young #0 of the LA Rams celebrates attempts to tackle runningback Cam Akers #27 of the Minnesota Vikings during the first half of the Minnesota Vikings versus Los Angeles Rams NFL Wild Card football game at State Farm Stadium on January 13, 2025 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Bruce Yeung/Getty Images) | Getty Images Byron Young is entering a contract year with the Los Angeles Rams, and he’s either going to be rewarded for his efforts or a victim of the team’s success. The Rams must decide which players they can afford to keep from a long list of impending free agents and Young, who had 12.5 sacks last season and is now paired opposite of Myles Garrett, is set to get a huge payday in the next 12 months. If not from the Rams, then from a different team. Young told reporters on Sunday last week that it would be “nice to get a contract right now”. Will Les Snead facilitate a deal with Young before Week 1 or not be so “nice”? OLB Byron Young Open To Rams Extension (profootballrumors.com) “Young has been a full-time starter throughout his Rams tenure, serving as an impactful presence along the defensive front each season. The 28-year-old set a new career high in several categories during the 2025 campaign, including sacks (12), tackles (82) and quarterback pressures (40). Another strong showing would result in a substantial market, although Young noted “it’d be nice to get a contract right now.” The Rams already have several notable deals on their books, including offseason acquisitions like Myles Garrett , Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson . Garrett is one of 10 edge rushers currently attached to a deal averaging $30MM or more per season. Young may not manage to reach that level on his second contract, but a substantial raise in 2027 will be in store barring an injury or an unexpected downturn in production. Another campaign working with Los Angeles’ starting front four is expected, and Garrett’s presence could help generate additional sack opportunities for Young, Turner and Braden Fiske .“ Aaron Donald works out with Rams players Donald hasn’t made a decision yet, but was seen working out with Braden Fiske and Desjuan Johnson on Sunday. @AaronDonald97 . Back at doing Speed , Footwork, & Conditioning @BradenFiske_ . @DesjuanJ . @RamsNFL . @NFL . @nflnetwork . @espn . @ESPNNFL . @NFLonFOX . pic.twitter.com/SFBp1ynT7Q — 2Tenths Speed & Agility (@210ths) August 9, 2026 ‘Iron sharpens iron’: New CB McDuffie elevating Rams’ WRs (espn.com) “Davante Adams said “certain guys make plays because they fall into them,” but that’s not the case for McDuffie. “But Trent’s out there doing something every single play,” Adams said. “… He’s always got the right technique. He’s got a great way of reading you out. He understands his position on any given play, whether it’s his leverage or situationally a smart player and great technique. “I don’t want to gas him up too much and have everybody thinking that he’s going to win MVP this year, but I’m really happy with what I see. It’s the epitome of iron sharpens iron. He’s made some plays on me. I got him a couple times yesterday and I’m assuming that’s how it’ll be all year.” CeeDee Lamb looking forward to Rams joint practices ( d210tv ) The Rams and Cowboys hold a joint practice on Tuesday. “That’ll never get old. Ever,” Lamb said. “I’m excited that we were able to do that more times than not and able to connect early on in camp.” The All-Pro receiver is also looking forward to Dallas’ upcoming joint practices with the Los Angeles Rams after spending weeks lining up against familiar teammates. “Being able to compete against somebody else,” Lamb said. “Tired of seeing my own guys who know our plays. They seen it for months now. I feel like we’ll see how we operate when somebody else is across the line of scrimmage.” Rams Defense Continues to Make Noise After Strong Finish to Training Camp (sports.yahoo.com) “A lot of those plays were more of a reflection of great individual plays than necessarily poor execution,” said McVay. “The plays that happened today, there were a handful of turnovers, but I thought it was a really great reflection of excellent execution defensively…I thought the defense was great today and it wasn’t as good for the offense, but it was more of great defense than it was bad offense.” Rams have 2 CBs in PFF’s top-15 ( Athlon ) What a difference one offseason makes! “Pro Football Focus released its cornerback rankings Friday, and the Los Angeles Rams landed two players in the top 15. Trent McDuffie came in at No. 4, while Jaylen Watson checked in at No. 15. The former Kansas City Chiefs defensive backs have transformed a position that was a weakness for the Rams last season, when the team struggled to contain wide receivers on the outside.“ Myles Garrett Is Already Changing the Rams Defense It hasn’t hurt that the defense has gotten Myles Garrett back in the mix after missing three practices toward the end of raining camp. As noted by The Athletic’s Jourdan Rodrigue, Garrett has the ability to take over a practice and had a pick-six off of a screen pass on Saturday.“ Aaron Donald decision updates: Latest rumors, news for Rams return (usatoday) “Coach Sean McVay and the Los Angeles Rams returned to their practice facility in Woodland Hills for the next step of their preseason preparations. The team had previously spent the past two weeks at Loyola Marymount University for training camp. The biggest storyline remains the status of Aaron Donald and whether he will return for a potential championship run this season. McVay had previously stated that there would be an update on Donald’s potential return when the team was back in Woodland Hills.“ “Let’s go o-line!” | Kevin Dotson Mic’d Up at Rams Training Camp (therams.com) “Los Angeles Rams offensive lineman Kevin Dotson was Mic’d Up at Rams Training Camp. Listen in on his day at camp as he chatted with fellow o-linemen, talked run-game strategy with Kyren Williams, and cheered on the big plays at practice.” Sean McVay Puts Rams QB on Notice During Training Camp (heavy.com) “McVay spoke candidly about the Rams vision for their upcoming preseason slate, which opens on the road against the Kansas City Chiefs , specifically regarding Bennett and Simpson. “Ty definitely will. Haven’t decided on Stetson yet,” McVay told reporters on August 8 when asked directly if either will play, before explaining what will determine his decision. “Just really seeing established position, stuff like that.” Notably, it was Bennett who took second-team reps in the Rams’ practice on Saturday. “That would be an endorsement of his status as the official QB2,” the Associated Press’ Greg Beacham posted in reaction. “Jimmy [Garoppolo] didn’t play in either of the past 2 preseasons.” Quentin Lake has a blunt assessment of his role next to Myles Garrett (ramswire) “”You’ve got two, which is I think unheard of, two potentially Defensive Players of the Year up front,” Lake said. “Now, at the end of the day, you just have to do your job and let those guys go do what they do. If it were just Myles, obviously we know where the slide’s going to go to. But if you get AD and Myles, it’s like pick your poison.” Lake, entering the final stretch of a rebuilt secondary that also added cornerbacks Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson this offseason, is coming off a three-year, $42 million extension signed Jan. 1 that runs through 2028.“ LA Rams’ Blake Corum Reveals Offseason Training Behind Camp Surge (sports.yahoo.com) “Corum’s training with Johnson went past a standard speed program. Per the Rams’ training camp observations , Corum said Johnson’s philosophy included “training without shoes on,” working the nervous system and developing fast-twitch muscles. Corum said the focus on his ankle stiffness has helped him get his foot into the ground and explode out of cuts more effectively. That improvement has been noticeable to the Rams.“ Grant Stuard is…
