title: Getting Fernando Mendoza, Aidan O’Connell game-ready vital for Raiders
summary: Kirk Cousins as the starting quarterback for the Las Vegas Raiders should provide no shock value. Not with minority owner Tom Brady adamant that a rookie signal caller sit, watch, and learn during their first year in the NFL. That modus operandi (MO) is echoed throughout Las Vegas as head coach Klint Kubiak and general […]
full_text: HENDERSON, NEVADA - JUNE 09: (L) Fernando Mendoza #15 and Aidan O'Connell #12 of the Las Vegas Raiders warmup during mandatory minicamp at the Las Vegas Raiders Headquarters/Intermountain Health Performance Center on June 09, 2026 in Henderson, Nevada. (Photo by Louis Grasse/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kirk Cousins as the starting quarterback for the Las Vegas Raiders should provide no shock value. Not with minority owner Tom Brady adamant that a rookie signal caller sit, watch, and learn during their first year in the NFL. That modus operandi (MO) is echoed throughout Las Vegas as head coach Klint Kubiak and general manager John Spytek expressed the same philosophy. And thus, it’s the 37-year-old Cousins (who turns 38 on Aug. 19, by the way), who is QB1 and headlining Kubiak’s Raiders offense this coming season. The f amiliarity that the veteran signal caller has with not only Kubiak, but offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko and offensive line coach Rick Dennison help expedite the learning curve for Cousins and the early returns are promising. Cousins age alongside being a short-term bridge quarterback to highly touted Fernando Mendoza — the Indiana product that the Raiders selected No. 1 overall in the 2026 NFL Draft — and the oft-unpredictable nature of the NFL game where injuries happen within a blink of an eye, getting both Mendoza and fellow backup signal caller Aidan O’Connell game-ready is vital for the Silver & Black. Like anything else in pro football, there’s significant challenges to accomplish this. Namely: Practice rep limitations, the learning curve mentioned above, and the career trajectories both backup quarterbacks have. And as our Matt Holder explored in his most-recent mailbag piece, there are viable reasons as to why O’Connell may be the first man up if something awry occurs to Cousins . That all noted, it’d be in the Silver & Black’s best interest to simulate situations to prep the backups and a tiff between Cousins and elite edge rusher Maxx Crosby — that resulted in both sitting out team sessions during the Raiders’ Saturday practice — gave the team that golden opportunity. As our Marcus Johnson observed, Mendoza had a sharp outing as de facto QB1 with Cousins held out . After a practice where Fernando Mendoza got ALL the action with the first team, #Raiders QBs coach Mike Sullivan talks about what stood out to him about his development so far and how the other QBs are a a great asset to one another #RaiderNation pic.twitter.com/lxLx4nvIs0 — Raider Nation Radio (@RNR920AM) August 8, 2026 “Well, I think as much as he has opportunities that are going to put him in realistic situations, and it could be with the threes or the twos or the ones. Also, along those same lines as the defensive players because the speed picks up a little bit,” Raiders quarterbacks coach Mike Sullivan said when asked how important it is to get Mendoza reps with the first team like Saturday’s practice. “So, I think it’s important that he doesn’t get too far ahead of himself, which a young man like that doesn’t do that, and he is locked in on the process and just trying to improve. And so those are the things that we’re looking for to help him take those next steps.” That development process is likely with the second- and third-team unit as Sullivan noted above. Which is an opportune time to talk about the biggest impediment of getting Mendoza or O’Connell first-team reps as practices are geared towards next week’s preseason opener and the regular season. The QB1 Tax Due to the NFL collective bargaining agreement (CBA) with the players union placing strict limits on practice, full-contact, and padded sessions — with eyes on reducing injury, off-setting season expansion to 17 regular-season games, and allow for player recovery — snaps for backup quarterbacks with first-team offense is severely dampened. This was the case long before the new CBA and 17-game expansion — the starter took over 90-percent of the reps to prep, hence, QB1 tax — and now it’s even more limited as there’s only so many snaps to go around for all 32 teams. Prior to Saturday’s practice that saw Cousins sit during the team sessions, Mendoza and O’Connell split the scraps. Meaning, the two did the most with the meager opportunities given to them as the elder statesman of the quarterback room readies himself for being the starter. This compounds both Mendoza’s and O’Connell’s ability to establish chemistry and rhythm with the rest of the offense. But it’s not all doom and gloom in this regard as the reps the backup quarterbacks do get help them establish rapport with other second- and third-team elements, fellow Raiders who would also be thrust into the spotlight if starters ahead of them became suddenly unavailable. #Raiders GM John Spytek on Aidan O'Connell: "He had a great spring. He came back a little bigger, a little stronger. He's thrown the ball really well." (via @Raiders ) pic.twitter.com/7EFUkD7J3p — SleeperRaiders (@SleeperRaiders) July 30, 2026 Learning Curve While Cousins uphill trek in assimilating to the Kubiak system once more has built-in familiarity, the current Raiders coaches he’s worked with prior evolved over time when they were apart from the quarterback. Thus there’s an acclimation period even for the 15-year veteran. Now exponentially multiply that for both backup quarterbacks. And the growing pains are evident for the entire quarterback room so far in camp. Each has taken their turn impressing the coaching staff alongside miscues that provide both on-field instruction and valuable teach tape. While Mendoza comes from a Hoosiers’ pro-style offense, the assimilation to a dominantly under-center operation that Kubiak runs to create play-action success is a big transition. Mendoza’s processing skills and ability to learn certainly help but alongside that are missteps that all rookie quarterbacks go through. “There’s 60 to 80 plays in a game and there’s going to be ups and downs,” Kubiak said regarding Mendoza after one of the team’s practices last week. “So, what quarterback can get the rest of the other 10 players playing at their best. That’s what we’re looking for. There will never be a perfect game or a perfect practice. I think he’s doing a good job. I don’t expect him to be perfect right now.” Flip it to O’Connell and the fourth-year veteran is doing much of the same. He’s also starting from square one with zero prior experience in Kubiak’s offense and while he has critical NFL experience (21 games total with 17 starts), much of his veteran advantage is zapped due to newness. What does help him is he’s no stranger to assimilating to complex offenses as he cut his teeth as a 25-year-old rookie in 2023 under then-head coach Josh McDaniels’ complex scheme. Now mix in divergent paths for Mendoza and O’Connell and things get a bit more complex. As the top pick in the 2026 draft, the former is viewed as the long-term heir apparent at the Raiders’ quarterback position. O’Connell, meanwhile, will be a 28-year-old on the final leg of his rookie contract as the team’s fourth-round pick (135th) in the 2023 draft. Raiders rookie QB Fernando Mendoza finds RB Dylan Laube on a quick outlet out of the backfield. After the period, HC Klint Kubiak spends extra time coaching up Mendoza on the details. 🎥: @cinedirector12 #RaiderNation | #Raiders pic.twitter.com/gUkXmwOMsV — Vegas Sports Today (@VegasSportsTD) August 3, 2026 “Yeah, it’s been fun. Obviously, when you’re in a quarterback room, you spend a lot of time with each other, talking about football a lot, but also talking about life a lot too. So, it’s been fun to get to know those guys on a personal level, and I think then when you do talk about football, it’s a better relationship because of that,” O’Connell said when asked about the competition amongst the quarterbacks. “And we can all learn from each other. We’ve all seen different things and had different experiences. So, I think it takes a growth mindset from each…

title: Las Vegas Raiders Position Coaches to Watch in 2026
summary: For what feels like the 100th year in a row the Las Vegas/Oakland/Los Angeles Raiders will roll into their next season with key changes to their coaching staff. The biggest being brand new coordinators to compliment a brand new head coach in Klint Kubiak. I mentioned the Raiders biggest wild cards being Klint Kubiak, Rob […]
full_text: HENDERSON, NEVADA - MAY 29: Tight end Brock Bowers #89 and tight ends coach Luke Steckel of the Las Vegas Raiders run through a drill during an OTA offseason workout at the Las Vegas Raiders Headquarters/Intermountain Healthcare Performance Center on May 29, 2024 in Henderson, Nevada. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images For what feels like the 100th year in a row the Las Vegas/Oakland/Los Angeles Raiders will roll into their next season with key changes to their coaching staff. The biggest being brand new coordinators to compliment a brand new head coach in Klint Kubiak. I mentioned the Raiders biggest wild cards being Klint Kubiak, Rob Leonard, and Joe DeCamilis in their respective units wild card segments, so feel free to read those and see more on each in that case. That said, a core principle of NFL teams comes with their position coaches, where one can argue the 2nd most important coach on a roster is the OL coach. The Raiders overhauled their total roster, and heavily in their coaching staff, where certain coaches will go a long way not just for 2026 but beyond. OL Coach Rick Dennison & Asst. OL Ben Wilkerson Dennison is the clear coach that’s going to be watched the most this season after the Raiders offensive line has struggled since the departure of former OL coach Carmen Bricillo. Dennison has spent 9 seasons as a primarily OL coach, the most recent coming in 2020 with the Vikings. To start his career, Dennison saw his units rank top 10 in 2002-2005 along with 15th in 2001. To end his career with the Jets/Vikings his unit ranked no higher than 18th. However, Dennison has seen his units rank incredibly highly in terms of the run game ranking top 8 each in 2025, 2019, and 2020 along with mostly top ten finishes outside of four seasons. The Raiders don’t need an elite offensive line, it would be nice, but they still are banking on heavy development. Kolton Miller & Tyler Linderbaum will anchor the unit, assuming both stay healthy, and after that there’s questions. DJ Glaze is the likely starter at RT and he needs a big season to cement his position on the offensive line, and at tackle after key struggles in 2025 against speed rushers. Glaze has strength, good hand skills, but lacks the athleticism. Finding ways to make up for a loss of athleticism with improve technique is crucial for the Raiders, and Dennison. Additionally, Jackson Powers-Johnson needs to find consistency and stay healthy, while the Raiders would also like to see development out of Trey Zuhn, Charles Grant, and Caleb Rogers should they play or not. In addition, Spencer Burford and Jordan Meredith seemed to be relied upon as a possible starter and/or key depth and finding improvements in their games, while getting Meredith back to his 2024 form is a big ask. I mention Wilkerson because of two things, the first being that Rick Dennison is unlikely to remain the Raiders OL coach after this season. Dennison served as an advisor and run game coordinator most of his career after 2020, and he joined the Raiders as their OL coach largely because of Klint Kubiak’s inability to find someone else to coach the room. Wilkerson has spent 2015-2025 as an assistant OL coach with the Bears, Giants, Jets, and Browns seeing some key development under coaches with the Jets and Giants. Wilkerson may be the one asked to step into the role as the Raiders OL coach in 2027, or the reason Las Vegas goes other ways. TE Coach Luke Steckel Steckel has been named not just a top TE coach in the NFL, but also a future OC and head coach candidate. Steckel saw a ton of development in his time with the Titans and Raiders while also having worked with WRs, QBs, and the OL. Steckel is big on blocking, something that the Raiders will want to see improved in 2026 after a poor 2025 season from the TE room. Additionally, Steckel has experience with OC Andrew Janocko, with familiarity working in a system similar to the one that Klint Kubiak will implement in Las Vegas. Steckel has seen Brock Bowers improve each season, and in 2026 Bowers will be tasked with working less as a TE and more in a functional joker position on offense. That in mind, the Raiders will want to see more from Michael Mayer, Ian Thomas, and Carter Runyon who can all step up into a role as a depth TE and see a fair share of 30-50 targets if not more. Steckel may end up working his way into OC considerations this off-season and a strong season from the Raiders TE room in 2026 will go far not only for the Raiders success, but Steckel’s career. DL Coach Travis Smith Smith rejoins the Raiders after spending time with the Bears and Titans as a DL coach, during his time both teams defensive lines struggled to see a ton of improvement, while also ranking near the bottom of the NFL outside of one season in Tennessee. Smith has done really well working with interior pass rushers on their development, something that Las Vegas has struggled with and ideally would like to see from Tonka Hemingway, JJ Pegues, Brandon Cleveland, and Thomas Booker. Smith will likely serve in a role that allows him to work alongside Rob Leonard, who should still have a big part of the defensive line coaching. Smith’s biggest role for the Raiders will be trying to find key development on their young defensive line especially with the Raiders investing decent capital the last two seasons along the defensive line. CB Coach Joe Woods A former DC, Woods should have a big say in helping DC Rob Leonard adjust to his role as an NFL DC. Leonard has most of his experienced tied into the run game and pass rush, with little experience working with coverage units outside 2 seasons as an assistant LB coach. Woods has experience working with the Raiders secondary, coaching them last season, and seeing a breakout season from Eric Stokes while Darien Porter saw a strong rookie season as well. Woods is also tasked with helping the Raiders see development from rookies Hezekiah Masses and Jermod McCoy with additional development from Eric Stokes and Darien Porter. The Raiders secondary is young, and Woods is tasked with a big ask of assisting Rob Leonard’s defensive pass game scheme while also helping to develop their young secondary. SAF Coach Matt Robinson Robinson worked with Rob Leonard during their time with the Ravens, and he should have an interesting role with the Raiders. Robinson worked as an assistant DB coach with the Ravens seeing some time under Colt DB Coach Chris Hewitt, Penn State DC D’Anton Lynn, Ravens DL coach Chuck Smith, Giants DC Dennard Wilson, and former Ravens DC Zachary Orr giving him a wide range of different schemes and coaches to learn from. Robinson spent just one season coaching DBs, and since transitioned to being a LB coach in 2024 and 2025 where in 2025 he was the primary OLB coach for the Ravens while also working with their nickel DBs (Alohi Gilman, Kyle Hamilton). Robinson is extremely young at just 32 years old, and he’s tasked with a weird Raiders DB room especially at safety. The Raiders will likely deploy Treydan Stukes across the defense working in the nickel, strong safety, and free safety along with a BANDIT role. Jeremy Chinn, Devin Lafayette, and Isaiah Pola-Mao can play strong safety/big nickel role while Dalton Johnson will be asked to play free safety more often than not. Robinson’s not only adjusting to a new position group, but tasked with key development of two Raiders rookies. Joe Wood’s experience as a DC and working with safeties should help ease the transition but it’s incredibly interesting to see how Robinson will adjust, and how the Raiders safeties/nickels will play.

He spent time in the programs of the San Francisco 49ers, Houston Texans and Chicago Bears in 2022 and ‘23 before sticking on the Dallas Cowboys’ 53-man roster in 2023. He has a chance to make the 53-man roster as a depth piece or stick around the program on the practice squad.

title: Is the light coming on for Jackson Powers-Johnson during Las Vegas Raiders training camp?
summary: Jackson Powers-Johnson is entering just his third NFL season but has already had an up-and-down career. There have been moments to believe in the 2024 second-round pick, but injuries and inconsistent play have left some room for doubt in his ability to remain a starter on the Las Vegas Raiders’ depth chart moving forward. As […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - NOVEMBER 02: Jackson Powers-Johnson #58 of the Las Vegas Raiders looks to block during the second half of a game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Allegiant Stadium on November 02, 2025 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jackson Powers-Johnson is entering just his third NFL season but has already had an up-and-down career. There have been moments to believe in the 2024 second-round pick, but injuries and inconsistent play have left some room for doubt in his ability to remain a starter on the Las Vegas Raiders’ depth chart moving forward. As a result, Powers-Johnson is competing for a first-string guard spot during the Raiders’ training camp . That being said, the Oregon product has been the first-team offense’s right guard since the spring practices in Las Vegas, and that carried over to the beginning of camp. Also, it seems like he’s made a strong impression on new offensive line coach Rick Dennison and is making strides in the mental part of the game. “I’ve seen a guy that’s very receptive,” Dennison said of Powers-Johnson. “He wants to learn. ‘Yes sir, no sir.’ [If I] tell him to do something, he does it the best he can, and he corrects mistakes. He’s been a great teammate. “…I have [seen consistency from him]. I think he’s done a really good job in the offseason. He’s studied really hard. He’s one of the first guys to answer any question I say in there, and he’s consistent. I wasn’t here, so I couldn’t tell you what happened the last couple years. I know I evaluated him when he came out of the draft, and I think he’s done a great job. He’s working hard, getting better every day.” It’s worth noting that JPJ has had far from the best position coaches to this point in his career. His first was James Cregg, who was fired halfway through the season and replaced by Joe Philbin. Since then, Cregg has been working for Lane Kiffin in the college ranks, serving as Ole Miss’ assistant offensive line coach last season and is currently LSU’s run game coordinator. And while Philbin has a good resume, he clearly was more of a placeholder to get through the 2024 campaign. Then, there was last year’s debacle with Brennan Carroll. Reports surfaced after the season that Carroll was in over his head, and one has to assume he likely would have been let go during the season if it weren’t for the fact that his father was the head coach. From the looks of it, neither Pete nor Brennan Carroll will be coaching in the NFL or College Football this season. Of course, Powers-Johnson has to put the work in and prove himself. But one could argue that he stands to benefit the most from working with a well-tenured offensive line coach like Dennison, who has been a part of four Super Bowl-winning teams and has been coaching in the league since 1995. Based on the coach’s comments, it seems like that’s already making a difference, and the former second-rounder said that’s part of what’s helping him be more consistent so far in camp. “Going out every day, trying to get better at something, knowing that I can go back to a position room and not be treated differently every single day, be treated the same way, and be treated how the coaches tell us they’re going to treat us,” JPJ said. “Also just kind of staying off social media. The only thing I look at now is fly fishing videos on YouTube. So just kind of staying off that, staying off the negativity, staying out of the anxiety, and simple, like make it as simple as possible.” But make no mistake about it; despite a strong start to camp, Powers-Johnson is still in the midst of a battle for a starting job. That was made clear at practice on Thursday, Aug. 6, as he flipped back and forth with second-year guard Caleb Rogers on the right side of the first- and second-string offensive lines. According to assistant head coach Mike McCoy, that’s part of head coach Klint Kubiak’s strategy to determine the five best players in the trenches. “Coach has put a plan in place and moving guys around to see who can do what and give guys opportunities to show what they can do with different groups, different offense and defense personnel groupings and how we’re rotating players,” McCoy replied when asked about the two guards spliting reps. “So that’s going to be a constant change all throughout camp.” This shouldn’t come as any surprise. It hasn’t been a secret that Powers-Johnson will have to earn his spot back this summer, and Dennison said that he’ll be mixing up the offensive line rotations as the offense wraps up installing the playbook. There’s still a lot of time between now and the end of camp, meaning JPJ has to continue to be consistent to win the job. But so far, he’s doing all of the right things and has gotten off to a good start.

title: Pros/cons of a Vita Vea trade
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders have been connected to a potential trade for Tampa Bay Buccaneers star defensive star Vita Vea. Here are some pros and cons of the Raiders trading for him: PRO S He would make the better: He is still an high-level player at his position. He’d be a top five Raider. He wants to be there: Vita reportedly wants to be dealt to one of the California teams or the Raiders since he is from Northern California. Anytime a player of Vea’s caliber has interest in your team, it is worth exploring to see if it makes sense It’s good advertising for the rest of the league. He’s a familiar fit: Vea was in Tampa Bay with now Las Vegas general manager John Spytek and Raiders’ part owner Tom Brady where they all won a Super Bowl together. In addition to knowing Vea, he is also a on-field fit for the Raiders. He’s be a great addition to the defensive line. CONS His age: Vea is 31. That is getting up there for an interior defensive lineman. With his size and age, injuries can start piling up. So, there may be a time limit on his overall effectiveness. His cost: Reportedly, a major reason why Vea wants to leave the Buccaneers, the only team has has played for in his nine-season career, is he wants a contract extension. Plus, the Buccaneers will likely want, at eaest, a Day 2 pick for Vea. That may be a lot for a rebuilding team to give. May not fit direction of rebuild: The age and draft pick and contract cost all play into this factor. Trading for Vea may make sense for a team that has instant playoff hopes instead of a team in a rebuild. Trading for Vea may be a luxury the Raiders can’t afford. According to Mike Reiss of ESPN, the Dolphins are sending the Patriots a 2028 sixth-round selection in exchange for Wallace and a 2029 seventh-round pick. The first man selected was Caleb Douglas out of Texas Tech — a 6’3”, 206 lb pass catcher who some thought was taken a bit early by Miami’s new general manager — Jon-Eric Sullivan. However, through nine training camp practices, Douglas has turned heads with his production thus far, and many are starting to think he could be a major contributor for the Dolphins’ offense during his rookie year. On Monday morning, Sullivan joined 104.3 WQAM radio to speak with the program’s host, Joe Rose, about various topics — including the excitement surrounding Miami’s rookie receiver. “Caleb has a lot of natural gifts. That’s what attracted us to him during the draft process… He’s tall. He’s long. He can run. The thing that he can do from a tall, long athlete is he can bend. He can get in and out of breaks. He’s got extremely quick feet… He’s honing his craft. He’s getting better every day. He’s learning that this is the National Football League, not the Big 12… Some of the hard lessons he’s learned early on, he’s starting to reap the benefits of that. That’s what you’re seeing.” If the Dolphins are to have success in 2026, new names will need to step up — especially in the revamped wide receiver room. If Sullivan found a diamond in the rough in Caleb Douglas, the organization will be able to retool much quicker than most expect.

title: How You Can Watch the Vikings’ 2026 Preseason Games Live
summary: Ladies and gentlemen, we are now mere days away from being able to see the Minnesota Vikings take the field for an actual football game once again. Well, for something that somewhat resembles a football game. It’s a preseason game, but it’s the first time the Vikings have taken the field since they beat the […]
full_text: EAGAN, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 01: Will Reichard #16 of the Minnesota Vikings participates in a drill during Training Camp at Twin Cities Orthopedics Performance Center on August 01, 2026 in Eagan, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ladies and gentlemen, we are now mere days away from being able to see the Minnesota Vikings take the field for an actual football game once again. Well, for something that somewhat resembles a football game. It’s a preseason game, but it’s the first time the Vikings have taken the field since they beat the Packers at U.S. Bank Stadium in Week 18 back in January, so it’s better than nothing. A whole lot better than nothing. Now, the preseason schedule is always a bit different because the games are carried by different channels in different areas, and there are different rules for the networks and those sorts of things. However, a recent development is going to make things significantly easier for out-of-market fans to catch preseason games. We’ll get to that momentarily. First off, I want to point out that the Vikings are going to have one nationally televised preseason game, courtesy of the NFL Network. That will be their third preseason game against the Denver Broncos. That game, which had been listed as TBD, is now officially scheduled for Friday, 28 August at 8:00 PM Central time . For those in the Twin Cities area, the game should be available on FOX 9, and for those in the Denver area, it looks like NBC 9 is the local affiliate there. As far as the other two preseason games, this coming Saturday against the New York Football Giants at MetLife Stadium and next Saturday against the Baltimore Ravens at U.S. Bank Stadium, you’ll first have to check your local listings to see if the game is on in your area. If they’re not, you can use the NFL+ app if you have it, and it used to be that was the only way to watch out-of-market preseason games. However, thanks to the new partnership between the NFL and ESPN, you have a couple of other ways to get your preseason fix. The first way is to use the ESPN app if you have an ESPN Unlimited plan. You can simply log into your ESPN app with your phone or mobile device, find the game there, and watch the action. But this next way is one that most out-of-market Vikings fans are probably going to be pretty happy with. . .and, as one of those myself, I can say that from firsthand knowledge. If you’re an out-of-market fan, there’s a decent chance that you already have YouTube TV, because that’s where the NFL Sunday Ticket package lives now. If you do have YouTube TV, and ESPN is a part of your YouTube TV package (and there’s about a 99% chance that it is), then congratulations. . . you have access to ESPN Unlimited, free of charge. All you need to do is connect your ESPN account to your YouTube TV account, and you’ll be all set. Here’s a link to how you can do that if you haven’t already done so. Now, keep in mind, neither NFL+ nor the ESPN app/ESPN Unlimited will work if the game is available over the air in your local area. The good folks from 506 Sports (who provide us with local coverage maps during the regular season) have a list of which networks are broadcasting each preseason game, so you’ll know which games are being shown where. After checking my ESPN app earlier today and doing a search for “Minnesota Vikings,” it shows that Saturday’s game against the Giants is not available on the streaming service in my area (and a quick check of 506 Sports shows that the game is being shown on my local ABC affiliate, which explains that) but the game against the Ravens, at least as things stand right now, is going to be available for streaming. I don’t know if that’s going to change between now and the 22nd of August, but I guess I’ll find out. So, if you were wanting to watch the Vikings’ preseason games live, you now have a least a couple of alternative ways of being able to do just that. Hopefully, they’ll be less costly than they’ve been in seasons past as well.

title: Gabe Jacas bringing the 3 E’s to the Patriots defensive line
summary: The New England Patriots had to wait a while before Gabe Jacas finally showed up. When he did, however, the second-round draft selection wanted to make sure to send a clear message to his new team and its fans. Jacas was bought in and ready to work. “I just want to let all the Patriots […]
full_text: Foxborough, MA - August 4: New England Patriots linebacker Gabe Jacas meets with the media at training camp on August 4, 2026. (Photo by David L. Ryan/The Boston Globe via Getty Images) | Boston Globe via Getty Images The New England Patriots had to wait a while before Gabe Jacas finally showed up. When he did, however, the second-round draft selection wanted to make sure to send a clear message to his new team and its fans. Jacas was bought in and ready to work. “I just want to let all the Patriots fans now that I’m all behind everybody,” the rookie defender said. “You’re going to get the best player out of me each and every game. Anything I can do to help the team win, I’m going to do it. Whatever it takes.” Coupled with his skillset, Jacas’ approach has allowed him to bring the three E’s to the Patriots defensive line: eagerness, energy, explosiveness. Just ask fellow outside linebacker Dre’Mont Jones “First impression is that he’s eager. He plays with that eagerness and that energy,” said Jones. “As a collective group, and as a team, and as a staff we’re all just trying to hone in his game to make him the most complete player.” Jacas heard his name called 55th overall in this year’s draft, but outside of a brief sideline appearance during rookie minicamp was absent from the Patriots’ offseason program. A left knee injury and subsequent surgery forced him into recovery mode, and the negotiations for his rookie contract to take their time. When he signed, on the second day of training camp, he was the second-to-last draft selection to do so. His deal also included some unusual safety nets to protect the team should his knee cause availability issues. Now that the pact is signed and Jacas back on the field after a brief stint on the non-football injury list, however, the sights are set on the future. And the aforementioned eagerness and energy are helping him with that. “He’s just eager to learn,” said defensive tackle Milton Williams about his young teammate. “He’s happy to be out there, to be competing. He’s a sponge right now. I told him, ‘Just be a sponge, learn as much as you can because we are going to need you this year.’ He’s going to be ready for that challenge but he has to go through his own process as a young player, and keep getting better each and every time he comes out.” So far in training camp, this process appears to have gone well. While working mostly with the backups coming off NFI, Jacas has steadily increased his workload to a point where he started seeing reps with the starters. While those have been limited, they have been enough to leave his teammates impressed and showcase the third of the E’s: his explosiveness. “Really explosive off the edge,” said second-year edge rusher Bradyn Swinson about the 22-year-old. “Real nice dude. Calm dude. He’s been learning everything pretty fast. Built like a freak house, but a good dude. He’s learning everything fast and I’m enjoying him being in the room.”

author: Brian Hines

title: What Caedan Wallace trade to Dolphins means for the Patriots
summary: The trade winds are blowing in Foxborough. On Monday, the team of head coach Mike Vrabel decided to make a move involving interior offensive lineman Caedan Wallace: the former third-round draft pick was sent to the Miami Dolphins in a late-round draft pick exchange. Wallace and a 2029 seventh-round selection were shipped to Florida for […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - DECEMBER 01: Caedan Wallace #70 of the New England Patriots in warm up before a game between the New England Patriots and the New York Giants on December 1, 2025, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Fred Kfoury III/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The trade winds are blowing in Foxborough. On Monday, the team of head coach Mike Vrabel decided to make a move involving interior offensive lineman Caedan Wallace: the former third-round draft pick was sent to the Miami Dolphins in a late-round draft pick exchange. Wallace and a 2029 seventh-round selection were shipped to Florida for a 2028 sixth-rounder. Let’s break down what the move means for the Patriots from a big-picture perspective. Writing on the wall When the Patriots drafted Wallace, they did so in hopes of him becoming their right tackle of the future. Those plans were quickly scrapped: instead of competing for the position in his second season, and first under the new Mike Vrabel-led coaching staff, he was moved inside to guard — a position he had played in practice at Penn State and during the draft preparation, but never in an actual game in either college or the NFL. What followed was effectively a redshirt season. Wallace took the field as an offensive lineman in just one game in 2025, a blowout win over the Jets in Week 17. Other than that, he mostly was part of the inactives list on game day. Heading into 2026, Wallace started out with the second-stringers. However, the Patriots’ sixth practice of training camp brought a change: instead of lining up in his usual position at left guard, second-year man Mehki Butler was the No. 2 left guard of choice. Wallace, meanwhile, was demoted to third string — an ominous sign that eventually set the stage for New England parting way with him. O-line competition evolving With Wallace no longer in the picture, the Patriots’ interior offensive line is now down to eight players: Interior offensive line (8): Alijah Vera-Tucker (75 | LG), Jared Wilson (55 | C), Mike Onwenu (71 | RG), Ben Brown (77), Andrew Rupcich (67), Mehki Butler (63), Jacob Rizy (64), JonDarius Morgan (69) Four of the eight can be seen as either roster locks or fairly safe bets to make the team: Alijah Vera-Tucker, Jared Wilson and Mike Onwenu are the starters, with Ben Brown the top backup. Behind that quartet, Andrew Rupcich seems like the best bet if New England wants to go five deep. The Patriots recently also had veteran Greg Van Roten in town for a workout , a possible reflection of how they feel about their center and guard depth. Marginal gains From a draft value perspective, the Patriots and Dolphins exchanging late-round picks in 2028 and 2029 is negligible. It does, however, mean that New England now is up to six selections in 2028 after it had traded away its first-rounder to Philadelphia in the A.J. Brown trade and a seventh-round pick in the Ja’Lynn Polk package to New Orleans. In total, the Patriots’ 2028 capital now looks like this: Round 2 Round 3 Round 4 Round 5 Round 6 Round 6 (via Miami) In 2029, the Patriots are now also down to six picks; the seventh-rounder they sent to the Dolphins is the first time they have either added or subtracted from that particular pool of selections. While we are on the topic of gains, the Patriots did increase their 2026 cap space by moving on from Wallace. Originally carrying a cap hit of $1.648 million, that number is now down to $303,782: his fully-guaranteed 2026 signing bonus proration, which now moves to the “dead cap” section of the payroll. The same, of course, is true for the 2027 proration also worth $303,782. Meanwhile, the team freed up cap space in both 2026 and 2027 by removing Wallace’s base salaries of $1.344 million and $1.619 million, respectively. For this year, and with the NFL’s Top 51 rule still in place, this means a net cap space increase of $339,392. Rinse/repeat The Patriots being set to release a former third-round draft pick only to reverse course at the last second sounds familiar to you? That’s because it is. Back in early April, reports surfaced that the team was about to waive 2023 third-round selection Marte Mapu. He was never actually put on waivers, though, and instead shipped to Houston : the Texans decided to send a 2027 sixth-round pick to New England for Mapu and a 2027 seventh-rounder — not quite the same trade, but the same circumstances Two left standing The Patriots’ first draft of the post-Bill Belichick era brought the team a franchise quarterback, and little else. With Wallace now gone, after all, only two of the eight original selections remain in New England. The full group looks like this: QB Drake Maye (1-3): Patriots starter WR Ja’Lynn Polk (2-37): traded to Saints, has since retired OL Caedan Wallace (3-68): traded to Dolphins OL Layden Robinson (4-103): released, currently with Falcons WR Javon Baker (4-110): released, currently free agent CB Marcellas Dial Jr. (6-180): Patriots roster bubble QB Joe Milton III (6-193): traded to Cowboys TE Jaheim Bell (7-231): released, currently with Steelers Drake Maye obviously is the one pick the Patriots needed to get right, and so far it seems that they did. That said, the draft as a whole looks a lot like the one in 2000, that resulted in Tom Brady and little else of long-term value. Not a bad outcome by any means, but still well short of expectation at various spots. Long snapper competition? Wallace getting traded to Miami was not the only domino to fall on Monday. The Patriots also re-signed long snapper Niko Lalos, who had been with them earlier in the offseason. Does this mean a long snapper competition is back on the menu? Not necessarily, because it appears Lalos was merely brought aboard to serve as depth behind Julian Ashby. The incumbent, after all, was limited during Monday’s practice due to what has been reported by ESPN’s Mike Reiss to be an ankle injury.

Fortunately for Patriots fans, the QB really is that much more important than everybody else. | Grade: C Pat Lane: I guess I can’t complain about getting something for nothing, but Wallace being a bust certainly hurts the Patriots’ depth at an important position. summary: Update 8/10/2026: Patriots reverse course, trade Caedan Wallace to Dolphins instead of release Caedan Wallace will be leaving the New England Patriots, but his departure will look differently than previously reported. Instead of getting waived by the team that had originally selected him in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft, he has been […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - AUGUST 16: New England Patriots offensive tackle Caedan Wallace (70) looks on after the NFL preseason game between the New England Patriots and Minnesota Vikings on August 16th, 2025, in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Update 8/10/2026: Patriots reverse course, trade Caedan Wallace to Dolphins instead of release Caedan Wallace will be leaving the New England Patriots, but his departure will look differently than previously reported. Instead of getting waived by the team that had originally selected him in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft, he has been traded to the Miami Dolphins. The Patriots, who made the move official on Monday, are receiving a 2028 sixth-round draft pick for Wallace and a 2029 seventh-rounder. Original story 8/10/2026: Patriots reportedly release former third-round draft pick Caedan Wallace, re-sign long snapper The New England Patriots decided to extend the tenure of one of their players on Monday. They also opted to end another’s. Offensive lineman Caedan Wallace, a third-round round selection by the team in the 2024 NFL Draft, is being released. NFL insider Jordan Schultz was first to report the news. In a follow-up move reported by Mike Reiss of ESPN, the team has re-signed long snapper Niko Lalos. Wallace, 26, joined the Patriots as the 68th overall pick in the 2023 draft. He played in six games with two starts during an injury-disrupted rookie campaign, followed by a move from tackle to guard ahead of a four-game sophomore campaign. He entered this year’s training camp as a backup along the interior O-line, but was recently demoted to third-string in favor of second-year man Mehki Butler. Lalos, 29, spent time with the Giants and Saints since entering the NFL as a rookie free agent in 2020. 6-foot-5, 270-pound Dartmouth product, who also had a stint with the now-defunct Seattle Sea Dragons of the XFL, has a combined six games on his résumé. Playing 72 snaps each on special teams and defense, the converted defensive end has registered six tackles, an interception and a fumble recovery. Lalos had originally joined the Patriots in March on a one-year free agency deal. He was released again in May and has now returned. With him on the Patriots’ active roster in place of Wallace, the team is keeping a full stack of players heading toward the upcoming joint practice and preseason opener against the Indianapolis Colts.

title: 5 performances of note from the Patriots’ 13th training camp practice
summary: Between two off-days and the Indianapolis Colts coming to town for a joint practice on Tuesday, the New England Patriots opted to go relatively easy on Day No. 13 of their 2026 training camp. Instead of the full pads that were commonplace last week, they wore shells and helmets during Monday’s session. To recap it, […]
full_text: Foxborough, MA - August 6: New England Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez competes in a drill at training camp on August 6, 2026. (Photo by Lane Turner/The Boston Globe via Getty Images) | Boston Globe via Getty Images Between two off-days and the Indianapolis Colts coming to town for a joint practice on Tuesday, the New England Patriots opted to go relatively easy on Day No. 13 of their 2026 training camp. Instead of the full pads that were commonplace last week, they wore shells and helmets during Monday’s session. To recap it, please head over to our Patriots training camp notebook . In the meantime, here is who caught our eye. Standout of the day WR Romeo Doubs: After a relatively quiet start to his first training camp as a Patriot, Doubs has started hitting his stride. And if that’s what to be expected come the regular season, fans and New England quarterback Drake Maye alike should be pretty excited about what’s in store. On Monday, Doubs caught a pair of touchdowns against the team’s No. 1 cornerback. He first beat Christian Gonzalez in an end-of-game situation by high-pointing a goal line fade just over the Pro Bowler, catching the 3-yard pass with 0:02 left on the clock. Later, he also caught a back-shoulder score against him. Gonzalez has a strong case as the Patriots’ top defender this summer — and maybe even best player overall — so Doubs beating him twice was nothing short of impressive. Other performances of note WR Efton Chism III: Have a day, Efton Chism! The sophomore wide receiver remains in a strong position to ultimately end up on the 53-man roster, especially when he is as productive as he was on Tuesday. Chism led the team with seven receptions during team drills, including one from starting QB Drake Maye. He continues to split his time between the first and second team, but continues to look good. His best play on Monday? A leaping 50-50 touchdown from Tommy DeVito against Marcellas Dial Jr. OT Caleb Lomu: Even with Will Campbell and Morgan Moses available as full participants, the Patriots decided to change up their tackle group. This involved moving the backups: first-round rookie Caleb Lomu went to left tackle, his college position at Utah, while sophomore Marcus Bryant moved to the right. Both saw action with the second- as well as the first-stringers. Lomu in particular looked good, including a perfect 3-0 record in 1-on-1s.. CB Christian Gonzalez: Sometimes you just have to tip your hat; Romeo Doubs’ catches against Gonzalez were simply fantastic plays by the wideout. Other than those two, which could hardly have been better defended, the Patriots’ lock-down cornerback was just that: Gonzalez forced a pair of incompletion while covering A.J. Brown, and also broke up a pass intended for Kayshon Boutte during the two-minute segment. CB Kindle Vildor: Carlton Davis returned to practice on Monday, but it was Vildor who earned the starting gig opposite Gonzalez. The offseason signing was able to build on his performance during Friday’s scrimmage, at one point running stride-for-stride with Romeo Doubs before a well-timed turnaround to break up a Drake Maye deep ball. The race for the CB5 spots continues to evolve, with Vildor seemingly in the process of moving ahead in the competition now. After 13 days working by themselves, the Patriots will welcome the Colts to Gillette Stadium on Tuesday. Their joint session on Tuesday is scheduled to begin at 10:15 a.m. ET and will be open and free to attend for fans.

summary: Hunter Henry received plenty of congratulations from his Patriots teammates out on the practice field on Monday. Just […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - AUGUST 01: New England Patriots tight end Hunter Henry (85) speaks with the media during training camp on August 1, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, MA. (Photo by M. Anthony Nesmith/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Hunter Henry received plenty of congratulations from his Patriots teammates out on the practice field on Monday. Just hours earlier, the tight end had signed a two-year contract extension worth $16 million with a maximum value of $20 million. “It means a lot, man. This place means a lot to me and my wife. Just the organization as a whole. The Kraft family has taken me in. They’ve been so good to me and my family. Giving me a chance, kind of in the middle of my career, to come over here. We have just appreciated it the whole time. We really have,” Henry said following practice. “We’ve enjoyed the area. Enjoyed this fan base. I’ve really just appreciated things a lot. It’s just a blessing. It really is. It’s a true blessing to be able to do this 11 years — coming up, this is my 11th year, and then some more years to go. I’m excited. Excited to be part of this team. I feel like we have a really good football team too, and excited to be a piece of that.” After originally signing in New England as a free agent back in 2021, the extension marks Henry’s third contract with the team. Those five years has featured plenty of ups and downs as a team, but Henry is now set up to finish his career as a Patriot. “To come in and kind of, I feel like, get things going in the right direction in my first year and go to the playoffs. Obviously, it didn’t end like we wanted to, but just felt like we were going in the right direction, and then we obviously hit a lull there for a few years and just weren’t able to kind of get on track, get things going,” Henry said. “And to kind of build and build and build and to get to where we got to last year and then continue to try to build to this year, it’s been a lot of fun to be part of that process, to be kind of a piece of that in the grand scheme of things. “It’s just like I said; it’s a true blessing to be part of it.” It’s been a productive Patriots tenure for the veteran, as Henry, who prides himself on consistency, has recorded over 40 receptions in all five seasons. He enters this season third in franchise history in receptions by a tight end, trailing only Rob Gronkowski and Ben Coates. The three-time captain turned in back-to-back career years in 2024 and 2025 with Drake Maye under center, including a career-high 768 receiving yards last season. Maye and Henry have formed a close bond during their first two seasons together, which played a role in Henry remaining in New England. “That definitely helped. Drake is a good friend of mine and obviously a great quarterback. Just excited to continue to build with him,” Henry said. “That’s my guy. Just a special person. We’ve grown really close over the last few years, and I’m excited to kind of build that relationship off the field but also on the field. He’s just a special player to be around.”

title: Patriots training camp recap: Romeo Doubs headlines offensive highlights
summary: The New England Patriots were back to work on Monday following a weekend off. With the Indianapolis Colts coming to town on Tuesday for a joint practice, the Patriots just donned shells and worked the scout team before ending the day with some more competitive situational periods. Here’s what went down throughout on the hot […]
full_text: Jul 28, 2026; Foxborough, MA, USA; New England Patriots wide receiver Romeo Doubs (87) walks to practice for training camp at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New England Patriots were back to work on Monday following a weekend off. With the Indianapolis Colts coming to town on Tuesday for a joint practice, the Patriots just donned shells and worked the scout team before ending the day with some more competitive situational periods. Here’s what went down throughout on the hot practice fields behind Gillette Stadium. Attendance Absent: DL Christian Barmore, CB Charles Woods, WR Kyle Dixon (new) Limited: CB Carlton Davis, LS Julian Ashby Returnee: WR Cameron Dorner, FB Reggie Gilliam (rest) PUP/NFI: ED Harold Landry III, S Brenden Schooler Despite Mike Vrabel stating that Carlton Davis was expected to be out through this week, the cornerback returned to the practice field for the first time since suffering an injury on July 28. Davis returned in just a limited fashion and likely will keep that status for Tuesday’s joint practice. New England remained with Christian Barmore and Charles Woods, while Kyle Dixon was a new absence after suffering an injury in Friday’s scrimmage. Fellow UDFA wide receiver Cameron Dorner did return. Long snapper Julian Ashby was then limited as he deals with an ankle injury, which sparked the signing of Niko Lalos. Takeaways Offensive highlights: It was a day full of highlight reel catches from the Patriots wide receiving core — particularly in an end-of-practice hurry-up drill with 1:05 on the clock and the offense needing a touchdown. That started with Romeo Doubs high-pointing a goal line fade over Christian Gonzalez on third-down with just seconds remaining. Doubs also hauled in another back shoulder ball with Gonzalez in coverage during the day. Doubs’ catch was quickly followed up by Efton Chism III, who went up-and-over Marcellas Dial Jr. in the corner of the end zone to haul in a touchdown from Tommy DeVito — a catch Chism seems to make on the regular. It was active day for Chism in general as the receiver caught seven combined passes in 7-on-7s and 11-on-11s, including one from Drake Maye as he continues to work in with the first-team offense. DeVito kickstarted an early practice highlight as well, as the quarterback dropped a deep ball perfectly in the bucket to Kyle Williams, who tracked it nicely down the left sideline for an explosive gain. Williams, unfortunately, dropped a short target in the following period. Lomu and the tackles: After mainly repping at right tackle throughout training camp, rookie first-round pick Caleb Lomu flipped back to his natural left tackle position on the second-string offensive line. That kicked Marcus Bryant back to the right side, although both players rotated in as the starting right tackle at times in place of Morgan Moses. On the top unit, Will Campbell returned to being a full participant but still wore the arm brace on his left arm. Defensive roles: With Christian Barmore and Charles Woods sidelined, a handful of defenders were elevated up the depth chart on Monday. Starting along the defensive line, Joshua Farmer, who has put together a strong camp to date, was first up next to Cory Durden and Milton Williams. Back in the secondary, veteran cornerback Kindle Vildor started opposite of Christian Gonzalez. Vildor, who had two breakups on A.J. Brown during Friday’s scrimmage, was impressive again on Monday smothering Doubs on a deep target down the right sideline. Rookies Karon Prunty and Channing Canada (one pass breakup) would then work in behind Gonzalez and Vildor. Other notes: Another impressive day for backup quarterback Tommy DeVito with a successful red zone and one-minute period after connecting on the deep ball with Kyle Williams. In his return, wide receiver Cameron Dorner caught a touchdown from Behren Morton. Rookie tight end Eli Raridon continues to be the top tight end behind Hunter Henry and often share the field with the veteran. On Monday, Raridon hauled in his two targets from Maye. Fellow tight end Jack Westover had three catches from DeVito and Morton in full-team periods. Gabe Jacas continues to mix in with the first-team offense, and was notable around the edge on one instance with the second unit flushing DeVito from the pocket. Rookie linebacker Khalil Jacobs had tight coverage on Lan Larison on a downfield wheel route to force an incompletion in the end zone. Before getting beat twice by Doubs, it was a lockdown day for Christian Gonzalez. He forced two incompletions while in coverage on A.J. Brown while breaking up a pass intended for Kayshon Boutte. Marcus Jones forced an incompletion in coverage on DeMario Douglas in the back corner of the end zone and also ran through untouched for a would-be sack in the hurry-up period. The Patriots will be back to work on Tuesday where they’ll face off against the Indianapolis Colts. Practice will start at 10:15 a.m. ET and Mike Vrabel will speak beforehand.

I enjoyed meeting each and everyone of you and hearing all your stories of how you guys enjoyed watching me play and letting me know the impact I left on… — Michael Thomas (@Cantguardmike) August 9, 2026 Many fans have been questioning the team’s lack of acknowledgement for Thomas, who logged 5,512 yards and 32 touchdowns over his first four seasons in the NFL, including a record breaking 149 reception season that saw the superstar win Offensive Player of the Year in 2019. The relationship between the two has been rocky since Brees and former head coach Sean Payton departed New Orleans and Thomas finding issue with former head coach Dennis Allen and quarterback Derek Carr. Despite the strained relationship, Saints fans have continued to show support to the New Orleans legend. With both the Saints sharing the images of Thomas’ and his meaningful message of gratitude to fans, many are hoping that this could be the beginning of steps to mending the relationship.

title: Cam Jordan dealing with hamstring injury ahead of preseason
summary: Longtime New Orleans Saints DE Cam Jordan suffered a hamstring injury last Thursday during training camp practice that will require further evaluation. Saints head coach Kellen Moore revealed the news after Monday’s media session. As the team is just 4 days away from its first preseason game against the Jacksonville Jaguars and five weeks out […]
full_text: Longtime New Orleans Saints DE Cam Jordan suffered a hamstring injury last Thursday during training camp practice that will require further evaluation. Saints head coach Kellen Moore revealed the news after Monday’s media session. As the team is just 4 days away from its first preseason game against the Jacksonville Jaguars and five weeks out from the regular season opener against the Detroit Lions, Jordan’s timetable for a return is unclear at this point. In June, the veteran edge rusher announced that he would be returning to the Saints on a one-year deal for “one final season.” Jordan has been an ironman for majority of his NFL career, missing just two games throughout his first 15 seasons in the league. He currently owns the franchise sack record and has the potential to rank within top ten all time of the stat. Last season, Jordan finished 2025 with 10.5 sacks, his seventh campaign to hit double digits. The defensive end also has 17 forced fumbles, 12 recoveries, and three interceptions in his career. There are many that expect Cam to be inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame eventually and his presence and leadership both on and off of the field would be sorely missed if this injury keeps No. 94 off of the field early this season.

summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know about after Day 11 of Giants training camp. What we learned from the Giants in West Virginia | ESPN.com Jaxson Dart & Co. are learning a new offense. This seems to be getting overlooked by many. The Giants are running an […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know about after Day 11 of Giants training camp. What we learned from the Giants in West Virginia | ESPN.com Jaxson Dart & Co. are learning a new offense . This seems to be getting overlooked by many. The Giants are running an offense that merges input from Harbaugh (from Baltimore) and Matt Nagy (from Kansas City and Andy Reid) with Greg Roman’s intricate run concepts and Brian Callahan’s modern West Coast concepts. Dart is learning to play under center more than ever and alter his footwork. It’s a process. The coaching staff is learning what Dart & Co. do well. Dart is still learning and mastering the schemes and plays. It will take time. But at least the Giants’ offense feels it made progress throughout training camp, especially with its corrections. “You’re getting a big install each and every day,” Dart said. “So, you just continue to learn, continue to get reps at things and have a lot of really valuable communication.” As long as the Giants continue to improve as the summer progresses and wide receiver Malik Nabers returns soon (which is likely), the offense will be fine. The offensive line looks good. Colton Hood does a day in the life at training camp Colton Hood takes us through a day at camp! pic.twitter.com/wjDldZlT75 — New York Giants (@Giants) August 9, 2026 Giants depth chart analysis: Is CB Paulson Adebo losing grip on starting job? | The Athletic Cornerback continues to be unsettled, with four players getting first-team reps. This is my unofficial tally on who has taken the most first-team reps, in order: Greg Newsome II, Deonte Banks, Paulson Adebo and Colton Hood. Newsome has been steady on the outside and has gotten some work in the slot with Dru Phillips sidelined by a sprained knee. Banks continues to play better than he has in his first three seasons. Even though it’s a new coaching staff, there has to be some internal trepidation about relying on Banks after his past performance. That he has moved ahead of Adebo indicates how disappointing the big-money corner has been. Adebo has given up far too many completions in camp for a supposed No. 1 corner, and his standing on the depth chart reflects the coaching staff’s dissatisfaction with his play. Hood doesn’t look ready to be a Day 1 starter, which is fine considering the Giants will face the Cowboys’ and Rams’ high-octane passing attacks to start the season. Phillips has remained the starting slot corner, but he has split reps with Ar’Darius Washington depending on the situation. 1 Player Each NFL Team Should Put on the 2026 Trade Block This Preseason | Bleacher Report New York Giants: WR Jalin Hyatt. There’s simply no way that Nabers, Darius Slayton, Calvin Austin III, Odell Beckham Jr., Isaiah Hodgins, Darnell Mooney, Braxton Berrios, JuJu Smith-Schuster, Ryan Miller, Beaux Collins, Jalin Hyatt, and rookie third-rounder Malachi Fields all make the 53-player roster. Of the receivers most likely to be cut loose at the end of the month, Hyatt is the one who could bring some sort of value back in a trade. The Tennessee product showed glimpses as a 2023 rookie, catching 23 passes for 373 yards and a 16.2 yards-per-catch average. While he’s largely disappeared since then, he’s still a former third-round pick with legitimate 4.4 speed who could interest receiver-needy teams. What’s next for Malik Nabers in return as he impresses at Giants camp? | The Record Malik Nabers is the best story of Giants training camp to this point, and it’s not even close. Now we will get the opportunity to see what the next chapter brings as the team takes the practice fields back home. And the Giants know Nabers will change the look of the offense the moment he steps into the huddle. title: NY Giants not in West Virginia, or the Taj Mahal, as they resume practice
summary: The New York Giants practiced on Monday for the first time this summer at the construction zone in East Rutherford, N.J. known as the Quest Diagnostics Training Center. The facility is undergoing a massive, multi-pronged renovation that is not expected to be completed until 2028. The Giants understand that they are not in West Virginia […]
full_text: John Harbaugh speaks to media after Giants practice on Monday. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The New York Giants practiced on Monday for the first time this summer at the construction zone in East Rutherford, N.J. known as the Quest Diagnostics Training Center. The facility is undergoing a massive, multi-pronged renovation that is not expected to be completed until 2028. The Giants understand that they are not in West Virginia any longer, and that they are going to have to work around the construction as they go through the season. “It’s not Taj Mahal over there,” Harbaugh said. “We have to make it better. It’s as good as we could do right now, but you kind of learn real quick what you need. The thing I really appreciate about the organization is that the ownership here will do whatever it takes.” Harbaugh used the grass practice fields at Quest as an example of ownership’s willingness to do whatever is necessary. “The fields were playing poorly in the spring,” Harbaugh said. “They went to work on the fields. We actually hired somebody, too. And the fields played great today. They were great. It was a major improvement.” Interesting note from John Harbaugh about the #Giants practice fields. He said they weren't playing well in the spring. So they hired someone and the fields "were great" for the first day at the Quest Diagnostics Training Center this summer. pic.twitter.com/NrYrViOTrf — Jordan Raanan (@JordanRaanan) August 10, 2026 Harbaugh admitted that the construction impacts the way the team operates, but knows they will have to learn to make the best of the situation. “We’re going to be in here for probably two seasons so they can build this over here. It’s going to be incredible. But that’s where we’re going to be operating on it,” Harbaugh said. “So, we have a lot of work to do to make that better. But the players didn’t bat an eye. They understand the circumstances. And it’s gritty. So, maybe it’s just what we needed. Maybe God said, “I need you to be a little grittier as a football team, so we’re going to put you in this park over here.” Edge defender Brian Burns said it was “good to be back home,” and didn’t seem bothered by the construction. “It’s just conditions,” Burns said. “Ain’t really got nothing to do with what’s going on between these lines.” Harbaugh cheered Dart’s slide Our practice report detailed how defensive players cheered when quarterback Jaxson Dart slid while scrambling on a third-down play. Harbaugh said he cheered, too. “I did,” Harbaugh said. “I clapped. I applauded. I applauded when he did that. It was great. “Critical situation drill. We were trying to get a third or fourth down, but mostly third down, like anywhere from three to five in a drive in a game where the offense can win the game in the fourth quarter with a conversion. So, play calls and execution to get that first down, that was what that was. So, we had a great play. He came open. He ran around the corner, got the first down, slid inbounds, kept the clock running. All those things were well done.”

title: Giants training camp, 8/10, practice report: Abdul Carter, Jaxson Dart injured
summary: The New York Giants got back to their home facilities at the Quest Diagnostic Training Center in East Rutherford New Jersey on Sunday, and got back to work Monday afternoon. The team continued to shuffle the bottom third of their roster, officially signing DB JT Woods and releasing defensive lineman Sam Roberts. The Giants practiced […]
full_text: Jaxson Dart | Getty Images The New York Giants got back to their home facilities at the Quest Diagnostic Training Center in East Rutherford New Jersey on Sunday, and got back to work Monday afternoon. The team continued to shuffle the bottom third of their roster, officially signing DB JT Woods and releasing defensive lineman Sam Roberts. The Giants practiced for nearly 3 hours on their first day back after having Sunday off. Our own Ed Valentine wasn’t in attendance today. Injury updates This is a preliminary report (via Dan Duggan of The Athletic) and we’ll update with additional information once we get it from head coach John Harbaugh. Did not practice WR JuJu Smith-Schuster (knee) OL John Michael Schmitz (head) OL Lucas Patrick (knee) OLB Abdul Carter (hand/finger) The most notable one here is Carter, who reportedly watched practice in sweats. After practice, Harbaugh informed reporters that Carter is “fine” and could be back to practice on Tuesday. Harbaugh also confirmed that Schmitz has a concussion. With trainers CB Dru Phillips (knee) CB Greg Newsome II (knee) Both Phillips and Newsome reportedly worked on the side with trainers during practice. New injuries Several Giants seemed to get (hopefully minor) injuries during a tough 2 hour, 50 minute practice on Monday. QB Jaxson Dart (ankle) OG Francis Mauigoa (head/neck) WR Jalin Hyatt (lower leg) DL Chauncey Golston (Head) Duggan reports that Dart rolled his ankle slightly early in practice but didn’t miss any reps. He was able to execute a bootleg rollout but also showed a slight limp walking around. Sisi Mauigoa was checked by trainers late in practice, but finished the final period. Harbaugh says that he doesn’t know the outcome of the check by the trainers and that he’ll know more tomorrow. Harbaugh also says Golston hit his head on the turf during practice. Hyatt injured his lower leg (Duggan reports “ankle”, Pat Leonard reports “knee”) late in the day, after which practice was called. Malik Nabers update Duggan also reports that Malik Nabers continued to do individual work and run routes against air at the start of practice. While he hasn’t worked in one-on-ones or team periods yet, that he’s tolerating this level of work is a positive sign as he works toward Week 1. Practice reports Pressure breaks pipes The Giants might not be as insanely blitz-happy as they were under Wink Martindale, or as Brian Flores is with the Minnesota Vikings. However, they won’t be shy about sending blitzers and forcing quarterbacks to execute under pressure. Duggan reports that Ar’Darius Washington tipped Jaxson Dart pass while blitzing, leading to a tip drill interception for Darius Alexander. Alexander came down with an interception back in West Virginia, and this time the big man returned it for a touchdown. Dart gets down Dart rolling his ankle is obviously a concern, particularly with the Giants’ preseason game against the Vikings looming. However, Jordan Raanan reports that Dart is indeed working on becoming a more discerning runner. Jaxson Dart sliding after running for the first on a live third-down play near the sideline. The defense, which was on that sideline, cheered him for the slide. Darius Slayton finds the end zone The Giants signed Darius Slayton to a big contract last year to provide a veteran presence on the offense as they transition to a new era. He never really seemed to find his groove with Jaxson Dart and required surgery to repair a double sports hernia over the off-season. It seems like he’s building chemistry with Dart in camp and finding his footing again after surgery. Via Art Stapleton : Darius Slayton ended 1st team 2-minute drill with a sweet double-move TD from Jaxson Dart. Went for 50-plus up the right sideline. Duggan reported that rookie CB Colton Hood bit on the double-move, leading to easy separation for Slayton.

title: College football ‘Freaks List’ members who could interest the NY Giants
summary: The 2026 college football season is just around the corner, and with it comes Bruce Feldman’s annual “Freaks List” on The Athletic. Feldman scours the college ranks to find the freakiest athletes in the country, giving us a handy watch list for the coming season. New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh might himself be […]
full_text: ﻿South Carolina wide receiver Nyck Harbor catches a touchdown against Clemson. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The 2026 college football season is just around the corner, and with it comes Bruce Feldman’s annual “ Freaks List ” on The Athletic. Feldman scours the college ranks to find the freakiest athletes in the country, giving us a handy watch list for the coming season. New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh might himself be a “Freaks List” reader. He said earlier this year that athletic traits are important to him. “They have to have — to be successful as a football player, you have to have certain traits,” he said. “So being big is a trait, being long is a trait, being athletic is a trait. Being physical, having strong hands, those are traits. Being fast is a trait. Being able to change direction, being fluid, being extremely coordinated. Some people just have a knack, you can say. Add athleticism to that as well.” As things stand now, we’re anticipating that the Giants could have pressing needs at wide receiver, defensive tackle, defensive back, and interior offensive line next year. Of course, needs today might not be needs in a month, but with the college season approaching, we can use the Freaks List as a good guide of players to watch. Wide receivers The Giants wide receivers are pretty big question mark going forward. We hope that Malik Nabers can build off of his rookie season and that Malachi Fields can prove the Senior Bowl hot takes that he’s a Top 5 receiver correct. However, most of the Giants’ receiving corps is on one-year deals, and the team could look to a freakish athletic talent around Jaxson Dart. As it so happens, this looks like it could be an amazing year for wide receivers. Nyck Harbor (WR, South Carolina) – No. 1 Freak We just can’t quit Nyck Harbor… But when a guy is as unique an athlete as Harbor, it’s understandable. This is his third time topping Feldman’s Freaks List in four years. And he could be high on the Giants’ radar this year. As great as Ohio State receiver Jeremiah Smith could be (and he’s the No.2 Freak), the Giants shouldn’t want to be in position to draft him in April. Harbor, on the other hand, could in the conversation for the Giants anywhere on the first two days. To be this big and this blazing fast is truly rare. NFL scouts who came through Columbia this offseason measured him at 6-foot-6, 243 pounds with over 35-inch arms. His wingspan is 82 1/2 inches. He ran a 10.1 in the 100 and 20.20 in the 200 for the Gamecocks track team, where he’s competing in the NCAAs against runners 60 and 70 pounds lighter than him. Harbor, who just turned 21 in July, has continued to blossom as a receiver. He caught 30 passes last season for a team-leading 618 yards and six TDs. His 20.6 yards per reception ranked third in school history. He finished the season with back-to-back 100-yard receiving games — the first of his career — against Texas A&M and Clemson. KJ Duff (WR, Rutgers) – No. 12 Freak A local boy and an under-the-radar prospect at this point. Duff is right in the Giants’ back yard, and he has unique size as well as an impressive sophomore season in 2025. One of the most impressive players the Scarlet Knights have ever had, the 6-6, 225-pounder is coming off a breakout sophomore season in which he made 60 catches for 1,084 yards and seven TDs. He also led the country with 22 contested catches, according to PFF. This summer, Duff ran a 4.16 shuttle time, which backed up some impressive agility. He did a 10-3 broad jump. Duff’s is definitely a name to keep an eye on for the Giants, and a second 1,000-yard season could have him rising up draft boards in the spring. Ryan Coleman-Williams (WR, Alabama) – No. 38 Freak Coleman-Williams absolutely exploded onto the scene as a 17-year old Freshman, but he had a sophomore slump last year. He also lacks the absurd size of Harbor or Duff, but he’s still an incredible athlete in his own right. He has some similarities in his game and frame with Malik Nabers. That could be a mark in his favor if the Giants want to double down on that skill set. By all accounts, he’s had a fantastic offseason and seems primed for a big season. He’s up to 185 pounds on his 6-0 frame after arriving in Tuscaloosa at 160. He improved his squat to 465 and his power clean to 295. His jump numbers are elite (44-inch vertical, an 11-2 broad jump) and he hit 23.1 mph on the GPS. Defensive line The defensive line could be a real need in 2027 and beyond. Even if Darius Alexander and Bobby Jamison-Travis step up in 2026, the Giants could be well-served to add to their line in next year’s draft. A’Mauri Washington (iDL, Oregon) – No. 3 Freak Washington caught my eye in a big way last year, and he was one of the first players I featured in this year’s Summer Scouting . Washington is a massive nose tackle with explosive power and surprising movement skills for his frame. He came in at No. 4 last year and went on to have a strong season for the Ducks, making a career-high 33 tackles with 4.5 TFLs, 1.5 sacks, 22 pressures and eight passes broken up, which tied for most among all FBS D-linemen. This offseason, Washington trimmed down to 327 pounds from 338 and clocked a 20.7 mph. In addition, he vertical jumped 35 inches, did a back squat with 765 pounds and power cleaned 365. He also did a Hatfield squat with 855 pounds for two reps, video of which went viral. “We limited even how much A’Mauri can squat now,” coach Dan Lanning told The Athletic in late July. “He can probably squat more than we’re even putting on the bar. He’s strong enough.” Washington could be in the conversation for the first defensive tackle off the board, but this also looks like a good year for defensive linemen. He certainly bears watching as a long-term successor to Dexter Lawrence. Junior Poyser (DT, Wisconsin) – No. 46 Freak I’ll freely admit that I didn’t watch Poyser last year at Buffalo, but I’ll definitely be paying attention this year at Wisconsin. He has a squatty frame, but his short shuttle and lower-body power are promising. Even if he doesn’t put up numbers behind the line of scrimmage, he has the potential to be stout at the point of attack. The Ontario native made third-team All-MAC last year at Buffalo after recording 31 tackles and 5.5 sacks. At 6-2, 325, Poyser moves surprisingly well. He ran a 4.55 shuttle time this summer, which would’ve been the fastest among defensive tackles at the 2026 NFL combine. He also vertical jumped 31 inches, broad jumped 9-0 and did 30 reps on the bench with 225, which would’ve tied for second at the combine among DTs. Defensive back The Giants might be deeper than anticipated in the defensive secondary this year if Tae Banks, Greg Newsome, Colton Hood, Ar’Darius Washington, and Tyler Nubin all hit this year. However, Banks, Newsome, and Washington are all on one-year contracts, while Dru Phillips, Nubin, and Jevon Holland are all free agents after this year. The Giants should probably pay attention to both the safeties and corners this year. Brenten “Inky” Jones (DB, OSU) – No. 29 Freak Jones is a former walk-on who was brought to Fields’ attention by Jeremiah Smith and Sonny Styles. If freaks like that are singing your praises, you have to be a special athlete. We’ll have to see what kind of role Jones has, but his special teams upside should catch the Giants’ attention at any rate. The Buckeyes have walk-ons who are Freaks. Last summer, both Jeremiah Smith and Sonny Styles stumped for Inky to be on this list. And with the numbers this guy keeps putting up, he definitely belongs on here. At 6-2, 216 pounds, Jones is a giant corner and gunner on special teams. He is a product of the Buckeyes program. His top end speed is 23.52 mph. Jones, a standout basketball player in high school who set his school’s record in the 400, broad jumped 11 feet this offseason and clocked a 1.47 10-yard split. He bench pressed 385 pounds and squatted 555. He might also have upside as a convert to…

title: NY Giants release defensive tackle, officially announce defensive back signing
summary: The New York Giants on Monday announced the release of defensive tackle Sam Roberts, thinning their competition for roster spots at that position. The release of Roberts is the corresponding move for the previously reported signing of defensive back J.T. Woods. Roberts, a sixth-round pick by the New England Patriots in the 2022 NFL Draft, […]
full_text: Sam Roberts | Getty Images The New York Giants on Monday announced the release of defensive tackle Sam Roberts , thinning their competition for roster spots at that position. The release of Roberts is the corresponding move for the previously reported signing of defensive back J.T. Woods . Roberts, a sixth-round pick by the New England Patriots in the 2022 NFL Draft, was signed this offseason in the hopes he would add depth to the defensive line. Roberts played for the Atlanta Falcons last season, and had a career-best 18 tackles in just five games, along with his only career sack. Roberts, though, missed the entire spring after undergoing surgery for an undisclosed injury. He was in uniform and able to practice throughout the Giants’ 10 workouts in West Virginia, but was not able to make any traction in the competition for roster spots. Woods has not played in an NFL game since 2023. With Dru Phillips dealing with a knee injury and Jarrick Bernard-Converse having been released, the Giants need Woods to help them practice and to get through Saturday’s preseason game against the Minnesota Vikings.
