title: 2026 Atlanta Falcons training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Falcons training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Atlanta Falcons ' camp is taking place in Flowery Branch, Georgia, and Falcons reporter Marc Raimondi has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Falcons camp. We will update this file often. How will the QB battle play out between  Michael Penix Jr . and  Tua Tagovailoa for QB1? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Falcons stories 
 
 Sources: Falcons, RB Robinson reach 3-year deal worth up to $75M 
 Falcons sign Matthew Bergeron to four-year, $96M extension 
 Falcons' Jalon Walker tore ACL, out for season 
 Wife of DC Ulbrich dies of cancer 
 
 
 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 Quarterback Michael Penix Jr . is still not cleared for 11-on-11 sessions, but he has mostly been sharp in practice lately.

 On Monday, Penix was 9-of-11 passing during a 7-on-7 series, including a beautiful completion to tight end  Kyle Pitts Sr . down the right sideline. The throw was right in the bucket and would have gone for a big gain. Penix did get picked off by cornerback Clark Phillips III on his final throw.

 Tua Tagovailoa was 4-of-6 in 11s and working more on pushing the ball down the field.

 Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said he has not yet made a decision on whether Tagovailoa will play in the team's first preseason game Friday against the Denver Broncos . As for Penix, he can't play in any game until he is cleared for 11s in practice, Stefanski said.

 More observations: 

 
 The Falcons signed defensive end Cameron Sample , who was waived last week by the San Francisco 49ers . Sample will provide depth off the edge after second-year standout Jalon Walker went down with a torn ACL last week. 
 Right tackle Jawaan Taylor was activated from the reserve/physically unable to perform list. He is likely to be the team's starting right tackle. The Falcons have been rotating Michael Jerrell , Brandon Walton and rookie seventh-rounder Ethan Onianwa in that spot. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 
 Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa had his best practice of camp, though it did not last long. The practice, that is.

 Lightning halted the Falcons' open practice at Lanier High School in Sugar Hill, Georgia, early on Saturday night. There was still more than 30 minutes left when things were called on the field of a packed stadium.

 Tagovailoa was 6-of-8 passing in 11-on-11 drills, including his best two passes of training camp: a 30-yarder with touch to wide receiver Jahan Dotson and a play-action rollout lob to wide receiver Drake London .

 Tagovailoa returned to full practices earlier this week after dealing with a tight back to start camp.

 
 

 
 
 Friday, Aug. 7 
 Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa hit running back Bijan Robinson on a wheel route that would have gone for a 90-yard touchdown or so during an 11-on-11 session Friday. The series was situational. The Falcons offense was backed up against the opposite goal line and Tagovailoa floated it nicely to Robinson, who had complete daylight.

 It was just another play in another practice this summer here in Flowery Branch, Georgia. But it also felt like more than that, something symbolic. Like a sigh of relief.

 For the first time this training camp, Tagovailoa and Robinson were both full participants in practice. Tagovailoa has been dealing with a tight back and Robinson was a hold-in before signing a three-year contract extension Wednesday that is worth up to $75 million. Robinson got his first carries in 11s Friday.

 More observations: 

 
 Quarterback Michael Penix Jr . is still not cleared for 11s, but has looked sharper lately in 7-on-7 work. On Friday, he was 6-of-9 in the red zone, helped out by a diving catch from wide receiver Keelan Marion . 
 Matt Ryan, the team's president of football and former franchise quarterback, threw to wide receivers Drake London and Jahan Dotson separated from everyone else during a drill Friday. 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 Michael Penix Jr . explained his current situation in the clearest way possible Wednesday.

 "If I can't be on the field," Penix said, "how am I going to be the starter?"

 Penix has been on the field. He has done individual drills and 7-on-7 sessions. But what the Falcons third-year quarterback means is that he has yet to be cleared for 11-on-11 work. And until he does, there cannot be any kind of quarterback competition.

 That is not necessarily news. The Falcons coaching staff made that clear in the spring. But back then there was some expectation Penix would be fully ready for training camp. That has not been the case and Penix said it could be another several weeks before he's good to go.

 Tua Tagovailoa (tight back) took another step toward a full return Wednesday with more work in 11s. He went 5-of-7 passing. At this juncture, it's fair to say Tagovailoa will be the team's Week 1 starter unless something major changes.

 More observations: 

 
 Edge rusher Jalon Walker was officially confirmed as out for the season with a torn ACL after getting injured Tuesday at practice. It's a major blow for a pass rush that was depending him on to make a major impact. He had 5.5 sacks as a rookie last season. 
 Running back Bijan Robinson officially put pen to paper on his three-year extension, which is worth up to $75 million. He is still limited in practice and has not done any 11s as the team ramps him up. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Falcons running back Bijan Robinson returned to practice after a five-day hold-in Tuesday. Robinson got a three-year extension worth up to $75 million and is now the highest-paid running back in the NFL.

 Head coach Kevin Stefanski referred to Robinson's hold-in as "very amicable." Robinson had been at every practice on the hip of running backs coach Michael Pitre prior to actually coming back.

 "He wants to be out there practicing," Falcons running back Brian Robinson Jr . said. "You know he wants to be competing. So, I used to just tell him, 'Yo, take your time, handle your business. Whenever your time comes, it's going to come. I know you want to be out there with us, but we going to hold it down until you come back.'"

 Bijan Robinson didn't do much Tuesday. He worked a bit with the running backs in individual drills and did a play-action drill after practice with quarterback Michael Penix Jr . Pitre said they will work to ramp Bijan up over the next few days based on recommendations by the training and medical staff.

 More observations: 

 
 Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa (tight back) said he continues to make progress and expected to be practicing fully Wednesday. Tagovailoa has eased into 11-on-11 sessions the last two days, but has only thrown seven passes. He was 3-of-4 in 11s on Tuesday. 
 Quarterback Cooper Rush , who signed with the Falcons last Wednesday, got reps with the first-team offense in a two-minute drill near the end of practice. Penix has still not yet been cleared for 11s, but got reps again in 7-on-7 work Tuesday. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa participated in 11-on-11 team sessions Monday for the first time this training camp. Tagovailoa has been dealing with a tight back and was still limited. He did two series, going 3-for-3 passing in 11s with individual drills, as well.

 Michael Penix Jr . (right knee) had his best 7-on-7 session Monday, going 6-of-8 with two drops, working mostly with younger players and reserves. His best throw of camp came on the final play of practice. Penix found  Antwane Wells Jr . for a long touchdown…

title: 2026 NFL training camp news, buzz, fantasy football updates
summary: Here's what we heard on the road at training camp for the 49ers, Bengals, Bills, Browns, Cowboys, Eagles, Jets, Raiders, Ravens, Seahawks and Steelers.
full_text:
NFL training camps are underway ahead of the 2026 season , and Jeremy Fowler, Dan Graziano and Ben Solak have been on the road for their respective annual camp tours. We had updates from their first 12 stops last week , and now we're sharing nuggets and notes from visits to the 49ers, Bengals, Bills, Browns, Cowboys, Eagles, Jets, Raiders, Ravens, Seahawks and Steelers over the past seven days.

 At each camp stop, Jeremy, Dan and Ben talked to players, coaches, executives and scouts to get the latest buzz. We compiled everything they saw and heard, including some nuggets that might be important for fantasy football managers.

 How are quarterback Jalen Hurts and running back Saquon Barkley looking in the Eagles' new offensive system? Are the 49ers veterans worried about all the preseason injuries? Is the plan still for the Raiders to start Kirk Cousins over Fernando Mendoza ? And could the Steelers have one of the best defenses in the league? Here's what we learned for each team on our most recent visits.

 

 
 Jump to a team's camp notes: 
 BAL | BUF | CIN | CLE | DAL | LV 
 NYJ | PHI | PIT | SEA | SF 

 
 

 

 Fowler's notes from Seattle Seahawks camp 
 Dates visited: Aug. 7 
 Location: Renton, Washington

 Best thing I saw/heard: This new offense is brimming with camp optimism. Offensive coordinator Brian Fleury has impressed one of the league's best defenses by "dialing it up," per safety Julian Love .

 "We think they have our script, pretty much," joked Love, noting the timely playcalling mixed with pre-snap adjustments from savvy veterans such as wide receiver  Cooper Kupp and quarterback  Sam Darnold . "They know what we're in. They were on our ass the first few days [of camp]."

 The Seahawks will have two tight ends on the field "very, very often," according to tight end  AJ Barner . That position will help facilitate the motions and shifts, a staple of the San Francisco offense from which Fleury came.

 Wide receiver  Rashid Shaheed  should also be a major factor in 2026. Love said his "blinding speed" has been a problem for the defense all camp, and though Shaheed primarily lines up on the outside, he's also moving around. He was spotted in the backfield during one portion of a Seahawks practice last week. Wide receiver  Jaxon Smith-Njigba 's heavy workload should continue after he accounted for 36% of the targets last season, but Shaheed having a full offseason in Seattle makes him a more viable option in the intermediate parts of the field -- not just deep.

 One thing Fleury did early in the offseason that coach Mike Macdonald liked: He "doubled down" on the fundamentals and how Seattle played stylistically before implementing the full scheme.

 

 "That really resonated with me," Macdonald said. The end result is an offense with the "same bones" as last season under Klint Kubiak but has "a little more variation in the running game," per Barner.

 One key fantasy nugget: The running back rotation will feature "two, possibly three guys in a game plan," Macdonald told me, starting with the preseason. That muddles the fantasy picture a bit. But Jadarian Price will be hard to keep off the field. Macdonald says Price "doesn't feel like a rookie" based on his attention to detail and coachability.

 "He's an impressive guy," Macdonald said. "It will be fun to see him in a game."

 Love says Price's burst is "like a prime Dalvin Cook ." And Barner added that Price has a knack for following the "track" that blockers create.

 Seattle likes to spread the wealth at tailback ( Kenneth Walker III  averaged 13 carries per game last season). George Holani and  Emanuel Wilson  are steady veterans who should be factors early, and Macdonald says he thinks  Zach Charbonnet ( torn ACL ) is getting closer based on how he looks in workouts. But Price's profile should only grow as we approach September.

 Best of the rest: 

 
 Championship messaging permeates the Seahawks building. Barner said a team room that once featured a picture of the Lombardi Trophy has been replaced with the mantra "12 is 1." Macdonald said the Seahawks staff wasn't trying to send a message with that change and just thought it "would look cool." But he has stressed that winning a Super Bowl is something to cherish and hard to replicate -- but what his players can replicate is the team's "way of life" and "going to work with your boys" every day. 
 The Seahawks say safety/big nickel Nick Emmanwori has a chance to return in Week 1 from offseason ankle surgery , but that's not a certainty at this point. Defensive back D'Anthony Bell is expected to step into a bigger role, though Macdonald says "everything is on the table." That means a cornerback, safety or linebacker could fill that spot. Love says Emmanwori is a "unicorn" -- Seattle can't perfectly replace him. Second-round safety Bud Clark could fill in at one of the safety spots in Seattle's three-safety package, and the team is hoping to get third-round corner Julian Neal back from a leg injury in short order. 
 Barner is an ascending tight end who should come into his own in Year 3. He's finally healthy after multiple offseason surgeries. And Fleury's offense should accelerate his progress. Barner can do a little bit of everything. But he made a point to emphasize another tight end when asked about up-and-comers on the roster: Elijah Arroyo . "Tremendously talented player," Barner said. "Year 2, you get more comfortable." Those two will be working off of each other a lot in 2026 as a strength of the offense. 
 The Seahawks' receiver dynamic is interesting, as the coaches are excited about Tory Horton now that he's healthy after cracking his tibia last season. Kupp will remain a factor with his football IQ and rapport with Darnold, and team officials say they feel as if he's moving well at age 33. Expect Seattle to mix and match to find enough snaps for both Kupp and Horton. Really, Smith-Njigba is the only player who won't come off the field much. 
 General manager John Schneider said he knew the Seahawks couldn't bring back everyone from the Super Bowl roster, losing several key players to free agency. And with limited draft capital in April -- the team entered the draft with four picks but left with eight -- Schneider acknowledges Seattle had to emphasize its needs more than it probably wanted. The team drafted players it loves at positions it had to backfill, such as running back and defensive back. The Seahawks also had pass rush high on the list, though they ultimately didn't fill that spot. Schneider says the 2027 draft frees up his staff to prioritize good players regardless of position, as Seattle is projected to have 12 picks next April. He will also keep close tabs on his offensive line. Even though Seattle has a good core there, it wants to maintain strength at that position. Schneider says he feels Seattle didn't do enough of that after the first Super Bowl win a decade ago: "We're a little more cognizant this time with that." 
 
 

 
 

 Solak's notes from Buffalo Bills camp 
 Dates visited: Aug. 7 
 Location: Rochester, New York

 Best thing I saw/heard: I started scratching out this note about halfway through practice when I realized just how many players were taking first-team snaps with the Bills' defense, this isn't complete. But aside from the obvious starters, here's my noncomprehensive list of players who took at least one "starting" snap last Friday for Jim Leonhard's defense: Javon Solomon , DeWayne Carter , Kaleb Elarms-Orr (a lot of excitement for the fourth-round rookie linebacker), Kani Walker , Sam Franklin Jr ., Phidarian Mathis , Keonta Jenkins , Jordan Hancock , Geno Stone  and  Zane Durant .

 

 Rest days and injuries played a part in this, but the Bills are throwing everyone at the wall right now defensively and seeing what sticks. It makes sense. This defense was very much built in the image of Sean McDermott, who ran Buffalo's D since 2017. That means even second-contract players such as …

title: 2026 Buffalo Bills training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Bills training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Buffalo Bills' camp is taking place at St. John Fisher University in Pittsford, New York, and Bills reporter Alaina Getzenberg has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Bills camp. We will update this file often. How will the transition to Jim Leonhard's defense go? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Bills camp 
 
 Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson carted off with leg injury 
 Josh Allen on Bills' alternate uniforms: 'Stop hating on the jerseys' 
 Bills unveil new 'Nickel City' alternate uniforms 
 2026 Buffalo Bills training camp preview 
 
 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 Injuries were the theme of the day as the Buffalo Bills held their first training camp practice at the team's facility in Orchard Park, New York.

 Several starters did not participate, including safety Cole Bishop , cornerback Maxwell Hairston and center Connor McGovern . Also not taking part were running back Ty Johnson , wide receivers Skyler Bell and Ja'Mori Maclin , defensive tackle Zane Durant , defensive back D.J. Miller and punter Mitch Wishnowsky .

 The team did not disclose the nature of the injuries.

 Starting safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson , who missed two practices with a right calf strain, also left practice early after falling to the ground while making a pass breakup in the end zone. Athletic trainers looked at his right leg. He eventually walked to the locker room on his own.

 Practice was held inside the Kaleida Health Performance Center as rain and lightning once again threatened.

 More observations: 

 
 Veteran Lloyd Cushenberry III continued to work with the first-team offense at center in place of McGovern. 
 Top camp standouts include tight end Keleki Latu and cornerback Kani Walker . 
 Offensive coordinator Pete Carmichael attended the Pro Football Hall of Fame ceremony Saturday. He was there in support of Drew Brees, whom he coached in New Orleans. "It was really special," Carmichael said. "Special moment. It was great to see not only Drew and Coach [Sean] Payton but the whole group of guys that had come out just to be there on his behalf." 
 

 
 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 
 On Saturday night, the Bills held their annual "Return of the Blue and Red" practice at Highmark Stadium. It was the Bills' first football activities in their new $2.1 billion home.

 The official welcome featured plenty of fireworks, quite literally.

 One of the biggest came during a two-minute drill, when quarterback Josh Allen found wide receiver Khalil Shakir , as he darted past safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson  and twisted his way into the end zone. Moments later, Allen joined him in the celebration by sliding into the end zone.

 As coach Joe Brady described it, "Josh throwing an unbelievable play to Khalil."

 The night went smoothly, outside of a brief downpour midpractice, and players later marveled at the arena.

 "Wow," tight end Dawson Knox said. "... I got here four hours early. I was just walking around on the field, taking myself on a little tour around everything, just kind of looking at all the details and just taking it in, because it still doesn't feel real yet. ... It's the coolest place I've ever played football in."

 More observations: 

 
 Nickel corner Dee Alford had a nice interception off Allen. The defense made a show of celebrating the pick, even being a bit late to get to the next play. 
 RB Ty Johnson went down during one-on-one drills with a right leg injury. He was helped off the field by athletic trainers and did not return to practice. 
 Starting center Connor McGovern also was injured on the first play of 11-on-11 drills. He returned to play, but then needed further attention from athletic trainers, who were looking at his right leg. McGovern then walked off the field and did not return. Lloyd Cushenberry III filled in for him (outside of a brief appearance by Sedrick Van Pran-Granger ). Brady did not have an update on McGovern or Johnson after practice. 
 Cornerback Maxwell Hairston missed a second straight practice because of an undisclosed injury. Rookie DT Zane Durant , P Mitch Wishnowsky , DB D.J. Miller and WR Mac Dalena also did not participate. 
 The punting job remains Tommy Doman Jr .'s to lose. With Wishnowsky out, Doman punted and held for kicker Tyler Bass , who made all eight of his field goal attempts. The rookie had one fumble, but otherwise a solid day. 
 Rookie undrafted free agent CB Kani Walker  continues to be a surprise in camp. 
 

 

 

 Friday, Aug. 7 
 The Bills wrapped up training camp at St. John Fisher University with a shorter practice in pads.

 Quarterback Josh Allen said one of his takeaways from the time away from Buffalo is how close the team has gotten.

 "This group from offense to defense is the tightest knit group that I've been around really since I've entered the league," Allen said. "The defense is meshing so well together. Just even when you walk in the dorm room or walk in the cafeteria, guys sitting down, talking, really getting to know each other. 
 
"There's just a lot of love on this team and that'll show on the field."

 Allen pointed to the veteran leadership new OLB Bradley Chubb brings as well as the growth of two-time captain ILB Terrel Bernard  in helping the team get to where it is.

 The Bills now head back to Orchard Park, New York, and camp practice starts with the first football work in the new Highmark Stadium on Saturday night.

 Other observations: 

 
 Two defenders took trips to the medical tent during practice. Rookie defensive tackle Zane Durant went in briefly but returned to the sideline with his helmet. Projected starting nickel Dee Alford was slow to get up after defending a pass by Allen to wide receiver Joshua Palmer . He returned to the sideline without his helmet, and second-year DB Jordan Hancock filled in during the absence, but practice ended quickly afterward. 
 LT Dion Dawkins had a veteran rest day. Backups Tylan Grable and then Jude Bowry spent time with the first-team offense. Bowry dealt with penalty issues from the officials present at the session. 
 No practice for CB Maxwell Hairston , WR Mac Dalena or DB D.J. Miller . Coach Joe Brady said the Bills were being precautionary with Hairston after an injury Thursday. Rookie CB Davison Igbinosun worked with the first-team defense in Hairston's place. 
 Former Bills pass rusher Von Miller has posted photos recently alluding to a desire to re-sign with Buffalo. Bills GM and president of football operations Brandon Beane said, "I talk to Von all the time. We're buds. But yeah, I mean, listen, I love Von. You could name 10 other ex-Bills that if everything lined up right, you wouldn't say no to a guy like that. But beyond that, there's nothing imminent or nothing going." 
 
 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 A significant first came from kicker Tyler Bass at practice. Returning after missing the entire 2025 season with a sports hernia, Bass practiced kickoffs and field goals on the main training camp field for the first time this camp. He went 5-of-7, with both misses coming from 45-plus yards. Bass had kicked once in a practice open to the media in the spring.

 Special teams coordinator Jeff Rodgers said earlier in the week that Bass had been kicking outside of open practices and that it was not planned for him to kick in practice until this point.

 "Just the whole organization, I think, Joe [Brady], Jeff ... have done a great job of just integrating me at the…

title: 2026 Carolina Panthers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our updates from Panthers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Carolina Panthers ' camp is taking place in Charlotte, North Carolina, and we'll have the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Panthers camp. We will update this file often. Will QB Bryce Young and the Panthers take another step forward after making the playoffs in 2025? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 A competition is brewing at inside linebacker next to one of the Carolina Panthers ' biggest offseason additions.

 Trevin Wallace is competing with veteran Claudin Cherelus for the second starting linebacker job opposite All-Pro defender Devin Lloyd , head coach Dave Canales confirmed Monday. 

 The Panthers signed Lloyd to a three-year, $41.9 million deal in March to lead their defense. However, when defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero uses a base set, the play-caller will deploy two inside linebackers, which is why the competition becomes paramount for the unit. Wallace, a 2024 third-round pick, has been limited to 25 games (20 starts) during his first two seasons. He has sustained back-to-back season-ending shoulder ailments and underwent surgery for the latest setback after landing on injured reserve in December of last year. 

 Despite his injury struggles over the past two years, Wallace was expected to be the first man up next to Lloyd. Now, he'll need to earn that spot in the lineup. Both Wallace and Cherelus played in the first half during Thursday's 33-30 win over the Arizona Cardinals in the Hall of Fame game in Canton, Ohio.

 Other observations: 

 
 Several players were forced to break up a tussle between center Luke Fortner and cornerback Mike Jackson in the middle of the scrum following an 11-on-11 rep. At one point, Fortner and Jackson, while hanging onto each other, slammed down to the ground. The bout was quickly separated, but backup offensive tackle Stone Forsythe was also pushed to the ground.  
 Canales acknowledged that the defense bounced back on Monday after being one-upped by the offense on Sunday. Backup linebacker Bam Martin-Scott , rookie cornerback Cam Miller and nickel corner Corey Thornton got hands on passes for deflections in coverage during team drills.  
 Backup Kenny Pickett had some nice moments. He made an excellent sideline toss to running back Trevor Etienne with safety Isaiah Simmons closely guarding his inside shoulder. Pickett located the ball perfectly to Etienne, who snagged the ball roughly 25 yards down the field, with Simmons' right arm barely missing a pass breakup. 
 Third-string quarterback Kyle Trask , who was added Sunday, made an excellent sideline throw to training camp standout Ja'seem Reed in team drills. The wide receiver has been getting open with regularity and has become a favorite of the depth QBs. 
 Left guard Damien Lewis (calf) and defensive end Derrick Brown (knee soreness) worked off to the side with trainers. Brown has missed the past two practices, while Lewis has been sidelined for more than a week. 
 
 

 Legette suffers apparent stinger, avoids concussion 
Panthers wide receiver Xavier Legette suffered a "stinger" on a hard fall during Tuesday's practice, according to coach Dave Canales , who added that the third-year player does not have a concussion.
 Legette was trying to make a catch in the corner of the end zone when he came down hard on the back of his head. Trainers rushed to his side and Legette was later seen wiggling his fingers in the air in front of trainers before boarding a cart.

 It was the latest scare in what has been an injury-riddled start to training camp for the Panthers, who have already lost starting linebacker Nic Scourton and rookie wide receiver Chris Brazzell II for the season. Read more 

 
 

 Pickett to start Thursday's preseason game 
 Panthers quarterback Kenny Pickett will start Thursday night's Pro Football Hall of Fame Game against the Arizona Cardinals  ( 8 p.m. ET, NBC ), per ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter . Pickett, No. 2 on the depth chart behind  Bryce Young , will lead a Carolina team that doesn't plan to play any of its starters Thursday night, including rookie offensive tackle  Monroe Freeling .

 Panthers coach Dave Canales added Pickett, 28, to develop behind Young, the No. 1 pick of the 2023 draft. Pickett replaced 38-year-old Andy Dalton , who was traded in March to the Philadelphia Eagles for a 2027 seventh-round draft pick. -- ESPN Staff 

 
 Panthers VP says decision on Young deal 'collaborative' 
 The Panthers remain tight-lipped about the long-term contractual future of quarterback  Bryce Young  as he prepares to enter his fourth NFL season.

 Panthers executive vice president of football operations Brandt Tilis said Monday he felt Young "ascended" to a new level last season, while adding that the 25-year-old's ceiling is still "unknown."

 After being benched early in his second season, the No. 1 overall pick in 2023 responded by throwing for 3,011 yards with 23 touchdowns and 11 interceptions last year while going 8-8 as a starter and leading the Panthers to an NFC South championship. Read more 

 
 Fans show up for scrimmage; injuries cast a shadow 
The Panthers scrimmaged in front of approximately 40,000 fans at Bank of America Stadium on Friday night in their first appearance on their home turf since losing in the opening round of last season's playoffs. Injuries continue to be the story of the team's training camp with three other players kept out of the action.
 Tight end Tommy Tremble , defensive tackle Derrick Brown and linebacker Devin Lloyd all sat out.

 Coach Dave Canales said after the scrimmage that Tremble had "general soreness" in his right knee on which he wore a sleeve on Friday night, and Brown and Lloyd were taking their regularly scheduled "veteran days." Read more 

 

 
  Panthers WR Chris Brazzell to have season-ending knee surgery 

 After suffering a moderate lateral collateral ligament tear in his left knee in practice Wednesday, the team announced Thursday that  Chris Brazzell II  will undergo season-ending surgery. 

 The injuries are beginning to pile up in Carolina, and the third-round pick out of Tennessee is just the latest one. Read more 

 

 Rookie WR Chris Brazzell suffers LCL tear 
 Panthers rookie receiver Chris Brazzell II suffered a moderate lateral collateral ligament tear in his left knee in practice Wednesday and is expected to be sidelined for up to eight weeks, a league source told ESPN, confirming a report by The Athletic.

 The injury came on a noncontact play. Brazzell, who is competing for the Panthers WR3 role, will seek a second opinion.

 Brazzell, selected in the third round out of Tennessee by the Panthers this year, had missed two practices earlier this week because of soreness in that knee. Read more 

 
 TE Evans carted off during camp practice 
 Panthers second-year tight end  Mitchell Evans  was carted off the field on Tuesday with an ankle injury.

 Panthers coach Dave Canales said after practice that Evans got rolled up on and that the initial diagnosis indicates the injury is not viewed as serious.

 "They [the medical staff] are pretty optimistic," Canales said. "But we're going to do a full evaluation just to make sure there's nothing happening in there. ... I'll give you more information as we do the full evaluation." Read more

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Cleveland Browns  camp is taking place at the CrossCountry Mortgage Campus and Browns reporter Daniel Oyefusi has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Browns camp. We will update this file often. The biggest question for Cleveland remains who will be the starting QB?  Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Browns stories 
 
 What are the Browns looking for in their QB competition? 
 Jerry Jeudy clarifies viral video, says he talked to Browns QBs 
 AJ Epenesa grateful to be Eagle after 'weird' Browns situation 
 Deshaun Watson: Preseason is 'great opportunity' after injuries 
 Deion Sanders gives Browns 'insight' on Shedeur Sanders 
 GM Andrew Berry 'hopeful' Browns can reunite with Jadeveon Clowney 
 Sources: Browns, Grant Delpit agree to 3-year, $48M extension 
 
 
 Monday, Aug. 10 
 Coach Todd Monken explained the change in the quarterback rotation last Saturday.

 Though Monken said before the practice that Shedeur Sanders would get a "majority" of first-team reps, he said he was later informed that Sanders had received more padded practices with the starters than Watson in the week. So Monken changed the order of reps.

 Sanders practiced with the starting offense Monday, while Watson led the No. 2 offense.

 "As long as we're still sharing reps, it's a competition," Monken said.

 Monken also said he has not decided which quarterback will start the preseason opener in Chicago on Saturday, but he intends to start Watson in one of the first two preseason games and Sanders in the other.

 "I'd like to get our starters out there for the first series together [in the preseason opener]," Monken said.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Both Watson and Sanders threw short touchdowns during red zone 11-on-11 team drills, but it was overall a mistake-filled practice for the offense. Monken ended a two-minute drill for the No. 1 offense after three consecutive pre-snap penalties. The head coach then called it a day after back-to-back pre-snap infractions for the No. 2 offense. 
 Monken made two notable non-quarterback personnel changes, as rookie left tackle Spencer Fano and rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston practiced with the first-team offense. Fano had been alternating days at starting left tackle with Dawand Jones . Monken said Fano's performance Saturday, in which he went head-to-head with defensive end Jared Verse and even engaged in a post-play scuffle, "solidified" the decision to give the first-round pick more first-team reps. 
 Right tackle Tytus Howard , rookie linebacker Justin Jefferson and cornerback Damarri Mathis returned to practice. 
 Fourteen players did not practice: tight ends Joe Royer (personal) and Jack Stoll ; cornerbacks Myles Bryant and D'Angelo Ross ; fullback Michael Burton ; linebacker Carson Schwesinger ; defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr ., Elijah Chatman , Sam Kamara , Kalia Davis and Maliek Collins ; and offensive linemen Parker Brailsford , Izavion Miller and Zak Zinter . 
 
 
 Saturday, Aug. 8 
 The Browns made a major change to the quarterback rotation in their 10th practice.

 Despite Shedeur Sanders being scheduled to lead the No. 1 offense in his alternating reps with Watson, it was Watson who took every starting rep in team drills. Sanders split the remaining reps with Dillon Gabriel .

 Before practice, coach Todd Monken indicated that there might be a 7-on-7 session in which Watson threw to the team's top pass-catchers but added that "Shedeur will take the majority of the 1 reps today."

 The Browns are off Sunday, and Monken said the coaching staff would use that time to discuss which quarterback will start the preseason opener against the Bears next Saturday in Chicago.

 More observations: 

 
 Watson had another productive practice to cap a bounce-back week for him. His highlight throws included a deep completion to wide receiver Isaiah Bond in 7-on-7 after he got a step ahead of cornerback Tre Avery , then a short touchdown pass to rookie wideout Denzel Boston on a back-shoulder fade in 11-on-11, beating corner Tyron Herring . 
 Right tackle Tytus Howard left practice early with a member of the team's medical staff. Rookie Austin Barber took Howard's spot with the starting offense in team drills. 
 Elgton Jenkins and Teven Jenkins returned to team drills after being limited to individual drills Friday. 
 Fifteen players did not practice: Justin Jefferson (new absence), Joe Royer , Myles Bryant , Michael Burton , Damarri Mathis , Carson Schwesinger ,  Mike Hall Jr ., Parker Brailsford , Izavion Miller , Elijah Chatman , Zak Zinter , Sam Kamara , Kalia Davis , Maliek Collins and Kendrick Green . 
 

 
 Friday, Aug. 7 
 The Browns had a lighter practice indoors and in helmets on Friday, as they are set to practice in pads for more than two hours on Saturday. It was still an eventful session, with all the quarterbacks pushing the ball downfield in team drills.

 Deshaun Watson looked his most comfortable attempting deep passes in camp so far. He connected with wide receiver Isaiah Bond for a long gain in 11-on-11s and also found wideout Jerry Jeudy for a 40-yard touchdown in 7-on-7s. Toward the end of practice during a two-minute drill, Watson evaded the pass rush and rolled out to his left before throwing a pass into the end zone that Bond leapt up and caught.

 

 More observations: 

 
 While Watson had some accurate downfield passes, he was also intercepted by cornerback Denzel Ward on an errant pass that went over the head of Bond; it's Watson's eighth interception in nine practices. 
 The Browns signed offensive lineman Jack Conley and cornerback Jeadyn Lukus , claimed defensive tackle Patrick Jenkins , waived wide receiver Jamari Thrash (injury designation) and linebacker, and placed guard Kendrick Green on injured reserve. 
 Rookie safety Emmanuel McNeil-Warren recorded his first interception of camp, picking off Shedeur Sanders after he overthrew tight end Jack Stoll in 11-on-11s. 
 Safety Donovan McMillon intercepted Dillon Gabriel in 11-on-11s on an underthrown deep ball to rookie wide receiver Kole Wilson . 
 Linebacker Winston Reid forced a fumble on running back Raheim Sanders and recovered the ball to end the two-minute drill led by Sanders. 
 Elgton Jenkins , Mason Graham and Teven Jenkins returned to practice, but both Jenkinses were limited to individual drills. 
 Thirteen players did not practice: Joe Royer , Myles Bryant , Michael Burton , Damarri Mathis , Carson Schwesinger , Mike Hall Jr ., Parker Brailsford , Izavion Miller , Elijah Chatman , Zak Zinter , Sam Kamara , Kalia Davis , Maliek Collins . 
 
 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 
The Browns' eighth day of practice concluded the installation of coach Todd Monken's offense. Going forward, Monken said practices would focus more on situational football, "premier plays," and work against defensive looks that Cleveland will see from opponents this season.
 "What we're trying to do is stack as many good plays as we can within what we're asking them to do on a given day," Monken said. "I'd much prefer stacking really good days, but as the head coach, if the offense is stacking really good days, it probably means the defense wasn't stacking a very good day. So, within every practice there's usually give and take, some ebb and flow of practice -- some things you all don't see, and some things that at the moment we don't see until we see it on tape. So it's really about how many plays in a…

title: Cowboys' D gets first test in joint practice with Rams
summary: We'll get our first peek Tuesday at Dallas' revamped defense under new DC Christian Parker.
full_text:
OXNARD, Calif. -- Looking back at last summer, the Dallas Cowboys ' joint practices with the Los Angeles Rams  could have been viewed as a precursor to what was to be for the 2025 Dallas defense.

 Jimmy Garoppolo  -- not future MVP  Matthew Stafford , who was dealing with back issues -- lit up the Cowboys' defense that day. Receivers  Davante Adams , Puka Nacua and Tutu Atwell had their way.  Kyren Williams broke off big runs.

 The counter by those in the organization was that the defense did not have Trevon Diggs (injury) or Micah Parsons (hold-in), and the unit was vanilla with its looks and didn't show anything.

 Without knowing then what is known now, that was all plausible -- but then the season started and the Cowboys allowed 511 points, most in the NFL.

 On Tuesday, the Cowboys travel to the Rams' facility in Woodland Hills, California, for a joint practice. Just like last year, they have a new coordinator -- Christian Parker replacing Matt Eberflus -- and an almost completely revamped staff.

 

 So far in Cowboys vs. Cowboys practices, the reviews have been positive for Parker and his defense, but the Rams offer a chance for a test. And with the starters not expected to play in the preseason games, the importance of this practice -- and the Aug. 18 work against the New Orleans Saints -- is not lost on Parker.

 "I think it's real important, especially as much experience as coach [Sean] McVay has and Matthew Stafford at that position," Parker said. "The pre-snap looks and the motions and the things they do formationally, they've been a very successful offense during his tenure there. So it's going to be a good test for us, where we're at, and make sure our eyes are right and we're playing with the right demeanor."

 Safety Malik Hooker is one of the holdovers from last year's practice against the Rams.

 "We allowed a lot of big plays given up on communication errors," he said. "Not only that, I feel like our physicality didn't really show as much that day. So looking forward to coming out here and being able to have a good healthy practice with those guys and put our skills to the test."

 A poor performance Tuesday should not dictate what the 2026 Cowboys can be, but holding up better against one of the NFC favorites would help a defense in search of confidence with 12 new starters or key contributors.

 Parker said the organized team activities and minicamp were about the defenders getting their undergraduate degree; training camp is about working toward their master's.

 "That's more of an accelerated program, so we've got to get going quick," Parker said.

 Communication is key for Parker.

 

 Coach Brian Schottenheimer noticed the difference when he heard how loud the meeting room has been. Dak Prescott joked that "it's like we're playing on the road" when the offense hears the noise coming from the defensive room.

 "I love what he says and how he refers to it as it's two parts, giving and receiving," Schottenheimer said. "You just can't be blurting out a bunch of stuff that doesn't matter and confusing people. You got to give it. You got to receive it."

 On the practice field, the defense is constantly communicating. It starts with the meetings.

 "If we're showing a play from practice, for example, if you're a linebacker on the field, you're making the front adjustment," Parker said. "If you're an outside linebacker and you see that the 'Y' [receiver] is off, you're saying something to your partner. If I'm a DB, I'm calling out the coverage communication. Motion happens, we're alerting this, we're passing off this. Once the play starts, what is that communication?

 "We want the meeting room to sound the same as it does on the field. Your brain doesn't know when you're not taking a physical rep. It just knows that your brain is strained. So as many reps that we can get on task, we want to try to take advantage of those in that space."

 

 The Cowboys' offense can stress the best defenses with Prescott, skill players  CeeDee Lamb , George Pickens , Javonte Williams , Jake Ferguson and a strong offensive line. There have been times through six padded practices that Prescott has admitted frustration offensively, but that is not a bad thing.

 "It's just the collab effort of their intensity and their communication is felt," Prescott said. "It's definitely felt when we're just out there and we're motioning and we're making our calls. And then post-play, anytime that they've made a play, they've celebrated deservingly so. I just think that raises the energy of the whole team, pisses us off a little bit on offense, but that's what camp's about."

 Stafford is expected to practice Tuesday, as are Adams and Nacua. Williams ran for 1,252 yards and 10 scores last year. McVay is one of the best playcallers in the NFL, known for his ability to scheme things open, although it is unlikely he will break out the full script, in part because these teams meet Dec. 20 at SoFi Stadium.

 But this will give the Cowboys' defense a test, and they'll need to fare better than they did a year ago.

 "It's definitely going to be a challenge," Hooker said, "but I feel like the way we've been coming out here, stacking the days up against our offense -- who I feel is the best in the league at what they do -- man, I feel like there's nobody we can't match up against."

title: Quinnen Williams agrees to a contract extension
summary: Todd Archer breaks down the Cowboys' decision to extend Quinnen Williams.

title: What Quinnen Williams' contract extension means for Cowboys
summary: With Williams' three-year, $105.9 million deal, Dallas appears to have rediscovered its old formula of locking in its stars.
full_text:
OXNARD, Calif. -- The Dallas Cowboys have rediscovered the formula they used in the past regarding contract extensions for their key players.

 The three-year, $105.9 million extension agreed to Monday by Pro Bowl defensive tackle Quinnen Williams  -- with an annual average of $35.3 million that is second highest among defensive tackles -- is yet another sign.

 The George Pickens  contract situation ( franchise tagged for 2026 ) not withstanding, in the past 12 months the Cowboys have made Pro Bowl guard Tyler Smith the highest paid interior offensive lineman (subsequently passed by the Raiders' Tyler Linderbaum and Falcons' Chris Lindstrom ) at $24 million per season and Pro Bowl kicker  Brandon Aubrey the highest paid ($7 million) at his position.

 They have also kept key players away from unrestricted free agency, including tight end Jake Ferguson and cornerback DaRon Bland , who signed deals that made each of them the eighth-highest paid player at their positions. Ferguson's deal averages $12.5 million a season, and Bland's checks in at $22.5 million. Add defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa to that list after he signed a four-year, $80 million contract in March 2025, though he was traded to the San Francisco 49ers  before the draft.

 "Every deal's different. You just hit certain bumps in the road where things don't [work out]," executive vice president Stephen Jones said. "It's not because we don't want to. It's just getting the right deal for what we think, for the organization. I think that's the important part.

 "Obviously, no one thinks more of Dak than we do, but it's not easy to get one of the top quarterbacks in the league [done] and it can take time. Made a run at CeeDee the year before and it wasn't the right timing. So we put it on the backburner, never any hard feelings, then got it done."

 

 It was not too long ago that the Cowboys sweated out deals with Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb . In 2024, Prescott did not agree to his record-setting $60 million a year deal until the morning of the season opener, and Lamb sat out most of training camp before signing his deal that averaged $34 million and made him, at the time, the second-highest paid wide receiver.

 Last summer was dominated by the Micah Parsons ' saga. He was set to play last season on his fifth-year option when discussions went haywire after owner and general manager Jerry Jones thought he and the edge rusher agreed to an extension only to see Parsons say he would not sign a deal without involvement from his agent.

 Parsons went through a high-profile hold-in during training camp, eventually demanding a trade while in Oxnard. The week before the season started, he was traded to the Green Bay Packers for defensive tackle Kenny Clark and two first-round picks.

 

 If the Cowboys finish with a better record than the Packers in 2026, then Green Bay's first-rounder will be dealt to the New York Jets as part of the trade Dallas made with New York to acquire Williams in November.

 Williams is 28 and was signed through 2027. He is now signed through 2030.

 In the past, the Cowboys used major extensions to keep star players well away from free agency, including  DeMarcus Ware , Tony Romo , Jason Witten , Terence Newman and more recently (2023) with Trevon Diggs , who was released in January.

 The Cowboys have a core of key figures under contract. Prescott and running back Javonte Williams  are signed through 2028; Lamb, Ferguson and Bland are signed through 2029; Williams, Aubrey and Smith through 2030.

 

 Stephen Jones likes to say it takes two sides to get a deal done. At the start of camp, he said the organization wanted Williams for the long haul. Over the weekend, Williams' agent, Nicole Lynn of Klutch Sports, was at practice, perhaps jump-starting discussions.

 Perhaps Pickens' will be the next contract to get done, but that cannot happen until next offseason.

 He is playing this season on the $27.3 million franchise tag after the Cowboys declined to engage in extension talks this offseason. Jerry Jones said he has a long-term vision for Pickens.

 If he performs as he did in 2025 with career highs in catches, yards and touchdowns, will the talks get done as early and smoothly as the others have lately? Or will we see a return to sweating out a new deal?

 Stephen Jones is not thinking about how the Pickens' talks will go next offseason.

 "I'm worried about this season, tell you the truth," Jones said. "I want to go win some games."

title: 2026 Denver Broncos training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Broncos training camp, including intel on the QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Denver Broncos camp is taking place in Englewood, Colorado, and Broncos reporter Jeff Legwold has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Broncos camp. We will update this file often as we track the Broncos' push toward getting to the Super Bowl after falling one game short last season. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Broncos camp 
 
 Payton to talk to Taysom Hill about interest in Broncos 
 Broncos QB Bo Nix won't be afraid to run on repaired ankle 
 How will Broncos' Sean Payton adjust to not calling plays? 
 Cooper practices Wednesday despite legal troubles 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 A recent spate of what Sean Payton called "soft-tissue" injuries prompted the coach to adjust the end of practice. After the two-and-half-hour workout, Payton had the strength and conditioning staff add a longer, more formal warm-down period. Payton said he expected to continue to have the players go through the longer warm down in the days ahead.

 "Got to get a handle on some of the soft-tissue stuff. ... Strains, hamstring or groins, [we] continue to fight through that," Payton said. "I don't think it's heat related. ... You always try to look at your pre-practice routine, your hydration obviously."

 Running back J.K. Dobbins left the practice field with an injury and did not return. Wide receivers Marvin Mims Jr . -- who returned to practice Monday -- and Jaylen Waddle have also had similar injuries in recent weeks.

 More observations: 

 
 Payton said he will play most, if not all, of the healthy starters for at least some snaps in Friday's preseason opener in Atlanta. Payton said the coaches hadn't yet formalized the snap counts yet, but that he wanted regulars to get at least some work. "You have to build callouses," he said. 
 Quarterback Bo Nix hopes first-year offensive coordinator Davis Webb will be on the sideline during games to call plays instead of in the coaches' box. Payton said Monday he and Webb hadn't yet discussed the gameday setup yet, but that he expected Webb to call plays from the sideline. "I always loved quarterback-to-playcaller when they're on the sideline with me," Nix said. "You get the feel of the game a little differently. ... They get to feel the emotions of a game on the sideline. ... I like when the playcaller is right there, and when I come off I can have that eye-to-eye conversation." 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 When the Broncos went through a scripted scrimmage, it was safety Brandon Jones who was 3-of-4 in field goal attempts.

 Why? Broncos special teams coach Darren Rizzi said most of the Australian punters he has worked with in his long coaching career, including the Broncos' Jeremy Crawshaw , have not kicked field goals.

 So the Broncos need a contingency plan in case  Wil Lutz gets injured in a game. And with Lutz and several Broncos coaches, including Sean Payton, in Canton, Ohio, to see Drew Brees be enshrined into the Hall of Fame, it was Jones getting the kicks.

 Rizzi said Jones' longest made field goal was 39 yards, but Jones said he made a 50-yarder in OTAs. At one point, as Jones moved into position before the snap, the crowd of several thousand people chanted his name.

 "Have a lot of respect for kickers when the crowd started chanting my name, I got really nervous, and I'm like, 'I'm about to shank this,' but thankfully it went in," Jones said.

 Jones was 2-of-2 from the center of the field, 1-of-2 from the left hashmark.

 Other observations: 

 
 With wide receiver  Courtland Sutton getting some rest days in camp to go with recent injuries to Jaylen Waddle and Marvin Mims Jr ., Pat Bryant has consistently made play after play as a reliable option for quarterback  Bo Nix . Bryant's leaping, get-the-toes-down scoring grab in red zone work was just another example. Bryant leaped over a double-team of Ja'Quan McMillian and Jahdae Barron to make the catch. Offensive coordinator Davis Webb said, "Man, Patty Ice has had some really, really good practices." 
 The Broncos closed out a stretch of six consecutive days on the practice field with a scripted scrimmage, but held out some of their healthy high-profile players, including cornerback Pat Surtain II , tackle Mike McGlinchey , safety Talanoa Hufanga and running back J.K. Dobbins . 
 The defense shut down both two-minute drives by the offense to close out the practice -- the situation was offense trailing by four with 1:14 left in the game. Nix led the first group, and  Sam Ehlinger led the other, which made it to the 8-yard line before the defense was credited with a sack to end the drive. 
 

 

 Friday, Aug. 7 
 If Broncos coach Sean Payton checks his phone on his flight to Canton, Ohio, on Friday he isn't going to like some of the messages. It was a rugged day of practice, as wide receiver Marvin Mims Jr ., tight end Nate Adkins and defensive lineman Matt Henningsen left with injuries.

 Mims pulled up after running a deep route and hopped off the field before he went to the locker room. Adkins walked into the locker room with Mims and a trainer while Henningsen, who missed last season with a ruptured Achilles he suffered in last summer's camp, was carted to the locker room with an apparent leg injury.

 That comes in addition to the other injuries the Broncos suffered already this week to wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (leg) and edge rusher Nik Bonitto (ankle/foot). Bonitto returned to practice Friday on a limited basis.

 More observations: 

 
 Payton, several assistant coaches and kicker Wil Lutz left during Friday's practice to head to Ohio for the events surrounding Drew Brees' enshrinement into the Pro Football Hall of Fame. Payton will be Brees' presenter at the Gold Jacket dinner Friday night and at the enshrinement ceremony Saturday. The group had all been with the New Orleans Saints during Brees' career. 
 Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph ran practice after Payton left and will run Saturday's workout in which the Broncos will go through a controlled scrimmage. Joseph spoke to the team at the end of practice as Payton usually does and cornerback Ja'Quan McMillian said he told Joseph "head coach looks good on you." 
 Wide receiver Courtland Sutton practiced fully Friday, while offensive tackle  Garett Bolles , defensive tackle D.J. Jones and defensive tackle Malcolm Roach had rest days. 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle , who left practice Wednesday with what appeared to be a left leg injury, did not practice Thursday and moved gingerly between drills as he watched practice. Coach Sean Payton said after practice Waddle had suffered a "strain" and "I think we'll see him back in the next four to five days."

 The Broncos practice Friday and Saturday before a player's off day Sunday. They have three full practice days next week before a travel day for their Aug. 14 preseason opener in Atlanta. Waddle's status for that preseason opener, which is when Payton typically plays starters at least one quarter, is still a question mark.

 More observations: 

 
 Courtland Sutton , who had been held out the previous two days for rest, participated on a limited basis and is expected to practice fully Friday. Payton said Sutton is not injured, but the rest schedule is "our protocol" for Sutton and that other veteran players in the coming weeks will have similar schedules. Sutton said the team's training staff showed him tracking data from practices late…

title: Jared Goff understands urgency, eager for Lions to return to form
summary: Coach Dan Campbell is thrilled with the urgency and guidance Goff shows his Lions teammates.
full_text:
ALLEN PARK, Mich. -- Moments after an intense two-hour practice where he was chased around by Detroit Lions defenders, veteran quarterback Jared Goff chased his toddler daughter around on the same practice field on Monday afternoon.

 As Goff enters his 11th season, the five-time Pro Bowler has felt more appreciative of sharing these training camp moments after practice with young Romy Isabelle and his wife, Christen.

 Now that everything is set -- his future, his money, and his team is in place -- the 31-year-old is looking to the help Lions get over the hump to return to the postseason and potentially bring home a Super Bowl.

 And fatherhood has helped him keep that perspective that time is valuable as Detroit hopes to bounce back from a disappointing 9-8 season.

 "Yeah, makes it fun when it's over. I get to see her and yeah, it's really fun," Goff said. "It's really cool. Something you've always dreamed about as a player, having your child here and her being able to enjoy it. I know she probably won't remember these days, but I know I will."

 More so than any mechanics or techniques, Lions coach Dan Campbell feels that Goff has grown over the past seasons with his "urgency" to win now, with his family routinely present throughout training camp.

 Goff and most of the Lions starters will not play in the preseason opener against the Cincinnati Bengals this week but could see some action against Washington on Aug. 22 ahead of the season opener against New Orleans on Sept. 13.

 "It's the mentality, the urgency, the leadership, the, 'Hey man, let's go.' We cannot accept anything less than the best. He wants to be the best in the league, and he wants to run the best offense in the league," Campbell said. "And to get there, we've got to go, we don't have time. That's where I really feel him growing. And every year I felt more of an urgency out of him in that regard, more command, more leadership and that has to come organically. It can't be forced on somebody, it can't. And so that's great to see out of him."

 Goff credits that seriousness to age, maturity and previous experiences in the NFL. He wants to erase that feeling of missing the playoffs for the first time since 2022 after back-to-back 12-win seasons.

 "I think it's just human nature. You start realizing where things can slip and you don't want to allow that to happen," Goff said following Monday's practice. "And the older I get, the more I'm learning and trying to stay on that type of stuff, but yeah, it's good that it's noticeable.

 "It's not necessarily something I'm conscious of every day, but I think it's maybe just overall a little bit more of that mindset this year."

 It's no secret that Goff is on the back half of his career, but backup rookie QB Luke Altmyer has also been attentive to how detail-oriented he still is, since the start of training camp. That professionalism continues to rub off on his new teammates.

 "Doing things at a high level, consistently day after day. Doing the mundane things, the ordinary things at a very high level," Altmyer said. "He makes the ordinary look extraordinary. And I try to master that as well, this position, and during camp it can get pretty mundane and ordinary and he does the things, the little things at a high level, over and over again."

 Goff spent the first five seasons of his career with the Los Angeles Rams , after being selected first overall in the 2016 NFL draft, and is heading into his sixth season in Detroit.

 He recently joined NFL legends Peyton Manning and Tom Brady as the only quarterbacks in NFL history to win 13 games in a season for multiple franchises and is one of six quarterbacks in NFL history to log 100 touchdown passes with multiple franchises.

 But he hasn't thought about how much longer he wants to play. His focus is on helping the Lions get back on track right now.

 "No, I'm right in the middle of it. No, I haven't," Goff said. "I think I said this other day, until I don't feel like I can help a team win a championship. And I think that's going to be a long time."

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Detroit Lions camp is taking place in Allen Park, Mich., and Lions reporter Eric Woodyard has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Lions camp. We will update this file often. Can Dan Campbell & Co. get Detroit back in the playoffs in 2026? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Lions camp 
 
 Lions OL Mays out into season; RB Pacheco hurts knee 
 Lions make Jahmyr Gibbs highest-paid running back in NFL history 
 Ex-All Pro LB Devin White joins Lions on 1-year deal 
 
 

 Monday, Aug. 10 

 Veteran OL Cade Mays suffered a wrist injury that is expected to sideline him for 8-10 weeks. In his absence,  Seth McLaughlin took first-team reps at center, where he battled against former Ohio State teammate Tyleik Williams and DT Alim McNeill  during Monday's practice. OL Michael Niese took the bulk of the second team reps at center as Detroit tries to identify the best starting unit ahead of the regular season.

 "I'm taking it one practice at a time, getting better," McLaughlin said. "With practice, it's (Day) 11 at camp and you're not who you wanna be on the first day of the regular season so there's a long way to go to keep getting better."

 Prior to Monday's practice, Lions QB Jared Goff didn't have many reps with McLaughlin, but has been impressed with him so far as he continues to adjust to the role. Throughout OTAs and the offseason, Goff mainly worked with Mays and veteran OL  Juice Scruggs , who is also expected to be in the mix for the starting role once he returns from a soft tissue injury that has kept him out.

 "He did a good job. He really did," Goff said of McLaughlin. "He stepped in there. He had good authority with his calls. He was sharp. He was decisive. I think that's all you can ask for."

 

 Sunday, Aug. 9 
 Detroit Lions QB Jared Goff , and most of the starters, will not play in the preseason opener against the Cincinnati Bengals this week but could see some action against Washington on Aug. 22, according to head coach Dan Campbell. Undrafted rookie QB Lions  Luke Altmyer will now continue in the QB2 role behind Goff and is expected to take heavy snaps on Thursday, but Detroit will likely be adding another veteran QB for depth purposes as early as this week after Teddy Bridgewater decided to step away from the team. Altmyer says he's "excited" for the opportunity ahead.

 "I've played at a high level with the Big Ten and I've played in football games but it's a different level and I think that's the challenge is can you maintain emotions because it can get you really high and really excited," Altmyer said after Sunday's practice. "But, trusting my abilities, trusting my preparation, trusting my teammates. I think that's the word trust."

 Other observations:  

 
 Lions veteran QB Teddy Bridgewater has decided to step away from the team amid training camp and was officially placed on the reserved/retired list ahead of Sunday's practice. Campbell says he will be "missed" but this retirement could be for good. 
 Lions HC Dan Campbell and his wife Holly attended the Pro Football Hall of Fame induction ceremony in Canton to support legendary New Orleans Saints QB Drew Brees on Saturday on an off day. Campbell was an assistant/tight ends coach in New Orleans from 2016-20 and signed with the Saints as a player in 2009. "It was a reminder. It was refreshing just to be able to stand in the presence of greatness with those guys," Campbell said. 
 The Lions signed CB Ryan Cooper and LB Amen Ogbongbemiga and waived TE Nick Muse . 
 
 

 Friday, Aug. 7 

 The connection between Jared Goff and  Amon-Ra St. Brown  was on display as St. Brown scored a touchdown in Friday's scrimmage off a slant at the goal line through tight coverage. St. Brown had a two-point conversion while also converting multiple fourth downs on a monster day in which his playmaking was consistently on display. WRs coach Scottie Montgomery credits Goff and St. Brown's friendship as the driving force of their on-field chemistry.

 "These guys, their timing is correct, but their off-the-field relationship also gives us an opportunity that a lot of people don't have," Montgomery said. "The communication between the two of them is probably what makes them as consistent as they are. There's certain things and there's nonverbal communication that happened between them now because of where we are in the offense, where they are in their relationship away from the building."

 More observations: 

 
 After signing a record three-year extension on Thursday, RB Jahmyr Gibbs was on the field and in uniform for the second straight day of practice but didn't participate in full team drills. "This process has been extremely stressful. I just wanted to play ball," Gibbs said. "I missed being out there with my teammates and coaches and it's just fun being out there now with my pads and stuff on. It just feels a lot better." 
 Detroit rapper Sada Baby and popular comedian Haha Davis were both in attendance for Friday's practice, sharing their excitement for the upcoming season while mingling with fans. "When you go 15-2 and reach the NFC Championship, at some point it has to go down and this is the year," Haha Davis said. "I really believe that." 
 The Lions are signing veteran DT Ben Stille to a one-year deal, per ESPN's Adam Schefter. 
 Detroit has waived injured CB  De'Shawn Rucker .﻿ 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 The Lions held a 2 ½-hour practice session in humid conditions. All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell wasn't pleased with the performance of the defense during red-zone drills and was brutally honest in his assessment. He also took accountability for his "fair share of mess ups" as they're looking to improve to reach their standard ahead of Week 1.

 "Not very good. I'll be completely honest with you," Campbell said. "What caused it? I feel like there's obviously communication and technique. It's really simple. Like football is simple, but it's hard to do. It's easy to talk about and hard to do."

 Campbell feels they will continue to get better.

 More conversation:  

 
 Running back  Jahmyr Gibbs returned to practice, taking part in the walkthrough portion and stretches for the first time all training camp, before working on the side with a team trainer. However, he didn't participate in any individual drills during the session as he seeks a new deal. A crowd of media members swarmed Gibbs as he strolled off the practice field to enter the locker room after signing autographs, but he carefully avoided reporters and flashed a thumbs-up sign to the group after being asked if he was close to reaching a contract extension soon. 
 CB De'Shawn Rucker (ankle) and DT Mekhi Wingo (groin) left practice early to be evaluated for potential injuries. Several other players were limited due to cramping from the heat on a humid day. 
 The Lions placed TE Miles Kitselman on reserve/injured and signed WR Tarik Black . 
 

 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Tuesday marked Day 2 of padded practices and veteran LB Devin White continued to get acclimated to the defense alongside guys like All-Pro Jack Campbell . White was signed as a free agent on Aug. 1 to add depth after rookie linebacker  Jimmy Rolder went down with a hamstring injury earlier in camp. He has received limited reps in practices so far but has been doing additional conditioning drills on the side with trainers to keep in shape. "Right now, they've got a plan for me…

title: 2026 Green Bay Packers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Packers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Green Bay Packers ' camp is taking place in Green Bay, Wisconsin, and Packers reporter Rob Demovsky has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Packers camp. We will update this file often. Will the revamped WR corps help QB Jordan Love and the offense take another step? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive into all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Thursday.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news out of Packers camp 
 
 Micah Parsons: Playing vs. Cowboys in Week 6 'realistic' 
 Packers RT changes last name to Bako-Bewele to honor heritage 
 Packers star TE Tucker Kraft activated off PUP after ACL recovery 
 Better, worse or the same: Packers defense 
 Packers CEO: Team needs financial bump to stay competitive 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 

 It was the kind of practice that would have excited a young, backup quarterback.

 But what about a 37-year-old going into his 16th NFL season?

 
"Oh yeah, the game still excites me," Tyrod Taylor said.

 
In what was perhaps Taylor's best practice since he signed with the Packers this offseason, he completed passes of all varieties. There was a deep post to Kisean Johnson . A quick-hitting slant to Will Sheppard for a first down. A 20-yarder to Sheppard down the left sideline. A big gain over the middle to J. Michael Sturdivant .

 
It didn't matter to Taylor that it was all with backup receivers -- many of whom might not make the team.

 
"There's a healthy rotation of guys that's going in and out with the group that I'm running with, and it's just up to me to communicate, get them in the right position but also give them a chance to make plays," Taylor said. "We've got a ton of playmakers at our skill positions."

 
The Packers had one of the best backup quarterbacks in the NFL last season with Malik Willis , who signed with the Dolphins as a free agent. Now, they have one of the most experienced.

 "I'm a firm believer that your actions speak louder than your words, especially early on," said Taylor, who has played in 100 career games (with 62 starts) for seven teams. "It's about me coming in, being myself, preparing on the field, off the field, being ready for the opportunities and taking advantage of them as well, and then gradually growing into more of a vocal leader and speaking on things when they fit."

 Other observations: 

 
 As if it weren't unusual enough to see cornerback Keisean Nixon with the second-string defense Sunday, it was even more surprising to see him taking snaps with the third-stringers Monday. In the very next period, he was back with the No. 1 defense, but it's a baffling way to handle a player who last season was considered the team's No. 1 cornerback. When Nixon wasn't with the starters, Benjamin St-Juste was in his spot along with rookie Brandon Cisse on the other side. Could it be a sign the Packers are thinking about demoting Nixon? "There's always competition," coach Matt LaFleur said. "All these guys got to be prepared for that. As far as the substitution, that's not something that I'm always micromanaging. A lot of that's on the position coach." 
 Though starting linebackers Edgerrin Cooper (foot) and Zaire Franklin (rest) returned to practice, the offense was still without two of its top receivers, Matthew Golden (toe) and Jayden Reed (ankle). Without running back Josh Jacobs (groin) and with tight end  Tucker Kraft (knee) not yet doing 11-on-11 periods, the primary skill position players with the No. 1 offense were MarShawn Lloyd at running back; Christian Watson , Bo Melton , Skyy Moore , Savion Williams and Isaiah Neyor at receiver; and  Messiah Swinson and Drake Dabney at tight end. 
 Add safety Javon Bullard to the injury list. He had a walking boot on his right foot during practice but said afterward that the issue was just a bruise that won't impact his availability for the start of the season. Kitan Oladapo played in Bullard's usual spot in the slot in the nickel package. 
 Two of the biggest plays of the day came from players fighting to make the roster. Cornerback Jaylin Simpson ended practice with a goal-line interception off undrafted rookie quarterback Kyron Drones . Meanwhile, Melton came down with a true 50-50 ball on a deep throw from Jordan Love . It looked like Nixon might have been in position to break it up or even intercept it before Melton came back for the ball and snagged it. "I just wanted it to be like a 80/20 or 100/0," Melton said. "My ball or nobody's." 
 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 9 
 If the Packers were looking for someone to emerge behind their top three receivers, then perhaps Sunday's practice will help.

 
With Matthew Golden (toe) and Jayden Reed (ankle) out, Christian Watson was the only available starting receiver.

 
Enter Savion Williams , the second-year receiver who had just 10 catches for 78 yards and a touchdown in limited opportunities as a rookie. In fact, last season Williams had more rushes (11) on jet sweeps and end arounds than he did receptions.

 
Williams got things rolling Sunday when he caught a 60-yard bomb from third-string quarterback Kyle McCord early in practice. Williams took advantage of having linebacker  Kristian Welch  on him in coverage. But Williams didn't just show his skills with and against the backups.

 
He caught four more passes -- all from starting quarterback Jordan Love  -- including another touchdown in the red zone and two more catches for first downs.

 
"His measurables are off the charts in terms of his size, speed and strength," coach Matt LaFleur said recently. "And then he's just a young player that's still learning and he's got a long way to go, but I think he's showcased a lot of great traits, and that's why we drafted him and that's why we loved him coming out."

 
Williams, a third-round pick, is in competition with the likes of Bo Melton , Skyy Moore , Isaiah Neyor and J. Michael Sturdivant for the backup receiver spots.

 Other observations: 

 
 Zach Bako-Bewele 's return to team drills for the first time since last season's knee injury might have cleared up the right guard situation. Instead of Anthony Belton going back to right guard, where he was a starter last season, the Packers instead went with Jacob Monk . Belton took mostly backup snaps at right tackle. Jager Burton took left guard snaps with Aaron Banks (knee) still limited to individual drills. 
 For the first time in camp, cornerback Keisean Nixon took reps with the No. 2 defense. It might not have been a full-fledged demotion because Nixon still got some first-team reps, but there were periods in which Brandon Cisse and Benjamin St-Juste were at the corners with the starting defense. 
 Defensive tackle Devonte Wyatt (ankle/leg) took 11-on-11 snaps for the first time in camp. Previously, he had done only individual drills. 
 Defensive tackle Javon Hargrave (knee) and running back Chris Brooks (hamstring) were activated off PUP and NFI, respectively, and did individual drills. Hargrave said his knee issue was something that lingered from the offseason program, while Brooks said his injury happened during the break between minicamp in June and the start of training camp. 
 Rookie Trey Smack went 2-for-3 on field goals, missing from 48 yards off the right upright. He's now 16-of-23 in camp.
