title: Do NFL superteams usually win the Super Bowl? Will the Rams?
summary: The Rams are loaded this season, and basically everyone is picking them to win the Super Bowl. But preseason darlings of the past 35 years haven't always met expectations.
full_text:
The 2026 Rams are the closest thing we've had to a preseason superteam in several years. Sean McVay's group was already a popular pick to win Super Bowl LXI before the offseason began. But then L.A. traded for Trent McDuffie and signed Jaylen Watson , shoring up the secondary at the expense of a potential Super Bowl opponent in the Chiefs. The move to draft Ty Simpson as Matthew Stafford 's successor struck a curious tone, but general manager Les Snead responded with the mother of all high-stakes moves, trading Jared Verse and three picks to the Browns for reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett .

 Unsurprisingly, the Rams have become prohibitive favorites to win the Super Bowl after their aggressive moves this offseason. Picking any other team to win the Lombardi Trophy at this point would almost require coming up with some sort of explanation for what happened to the Rams along the way.

 And yet, we have to look back only one year to remind ourselves how NFL seasons can play out entirely differently once players get on the field. In 2025, 68 ESPN personalities picked  their AFC and NFC champions, along with an eventual Super Bowl winner, before the season kicked off. Not a single person picked the Seahawks or Patriots. I predicted the  Chiefs and Packers , who combined for exactly zero playoff wins. Preseason darlings like the Chiefs, Lions and Commanders each missed the playoffs altogether.

 Was 2025 just a weird year? And how often do heavily favorited superteams such as the 2026 Rams actually win the Super Bowl? I decided to take a more comprehensive look through history to get a sense of how confident we can be that Los Angeles will be the last team standing come Feb. 14 .

 
 Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show' 

 
 To do so, I'm going to look at the 15 largest preseason favorites since 1990 and see how their seasons played out. I'll be using the preseason odds compiled at Pro Football Reference from 1990 to 2025 and compare them with the odds posted for this season's Super Bowl at  DraftKings . The Rams have odds of +550 at DraftKings to win the Super Bowl, while nobody else in the league is shorter than +1000. After we adjust for the vigorish and convert the betting lines into probabilities, the Rams have an implied 12.5% chance of winning this season's Super Bowl, putting them 5.1 percentage points ahead of the second-placed Bills and Ravens.

 While the absolute number might be a better sense of how the market views a particular team, I'm going to use the latter figure to sort through our top 15 teams (well, 16, if we're including the 2026 Rams). There were plenty of seasons in the 1990s where two or three superteams -- such as the 49ers and Cowboys -- were seen as significantly better than the rest of the competition. I want to get a sense of what it was like for the teams that truly separated from the pack before the season began, as appears to be the case for this Rams squad.

 Did those teams hold up to their preseason expectations? Was the market overconfident about their chances? Let's go team by team before using the lessons from those 15 earlier cases to talk about what it means for the 2026 Rams and their chances of winning McVay and Stafford their second title.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 2026 Rams | 2021 Chiefs | 2019 Patriots 
 2018 Patriots | 2017 Patriots | 2009 Patriots 
 2008 Patriots | 2007 Patriots | 2002 Rams 
 2001 Rams | 1998 Packers | 1997 Packers 
 1996 49ers | 1995 49ers | 1994 49ers | 1990 49ers 
 Can this season's Rams win the Super Bowl? 

 
 

 

 2017 New England Patriots 
 Implied odds: 19.8% 
 Gap to the rest of the NFL: 11.5% 
 Result: Lost Super Bowl LII to the Eagles, 41-33 

 I wouldn't have guessed that the 2017 Patriots stood out in terms of Super Bowl odds more than any other New England team from the Tom Brady-Bill Belichick era, but let's contextualize this. The Pats were coming off that legendary 34-28 win over the Falcons in Super Bowl LI . Brady was getting Rob Gronkowski back from injury after the star tight end missed the playoff run with a back ailment , while Belichick added a new star receiver to the mix in Brandin Cooks . After a 14-2 season and with Brady motivated by the four-game suspension he took for the Deflategate scandal, you could understand why the Patriots were heavy favorites to repeat as champs.

 

 Some things went as expected. Brady won the league MVP award. Cooks and Gronkowski each topped 1,000 yards. The Pats went 13-3 and took home the top seed in the AFC.

 Others did not. Belichick's team started 2-2 and needed a last-minute comeback win over a 4-12 Texans team to avoid opening the season 1-3. The Pats righted the ship quickly, but they were trailing by 10 points in the fourth quarter of the AFC title game and were down nearly three scores to the Jaguars, only for Myles Jack 's fumble recovery touchdown to be overturned. Two late touchdown passes to Danny Amendola controversially pushed the Pats into the Super Bowl.

 There, well, nothing went as planned. The Patriots defense had quietly been a mess all year, finishing the regular season ranked 31st in DVOA. The offense covered up the weakness by holding on to the ball and getting out to early leads. The Eagles were heavy underdogs with backup quarterback Nick Foles in for the injured Carson Wentz , and you know what happened next. Brady threw for 505 yards and three touchdowns, still the record for an NFL quarterback in a losing effort, but the defense couldn't stop Foles & Co. The Pats fell 41-33.

 

 
 

 2007 New England Patriots 
 Implied odds: 20.9% 
 Gap to the rest of the NFL:  10.5% 
 Result: Lost Super Bowl XLII to the Giants, 17-14 

 Are you sensing a trend? This was another Patriots team that rode offseason optimism about its offensive additions to high hopes before falling short in the Super Bowl. The 2006 Pats had blown a 21-3 lead to the Colts in the AFC Championship Game , but they also weren't far removed from winning three titles between 2001 and 2004. Brady had improved as a quarterback over that time, and during the offseason, Belichick had rebuilt the offense by trading for Randy Moss and Wes Welker and signing Donte' Stallworth.

 What happened next is one of the more notable seasons in NFL history. The Pats were caught spying on the Jets during a 38-14 blowout victory in Week 1, turning a team that had been the underdog favorites during their win over the Rams in 2001 into the villains of the NFL. On the field, the Patriots blew defenses away with their spread attack, as Brady produced arguably the greatest season in league history under center. The Patriots went 16-0 in the regular season, winning their average game by nearly 20 points.

 By the time the postseason came around, though, the cracks were beginning to show. Brady threw three picks in the AFC title game , but with Philip Rivers playing through a torn ACL and LaDainian Tomlinson limited by injury to three touches, the Chargers couldn't take advantage in a 21-12 defeat. And in the Super Bowl, again as heavy favorites, the Patriots were upset by a Giants team that was able to control Brady in the pocket with its pass rush.

 

 

 
 

 1996 San Francisco 49ers 
 Implied odds: 19.2% 
 Gap to the rest of the NFL:  9.6% 
 Result: Lost in divisional round to the Packers, 35-14 

 The 49ers were the preseason favorites to win the Super Bowl in 1994, 1995 and 1996. Their status as the third team on this list might have more to do with a lack of competition in the AFC than anything else. The Bills were among the Super Bowl favorites earlier in the decade, but after a 7-9 season in 1994 and a 10-6 campaign in 1995, they had fallen back to the pack. The Steelers had advanced to the Super Bowl the prior season, but starting quarterback Neil O'Donnell had signed with the Jets in free agency, turning things over to 34-year-old Mike Tomczak as the team's starter. And while the Chiefs were coming off a 13-win season, they had relied on a…

title: 2026 Houston Texans training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Houston Texans training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Houston Texans ' camp is taking place in Houston at at NRG Park., and Texans reporter D.J. Bien-Aime has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Texans camp 
 
 Tank Dell returns to practice for first time since 2024 
 Houston bringing back former No. 1 pick Clowney 
 Texans have 'productive' contract talks with Stroud 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 

 For the Texans' first preseason game against the Los Angeles Chargers  on Thursday, coach DeMeco Ryans said, "We'll have a select group of guys who will not go out there and play."

 So don't expect the key starters to play much. Anticipate seeing only rookie starters, such as center Keylan Rutledge , and a few second-year players, such as wideout Jayden Higgins  and left tackle Aireontae Ersery .

 The preseason opener will be about early impressions from younger players and seeing where they are with depth. It'll be about seeing the guys they'll have to make decisions on to fill out the back end of the roster with limited spots among the starters being unsettled.

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 
 The Texans held a night practice on Saturday. It was not pretty for the Texans offense as quarterback C.J. Stroud had many incompletions and the run game had little running room.

 However, the defense displayed the potential of a top-three unit in the NFL. There were plenty of sacks, an interception from Pro Bowl safety  Calen Bullock  and pass break ups. But most importantly, they're not satisfied. Texans defensive coordinator Matt Burke's assessment of the defense was "okay."

 Burke said Houston is chasing perfection defensively.

 

 
 Friday, Aug. 7 

 After an off day, the Texans dialed back their intensity as they went through drills without pads, but notably, wide receiver  Tank Dell practiced for the second straight day of training camp, albeit in a limited capacity.

 It's another step in Dell's recovery, with Wednesday being his first time practicing since he suffered multiple torn ligaments and a dislocated kneecap in Week 16 of 2024.

 Speaking to the media for the first time, Dell said he had no fear in the strength of his knee, pointing towards Houston's doctor stating his knee is "100 percent stable." 

 "Trusting the work you put in prior to going out there," said Dell when asked about trusting in his health. "Going out there to put your foot in the ground, trusting the process with the training staff and what they had set out for me. So when I got out here, I wasn't scared."﻿

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 Wideout Tank Dell made his return to the practice field, participating in limited capacity. It marked the first time he engaged in any sort of team padded practice since Week 16 of 2024 after the 2023 third-round pick suffered multiple torn ligaments and a dislocated kneecap against the Chiefs.

 He caught a few passes from quarterback C.J. Stroud during individual drills and ran full speed routes.

 Dell didn't do much more after that, but this is the step in the right direction. Coach DeMeco Ryans won't rush Dell back and said "Tank is on the right plan." The goal is have him ready for team 11-on-11 contact reps. He still has a ways to go, but this is positive progress.

 Other observation:  

 Wideout Jayden Higgins continue to flash throughout practice. He made another impressive catch with Derek Stingley Jr . in coverage. It was a tightly contested catch but that's always a positive because it's against an All-Pro corner.

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 Texans wideout Jayden Higgins is starting to blossom as he's entering Year 2. When Pro Bowl wideout Nico Collins  was asked about Higgins' progression he said "He's hooping right now, and I can't wait to see him rock out when it really matters."

 During Tuesday's practice, Higgins made multiple catches with All-Pro cornerback  Derek Stingley Jr . in coverage. One of those receptions occurred during a team third-down period for a 20-yard gain. The other one was during 1-on-1s -- where Stingley tried to aggressively jam Higgins, but he avoided the powerful jab and broke free for an easy toss from quarterback C.J. Stroud .

 Early in camp, Stroud said he expected Higgins to have a "dominant" Year 2, and so far we are starting to see it.

 Other observation:  

 Linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair was slow to get up after a collision with tight end Dalton Schultz . Al-Shaair was fine shortly after.

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 

 This was Day 1 of padded practices, and the defense shined. Quarterback C.J. Stroud  was forced to hold the ball longer than he would like as the secondary coverage was stout.

 Stroud occasionally scrambled more than usual to buy time to make throws and the defensive line forced a few sacks. Safety Calen Bullock intercepted Stroud.

 Also coach DeMeco Ryans used exotic blitzes throughout the day, and the offense sometimes had answers and other times didn't. Ryans deemed the first day in full pads as "successful." 

 Other observation: 

 First-round pick Keylan Rutledge is adding an extra juice of aggression to the unit. He got into a mini tussle with defensive end Danielle Hunter after a successful run play by running back Woody Marks .

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Saturday's padless practice featured more back and forth from the offense and defense. Some periods the defense dominated and others, the offense was able to counter their blitzing.

 The Texans start padded practices on Monday and that will be a "big part" of the evaluation process for the team according to coach DeMeco Ryans.

 The fourth-year head coach said: "There's a lot of all-stars in shorts," and later added the staff wouldn't be fooled by what players have done without pads.

 Another observation: 

 
 Cornerback Derek Stingley Jr collided with linebacker Henry To'oTo'o and was slow to get up, but he shook it off and was back on the field. 
 

 

 Friday, July 31 
 It was mainly walk-throughs for the Texans. It's a theme that's been consistent for coach DeMeco Ryans throughout the offseason -- where he has focused on helping his team mentally work toward executing deep in the playoffs.

 "I've grown as a head coach," Ryans said in June. "For me, it's more so now about how much smarter can we play as a team. How can we be more elite on our execution? Our communication, can it be louder? Can we echo it more? Can we truly be tied together every time we line up? That's what I've seen when I talk about the process of us this year being better."

 Saturday's practice will be the first day with fans in attendance since training camp has opened. That will be a longer practice with more intensity compared to today's practice that was roughly a little over an hour.

 

 

 Thursday, July 30 
 The passing attack was centered around the quick game time to throw on Day 2 of practice. Quarterback C.J. Stroud was quick and decisive with his throws with all but one of his throws being made under 2.8 seconds, and his only rep over three seconds was when he extended the play and tried to find wideout Jayden Higgins in the back of the end zone.

 It fell incomplete, but the majority of his throws came with precision and decisiveness. Stroud was able to connect a few times with Higgins, who's development in Year 2 will be huge for the offense.

title: How Jaguars WR Brian Thomas Jr. prepared to be better in 2026
summary: Thomas has worked intentionally to improve his hands for 2026, and as Liam Coen said, "It elevates everybody's game when BT is playing at his highest level."
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Jacksonville Jaguars receiver  Brian Thomas Jr . stands in front of a JUGS machine after every practice with his hands inches away from it and his thumbs and pointer fingers forming a triangle. The setting on the machine is usually between 2 and 3 -- for reference, when it's used to simulate a punt it's set on 6. Each football rockets out between the two spinning wheels and slams into his hands over and over.

 And Thomas has caught them nearly every time.

 Over the offseason, strengthening his hands was a main goal. The JUGS routine is one of the things the third-year receiver is doing to bounce back from a disappointing 2025 season that saw him catch eight fewer touchdowns than the year before.

 "In the spring, very early on, honestly, you could sense that he had really looked at things in areas in which he thought he could improve upon, and he was attacking those areas," head coach Liam Coen said. "I thought he was extremely intentional about the things he wanted to improve on."

 Coaches and teammates noticed a difference this spring and it has carried over into training camp.

 "When you put the work in and just be super intentional about little things like that, you'll definitely see the work paying off," Thomas said. "I feel much stronger at the catch point. I'm able to go and do a lot more things. I really just feel stronger in general."

 As a result, there's optimism that Thomas is headed for the kind of big season he had as a rookie when he ranked third in the league with 1,282 receiving yards.

 "He's playing confident right now," Coen said.

 

 After making the Pro Bowl as a rookie in 2024, his second season was filled with drops -- five in the first seven games -- and injuries to his left ankle and shoulder that cost him four games. There was also a nagging left wrist injury that started in Week 1 and lingered throughout the season.

 At one point the Jaguars moved rookie Travis Hunter ahead of Thomas as WR1, but a knee injury ended Hunter's season after seven games. The team then traded for Jakobi Meyers in early November, and by the end of the season Parker Washington had become  Trevor Lawrence 's No. 1 target.

 Thomas finished 2026 with 48 catches for 707 yards and two touchdowns -- and the determination to have his best offseason.

 "I knew I had to be super intentional about everything I did, whether it's just staying focused, staying locked in on catching the ball, staying locked in to the catch point," he said. "Getting my body right, to come in and be the best I can be, being [in] the best shape I could be. Just little things. My whole offseason was about just fixing all the little things ... that I know I can clean up."

 Thomas put together a workout plan, focused on his nutrition and emphasized improving his hand-eye connection in catching the football. Part of that was actually strengthening his hands by using the JUGS machine as well as jamming his hands into a bucket of sand and moving them around. He also caught tennis balls to improve his focus and worked on making sure he watched the ball all the way from the throw until he tucked it. And he never deviated from his plan.

 "It's basically just growing up," Thomas said. "I was young. Coming in, I just had to learn. Really, everybody's got to learn. Coming in and learning, seeing the things that vets do, learning how to take care of your body, what works for you, what doesn't work for you."

 When he got back around his teammates, they noticed.

 

 "He's having a great camp so far," Meyers said. "And it's just built off the spring. He had one of the better springs that I've seen of a younger guy since I've been in the league (eight years), but if he's just doing half of what he's doing now [during the season], I think he would be in a good spot."

 Receivers coach Edgar Bennett was also impressed.

 "It all starts with the mindset [and] he came in with the right mindset," Bennett said. "He knew these are the areas that I want to improve on. And I mean, he literally takes a day-by-day approach. Every single day we're improving at something.

 "You see BT now loving the process. And [Coen] talks about it all the time, the process, loving the process. And you see a guy loving it."

 Thomas said this is the best he has felt mentally and physically going into a season. His confidence is sky high, too. That's evident by what he has done in practice, Coen said, and the rest of the offense is feeding off it.

 "I think it brings everybody up," he said. "It elevates everybody's game when BT is playing at his highest level."

title: 2026 Kansas City Chiefs training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Chiefs training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Kansas City Chiefs ' camp is taking place at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, Missouri, and Chiefs reporter Nate Taylor has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Chiefs camp. We will update this file often. Can coach Andy Reid get the Chiefs back into the playoffs? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive into all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Chiefs camp 
 
 OC Eric Bieniemy returns to Chiefs after shooting of wife 
 Reid: Mahomes unlikely to play in preseason opener 
 Rookie wideout Cyrus Allen an early star of Chiefs training camp 
 Chiefs' Reid: Eric Bieniemy's wife out of ICU, 'doing great' 
 As training camp opens, Chiefs point to brighter future in 2026 
 
 
 
 

 
 Monday, Aug. 10 
 With just seven practices left in training camp, Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes appears to be close to having his full complement of receivers on the field. For the first time in camp, Monday's on-field work featured Mahomes' top four receivers -- Rashee Rice , Xavier Worthy , Tyquan Thornton and rookie Cyrus Allen .

 Worthy, who missed last week's practices with a sprained right shoulder, was the lone receiver who didn't participate in the 7-on-7 and 11-on-11 reps. He could be a full participant later this week ahead of the preseason opener Saturday against the Los Angeles Rams .

 In the 7-on-7 period inside the red zone, Allen showed his ability to improvise in the middle of one play to get behind linebacker Nick Bolton for an 11-yard touchdown. A few minutes later, Rice caught a 6-yard touchdown pass in the back of the end zone against tight coverage from Nohl Williams .

 Mahomes had several reps with his top three receivers being Rice, Thornton and Allen alongside tight end Travis Kelce and running back  Kenneth Walker III .

 More observations: 

 
 The players who missed practice were right guard Trey Smith (hip), cornerback  L'Jarius Sneed  (rest), linebacker Drue Tranquill (lower-back spasms) and defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (right knee). 
 For the first time in camp, rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane was in pads and cleared to participate in 7-on-7 periods, although he was still wearing a noncontact yellow jersey for the shoulder injury he sustained in May that forced him to miss the mandatory minicamp in June. In Monday's practice, Delane had two quality reps, where he covered Kelce and the other against Thornton inside the red zone. "He did a nice job with that," Reid said of Delane. 
 For the third straight practice, Kahlil Benson , the undrafted rookie from Indiana, had his reps at right guard in place of Smith. Jaylon Moore , the five-year veteran, played at right tackle with the first-team offense. "I think it's good for him to have some flexibility to do both [positions]," Reid said of Benson, who began camp at right tackle. "We worked him a little bit in there in OTAs and liked what we saw. This gives him real competition in there now where [defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo] is throwing a lot of different things at you, so you have to be able to adjust. It'll do nothing but help him, even at the tackle spot once he jumps back there." 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 
 More than halfway through camp, the Chiefs finally had a practice where multiple players had physical altercations. Coach Andy Reid doesn't want his players to fight, but he designs the Chiefs' camp to push the players, both physically and mentally.

 This was the sixth consecutive practice before an off day Sunday. After an 11-on-11 repetition, defensive end  Felix Anudike-Uzomah  and left guard Kingsley Suamataia , who kept engaging him after the play was over, got into it. Suamataia even threw a punch with his right hand while several teammates were trying to separate him and Anudike-Uzomah.

 "It's kind of unusual, and we haven't done that in the past," special teams coordinator Dave Toub said of the Chiefs' six straight practices. "It was a little bit of a grinder. It was chippy. That's how you know. It's hot and that's football sometimes."

 Toward the end of practice, the first-team offense was in the middle of the long-drive drill -- a period in which the projected starters had 16 consecutive repetitions -- when running back Kenneth Walker III became frustrated with safety Alohi Gilman . Walker felt Gilman hit more than was necessary when he had the ball near the sideline. After the repetition, Gilman put his face mask directly in front of Walker's. When Gilman shoved his teammate, Walker threw the ball at him and tackled him, which forced multiple teammates to separate them.

 "Going against the same guys and just being competitive, I think that's what's been great about this camp," quarterback Patrick Mahomes said. "It's super competitive on both sides, so little scuffles here and there but nothing crazy. As long as we keep it like that and keep competing, that's where you get the best team you can get."

 Other observations: 

 
 The players who missed practice were right guard Trey Smith (hip), cornerback  L'Jarius Sneed  (rest), linebacker Drue Tranquill (lower back spasms), defensive end Ashton Gillotte (strained right hamstring), defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (right knee) and receiver Xavier Worthy (sprained right shoulder). 
 For the second consecutive practice, Kahlil Benson , the undrafted rookie from Indiana, had his repetitions at right tackle in place of Smith. Jaylon Moore , the five-year veteran, played at right tackle with the first-team offense. 
 Rookie receiver Cyrus Allen , who missed four practices with a left shin injury, participated in the 7-on-7 periods but was held out of 11-on-11 repetitions. Rashee Rice , the Chiefs' No. 1 receiver, participated only in the individual period and left the field early to receive more treatment on his right knee, the same knee he had surgery on in May to remove loose debris that was causing inflammation. 
 Toub revealed Saturday that his top kickoff returners are receiver Nikko Remigio and running back Brashard Smith . "Brashard has taken a really nice step as far as a punt returner," Toub said. "He's catching the ball a lot cleaner. Nikko just keeps getting better. [Allen] was doing a good job up until he got hurt. Now he's back out there catching again, so we've got to continue to develop him." 
 
 

 

 

 Friday, Aug. 7 

 One player who is having a steady camp for the Chiefs is defensive end Felix Anudike-Uzomah , the team's 2023 first-round pick. For most of this week, Anudike-Uzomah has had his reps with the first-team defense, a result of him replacing Ashton Gillotte , who sustained a strained right hamstring in Monday's practice. Rushing from the left side, Anudike-Uzomah has had several strong 11-on-11 reps in which he has won the one-on-one battle with right tackle Kahlil Benson , an undrafted rookie out of Indiana.

 "His get-off is what jumps out to me," Reid said of Anudike-Uzomah. "He's bringing power with it. It's one thing to run around people, but there's a point, as a defensive end, you've got to physically blow things up a little bit. He's worked hard at that."

 Almost a year ago, the Chiefs had to place Anudike-Uzomah on season-ending injured reserve because of a strained right hamstring he sustained in the preseason -- an injury that required surgery. The Chiefs are hopeful that he can be a reliable contributor in the final year of his rookie contract.

title: 2026 Los Angeles Chargers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Chargers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Los Angeles Chargers camp is taking place at The Bolt in El Segundo, California, and Chargers reporter Kris Rhim has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Chargers camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 
 Latest from Chargers camp 
 
 Players with the most at stake during Chargers' training camp 
 Tracking 2026 NFL hold-ins: Tuipulotu 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 

 Left tackle Rashawn Slater and cornerback Tarheeb Still missed practice for the third straight day. Coach Jim Harbaugh originally said Slater's absence two days ago was part of a veteran rest day, but his continued absence suggests there may be more to it. The Chargers have not provided a reason for Still's absence.

 In Slater's absence, Branson Taylor and  Trey Pipkins III  have played left tackle, and Cam Hart has taken the bulk of snaps at outside in place of Still. Before, Still and Hart rotated with the first group.

 Other observations: 

 
 Jake Slaughter and Kayode Awosika rotated at left guard, offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel said "no one's eliminated themselves from the tournament." 
 McDaniel ran across the field yelling, "Great job,  Joe Alt " during practice Monday after Alt blocked outside linebacker Khalil Mack on a screen, something the Chargers have struggled to do throughout camp. McDaniel said Alt has "exceeded my expectations that were pretty high coming in" and called him an "over-the-top pleasant surprise." 
 McDaniel said he'll use running backs Omarion Hampton , Kimani Vidal and Keaton Mitchell in probably every game this season, with the workload depending on the opponent and "hot hand." 
 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 9 

 During the first 11v11 period of Sunday's practice, the crowd roared for a Quentin Johnston reception that quarterback Justin Herbert perfectly placed by the outstretched arms of cornerback Nikko Reed .

 But had this not been training camp, Herbert likely would've been on his back or running for life before that ball had the chance to be released. Outside linebacker Tuli Tuipulotu -- rushing from the interior on a front that featured Justin Eboigbe , Akheem Mesidor and Khalil Mack -- put a swift spin move on center Tyler Biadasz and was in Herbert's lap as the play was beginning. This sequence was a microcosm of Sunday's practice, as the defensive line controlled the day, constantly putting pressure on quarterbacks and stopping running plays before they could begin.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Branson Taylor , Kayode Awosika and Jake Slaughter rotated at left guard throughout practice. 
 Cornerback Tarheeb Still and left tackle Rashawn Slater both missed practice for a second straight day. Trey Pipkins and Taylor played left tackle in his absence. 
 Tre' Harris was active throughout practice with several receptions. 
 Avery Smith blew up a running play on a blitz, drawing celebrations from the defense. 
 Junior Colson pressured DJ Uiagalelei into a throw that landed in the hands of cornerback Isas Waxter , but Waxter dropped the interception. 
 Kyle Kennard had perhaps his best practice of camp, with several impressive wins in one-on-ones and pressures during 11-on-11 periods. 
 Trevor Penning had a good day, holding up well in one-on-ones and during team periods while working with the second and third groups. 
 Mesidor had one of the most impressive one-on-one wins of practice, beating Joe Alt cleanly with a spin move. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 
 

 Rookie left guard Jake Slaughter got his first reps with the group blocking for Justin Herbert in a padded practice this training camp. The Chargers drafted Slaughter -- who played only center in college -- to be the team's starter at left guard, but he seemed to fall out of favor through camp as veteran Kayode Awosika and second-year lineman Branson Taylor emerged.

 Slaughter fared well in his reps at guard, showing a firm anchor when pressured from defensive tackles and the ability to pick up defensive stunts. His best moment came on a pancake block of defensive tackle Dalvin Tomlinson , but he was also beaten badly on a rep by defensive tackle Justin Eboigbe .

 Other observations: 

 
 Offensve lineman Trevor Penning appears to be falling back in the competition for the starting left guard job. He continues to work largely with the group, blocking for DJ Uiagalelei , though that could still change. 
 Rookie wide receiver Brenen Thompson made an impressive toe-tap catch down the left sideline that drew a roar from the crowd. 
 Outside linebacker Khalil Mack was explosive throughout practice and had several would-be sacks. Tuli Tuipulotu and Nadame Tucker were also consistently disruptive off the edge. 
 Defensive tackles Jamaree Caldwell , Teair Tart and Eboigbe continued to disrupt the run game and generate pressure on the quarterback. 
 Uiagalelei, may have had the throw of the day, a 50 or so yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Derius Davis . 
 Herbert continues to be sharp and on target with his receivers. It appears he -- and the other quarterbacks -- has grown comfortable with the timing of McDaniel's offense. Receivers are getting passes early and in space. 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 The Chargers' five-man race for guard continued Thursday with a new twist, as second-year lineman Branson Taylor took all the reps with quarterback Justin Herbert 's group at left guard. Before Thursday, two players had rotated at left guard, but Taylor got all of the reps with the first group in the team's first true padded practice.

 Taylor, a sixth-round pick in last year's draft who didn't make the 2025 53-man roster, was mainly a practice squad player last season. One year later, it seems that he has impressed the staff enough to have a legitimate shot at starting. On Thursday, Taylor fared well, creating running lanes and protecting Herbert throughout, a much-improved version of the player at camp last year.

 Coach Jim Harbaugh said on Wednesday that veteran Kayode Awosika was leading the race to start, and that Taylor, Pipkins, Trevor Penning and rookie Jake Slaughter were in the mix.

 Other observations:  

 
 OLB  Tuli Tuipulotu participated in team drills during Wednesday's padded practice, his second day in a row after not participating in team drills for the first six days of training camp. Harbaugh originally said that Tuipulotu's absence was being "handled internally," then later said it was a "ramp up." Neither Tuipulotu, his representatives, or the Chargers have acknowledged a contract-related absence, but his return to the field signals that whatever matter was being handled internally is resolved. 
 Rookie S  Genesis Smith intercepted Justin Herbert after a pass went through Charlie Kolar's hands. 
 CB  Donte Jackson had an impressive diving pass breakup on a pass by QB  Trey Lance during 7-on-7 that led to an interception by safety Elijah Molden . 
 DT  Justin Eboigbe continued his strong camp, consistently generating interior pressure 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 Outside linebacker Tuli Tuipulotu , who has been a limited participant in practice this training camp amid ongoing contract negotiations, was a full participant in Wednesday's practice. The caveat is that the practice was a walkthrough, so Tuipulotu and the other Chargers players were going at half speed. He still has yet to participate in a non-walkthrough practice 11-on-11 period, but his participation on Wednesday could be a sign…

title: 2026 Los Angeles Rams training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Rams training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Los Angeles Rams  camp is taking place at Loyola Marymount University in L.A. Rams reporter Sarah Barshop has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Rams camp. We will update this file often. Can the Rams live up to the hype? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Rams camp 
 
 Sean McVay praises Aaron Donald as Rams await DT's decision 
 Myles Garrett out third straight day with soreness 
 Puka Nacua says it 'never crossed my mind' to not take part in camp 
 Rams unveil two new alternate uniforms for 2026 
 
 
 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 Tuesday will mark the first joint practice of training camp for the Rams, as they will host the Dallas Cowboys at their Woodland Hills facility. Because head coach Sean McVay does not play his starters or key backups during the preseason, he especially values the chance to get his starters in these competitive, but more controlled environments.

 McVay said he tries to schedule at least two joint practices during the preseason; the Rams will host the New Orleans Saints for a joint practice on Aug. 20.

 The Rams don't gameplan for the practice, but McVay said he's looking forward to "the competition" of going against a different team than his players see practicing against each other.

 "I think when you go against each other as much as we've done up to this point, it's good to be able to just change it up and get a feel to go against different schemes and great players," McVay said.

 
 Monday's practice was a rest day for quarterback Matthew Stafford . He is scheduled to practice against the Cowboys on Tuesday. 
 
 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 In the Rams' return to their Woodland Hills facility for the remainder of the preseason, "the defense was outstanding," coach Sean McVay said.

 "There was great coverage, some great individual plays, disrupting timing and rhythm," McVay said. "It was a great day for the defense. Offensively they were able to run the football with some success, but throwing and catching was a real struggle."

 McVay said he was not discouraged by the performance by the offense, because the takeaways "were more of a reflection of great individual plays than necessarily poor execution."

 "What I get upset about is when the other opponent or whether the other side of the ball doesn't have to earn it because it's sloppy -- whether it's poor execution or communication on one side or the other," McVay said. "The plays that happened today, there was a handful of turnovers, but I thought it was a really great reflection of excellent execution defensively, some outstanding individual plays. And sometimes that's the price of doing business."

 And that defense might even get stronger as the Rams await the news of a possible return from defensive tackle Aaron Donald. McVay said Saturday that he did not have an update on Donald's decision.

 Other observations: 

 
 First-round pick Ty Simpson will "definitely" play in the first preseason game next Saturday against the Kansas City Chiefs , McVay said. 
 McVay said he has not made a decision on whether  Stetson Bennett IV  will play in the game. McVay typically does not play his starters or key backups in preseason games. Last year Jimmy Garoppolo , the Rams' established backup quarterback, did not play. Bennett and Simpson are competing to back up starting quarterback Matthew Stafford , but if Bennett does not play, that could be an indication he will start the season in the backup role. 
 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 Much of the talk during Rams training camp has been about a player not currently on the roster: Aaron Donald.

 On Thursday, as the Rams concluded training camp at Loyola Marymount University, coach Sean McVay said he didn't have an answer on whether the defensive tackle would come out of retirement.

 And if Donald does return? While defensive coordinator Chris Shula emphasized he's focusing on the roster guys now, he said, "I think I'd be lying if I said I hadn't thought about" the possibility of pairing up Donald and reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett .

 "You're anticipating, but at the same time, we're putting it in the core of our defense right now," Shula said. "We're building our defense step by step. If he decides to come, whenever that is, that's not going to affect exactly how we're doing it right now."

 McVay said Thursday that if Donald comes back, "those are things that you have to be able to figure out on the fly."

 "But what we are focusing on is the guys that are here," McVay said. "And then if Aaron is a part of it, it's obviously going to add value to our group, which is a positive."

 Another observation: 

 
 Thursday was the Rams' final practice at LMU before they head back to their team facility in Woodland Hills for the remainder of the preseason. 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 The Rams had a familiar face at their team facility this week, as Aaron Donald's name appeared on the NFL's transaction wire on Wednesday as a player taking part in a tryout for the team.

 The workout had to be reported to the league because it was supervised by a member of the Rams' football staff. Defensive coordinator Chris Shula said he was not at the Woodland Hills facility for the tryout, but said he talked to defensive line coach Giff Smith afterward.

 Last week, Rams head coach Sean McVay said he doesn't expect Donald to make a decision about coming out of retirement until after the team returns to its facility in Woodland Hills. The Rams' final practice at LMU is scheduled for Friday.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Defensive end Myles Garrett returned to practice on Wednesday after missing the last four practices with a little "lower body soreness." Garrett said he feels good and that the Rams were just trying to make sure he got back "100%." 
 Garrett was asked whether he feels like he can play with more "freedom" during practices in Los Angeles. He said that was a good way to describe the way the coaching staff allows players to play. "Not being punished or critiqued for trying to make a play," Garrett said. "There's guidelines and boundaries you got to stay within in the defense, but as long as we put ourselves in the right spots, they're all for it." 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 
 The Rams finished their second training camp block on Monday with what head coach Sean McVay called more of an unscripted practice. Matthew Stafford and  Stetson Bennett IV  took all of the quarterback reps for the Rams, with rookie Ty Simpson only taking part in individual drills.

 The first-team offense and the secondary exchanged several standout plays, including a pass breakup on receiver Puka Nacua by cornerback Trent McDuffie . Later, Stafford found wide receiver Davante Adams for a completion down the sideline.

 "I thought there was especially some really good back and forth with the ones," McVay said after practice. "Some really good plays on both sides, but that's what we're looking for is good quality play where you can really see guys playing through the cycle of the snap."

 McVay pointed to "some big breakups down the field" by McDuffie and cornerback Jaylen Watson .

 "Guys made plays on both sides and it felt like it was a quality operation," McVay said.

 More observations from the day: 

 
 
 McVay said he hasn't determined how he will allocate reps during the preseason between the quarterbacks other than Stafford not playing in any preseason games.…

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Las Vegas Raiders  camp is taking place at Intermountain Health Performance Center in Henderson, Nevada, and Raiders reporter Ryan McFadden has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 
 

 Latest news from Raiders camp 
 
 Nine takeaways from Raiders' nine training camp practices 
 Maxx Crosby's approaching Raiders training camp with intensity 
 Three-time Pro Bowl guard Andrus Peat announces retirement 
 Cousins gets nod over Mendoza to open Raiders camp 
 What's next for Crosby, WR and CB rooms? 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 

 Maybe coach Klint Kubiak's decision to hold Kirk Cousins from Saturday's practice due to his scuffle with Maxx Crosby sparked a fire within the veteran quarterback. Maybe it didn't. Either way, Cousins had his best performance of training camp.

 Monday featured Cousins fitting the ball into tight windows and effectively conducting two-minute drives. He threw a touchdown pass to Brock Bowers in the corner of the end zone despite tight coverage from Taron Johnson . Both players later connected on a deep pass over the middle, positioning the offense near the goal line.

 Cousins delivered a nice pass to wide receiver Tre Tucker on a crossing route with rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses in coverage. He also connected with Malik Benson , who made a contested catch against cornerback Darien Porter .

 During the two-minute period, Cousins completed four passes, including a touchdown throw to wide receiver Jalen Nailor .

 Fernando Mendoza , on the other hand, went back to playing with the second-team offense. He didn't put together his best performance. He ran into running back Dare Ogunbowale during the handoff exchange.

 He threw his third interception of camp. Mendoza attempted a pass to wide receiver Deven Thompkins on an out route. Greedy Vance was in front of Thompkins in man coverage, and Mendoza threw the ball directly into the second-year defensive back's hands.

 His best throw -- a back-shoulder pass to Benson -- was called back because he was sacked on the play.

 Other observations: 

 
 Defensive end Kwity Paye returned to practice, but did not participate in the team period. Rookie defensive end Keyron Crawford practiced, but wore a red non-contact jersey. Guard Caleb Rogers , tight end Carter Runyon and wide receiver  Dont'e Thornton Jr . did not participate. 
 From a health standpoint, rookie cornerback Jermod McCoy said he feels closer to how he was in 2024. McCoy, who missed the entire 2025 college football season at Tennessee, said the Raiders' rehab plan has him feeling much better. "I'm still getting there. It's been a long time since I really played football. 
 McCoy mentioned that the biggest challenge was getting back into football shape and pre-snap stuff. McCoy felt rusty during the first day of camp, but was comfortable by Day 3. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 
 

 With  Kirk Cousins and Maxx Crosby  not practicing for violating team rules ,  Fernando Mendoza  played with the starters for the first time in camp.

 Mendoza had his good and bad moments. He overthrew wide receiver Jack Bech a couple of times. And he had trouble securing the ball when snapped to him by Tyler Linderbaum and Jordan Meredith .

 Mendoza, however, didn't get flustered. He had one of his best throws of camp during the red zone period. He threw a touchdown pass to Tre Tucker , in which he zipped the ball through tight coverage by cornerback Taron Johnson .

 Mendoza also threw touchdowns to tight ends Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer .

 The highlight of the day was Mendoza's efficiency during the two-minute period to close out practice. He completed five straight passes, including a throw to Tucker in tight coverage, to set up a field goal from kicker Matt Gay .

 During Mendoza's reps with the first-team, quarterback coach Mike Sullivan said the biggest things he was evaluating were the rookie's command of the offense and not panicking in the pocket. Sullivan added that the team is pleased with Mendoza's development.

 Mendoza's comfort and command of the operation have grown since the spring. Sullivan has also noticed improvement in Mendoza's play from under center.

 Other observation: 

 Wide receiver Jalen Nailor and running back Dare Ogunbowale returned to practice after being sidelined Friday. Defensive ends Kwity Paye and Keyron Crawford , wide receiver Dont'e Thornton Jr.  and tight end Carter Runyon did not participate.

 

 Friday, Aug. 7 
 Friday was an eventful morning at Raiders HQ.

 Las Vegas' eighth practice was highlighted by a scuffle between Maxx Crosby and Kirk Cousins . Other than that, both sides made plays throughout the team's third padded practice.

 Cousins was picked off twice in the red zone. First, Crosby disrupted Cousins' pass attempt, causing the ball to be picked off by safety Jeremy Chinn . On the following play, rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses intercepted Cousins in the back corner of the end zone.

 

 Cousins responded well. He connected with tight ends  Michael Mayer  and Brock Bowers on a few big throws in the middle of the field. He was even efficient during the two-minute period near the end of practice, quickly moving the offense down the field into field-goal range.

 Rookie running back Mike Washington Jr . had an explosive run, in which he ran over cornerback Jermod McCoy and continued to sprint down the field for a big gain.

 Fernando Mendoza  was sharp. His performance was highlighted by a touchdown pass to wide receiver Deven Thompkins during the red zone period. Mendoza zipped the ball through tight coverage

 Other observations: 

 
 Wide receiver Jalen Nailor , defensive ends Kwity Paye and Keyron Crawford , tight end Carter Runyon and running back Dare Ogunbowale did not participate in practice. Second-year wide receiver  Dont'e Thornton Jr . left practice early, but coach Klint Kubiak didn't sound concerned about the various absences. With Nailor out, rookie wide receiver Malik Benson took the majority of the first-team reps on the opposite side of Tre Tucker . "We had a few guys nicked up, and we're trying to be cautious," Kubiak said. 
 Jackson Powers-Johnson and Caleb Rogers alternated first-team reps at right guard. Kubiak said it's a part of the plan the team has in place to figure out the best starting offensive line combination. Right guard has been the only position on the first-team offensive line that has had changes. 
 Kubiak clarified that he didn't take the coaching staff to drinks after the Baltimore Ravens backed out of a trade agreement for Crosby. Making a guest appearance on the "Ball in the Family" podcast, hosted by NBA player Lonzo Ball, Crosby recalled Kubiak called him and said the coaching staff was going to celebrate after the announcement was made. "He is in big trouble for revealing that," Kubiak jokingly said. "We haven't gone out as much as a staff. We have been grinding. We probably need to do that more."

 Tight end Brock Bowers keeps stacking up good practices.

title: Takeaways from Raiders' nine training camp practices
summary: Nine takeaways after nine Raiders training camp practices. Here's what we've learned.
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev. -- The Las Vegas Raiders ' training camp is in full swing . We've seen Kirk Cousins and Brock Bowers ' connection be on point. The good and bad from top pick Fernando Mendoza . Maxx Crosby being the game wrecker that he normally is, despite undergoing offseason knee surgery. And a pair of Day 3 draft picks showing the potential of having meaningful roles in the fall.

 But let's not jump to conclusions just yet. Coach Klint Kubiak said 90% of the roster has yet to solidify a role. And when offensive line coach Rick Dennison spoke to reporters last Tuesday, he said the team was still in the midst of its install phase.

 At the same time, there have been plenty of notable performances, intriguing lineup combinations and position battles through two weeks of playing in the blazing Nevada heat. Here are nine takeaways from nine training camp practices:

 

 Cousins remains in the driver's seat for QB1. 

 There hadn't been any new developments in the starting quarterback race between Cousins and Mendoza until Saturday. Mendoza played with the starters for the first time in camp due to Cousins not participating during the 11-on-11 period after violating team rules after scuffling with Crosby .

 

 Despite Mendoza having an overall solid day with the first team, Cousins still has a strong edge in the race to be QB1. He has played solely with the starters, as expected, and has looked better than Mendoza and Aidan O'Connell . Cousins has been efficient and has rarely put the ball in harm's way. On top of that, the players have brought Cousins in as one of the leaders on the team.

 "I really appreciate my time working with him. [He's] making me better," wide receiver Tre Tucker said of the 15-year veteran. "Very bright IQ. That was a great addition for us to add him because it's going to make us all better."

 Mendoza has been what the Raiders expected him to be. Compared to OTAs and mandatory minicamp, Mendoza has better command of the offense and more confidence in his knowledge of the system. His accuracy has been solid, and he has done a good job of getting the ball out of his hands quickly. The coaching staff has praised his improvement in playing under center.

 He has had his fair share of struggles, though. There have been moments when Mendoza was off-target on his throws, had difficulty getting his teammates aligned and controlling the ball when snapped to him. As Kubiak said, not every game or practice will be perfect, especially for a rookie like Mendoza, who is growing through his first training camp.

 Nonetheless, Las Vegas has been pleased with his development, especially how he bounces back from mistakes.

 "We've got three NFL-ready quarterbacks," said Kubiak, who has noticed improvement each day from Mendoza. "He's like every other rookie. They are introduced to a whole new level of football, and there's going to be days of failure and days of success."

 

 Tonka Hemingway could become a major contributor on the defensive line. 

 The second-year defensive tackle has frequently played with the first-team defense since the beginning of camp. The Raiders have alternated reps with Benito Jones , Jonah Laulu , Adam Butler and Thomas Booker IV . When it comes to Hemingway, he has been a consistent presence up front and has made the most of the opportunity.

 Hemingway has been effective in the run and pass game, showing off the traits of a potential impact player as a 3-technique. Teammates have raved about Hemingway. Left guard Spencer Burford said Hemingway has been flying around the ball. Edge rusher Kwity Paye said he has played "great."

 "Tonka, he put in a lot of work this offseason. He got an award for the defense for the guys putting in the most work in the weight room," Paye said. "...You can just see it in camp, like he's been popping up on the field everywhere."

 

 

 Bowers remains dominant. 

 The chemistry between Cousins and Bowers has grown each practice. Whether it's 7-on-7 or 11-on-11, Bowers has figured out a way to make plays. Cousins has consistently found Bowers in the middle of the field on those crossing routes.

 Bowers has matched up against multiple defenders and consistently gotten open. That was the case during Thursday's practice when Bowers slipped by the defense before catching a deep pass from Cousins for a touchdown. The third-year tight end is playing at full strength after dealing with a knee injury for a good chunk of last season.

 The way Cousins has relied heavily on Bowers in practice indicates that the All-Pro pass catcher is in line for a big season, and the passing game will go as far as he takes it.

 "He's a special player [and] super consistent," O'Connell said. "He knows [how to be in the] right place at the right time, and when you add his skill set, it adds to how special he is."

 

 There are a ton of moving parts on defense. 

 Linebacker Nakobe Dean described the defense as a group that can do multiple things. Las Vegas has moved players all over the field during camp. Quay Walker has lined up next to Dean as an inside linebacker and has had snaps on edge in the Raiders' nickel packages.

 Paye mentioned that he has played as a strongside linebacker, defensive end and 3-technique. As for defensive back Taron Johnson , the Raiders have rotated him between safety and nickel. Even during individual drills, Johnson has been seen working with the defensive backs and linebackers.

 Last season, there wasn't too much movement outside of safety Jeremy Chinn , who has made a career of lining up in the back end, at linebacker or nickel. It appears that versatility will be the identity of the Raiders' defense under  coordinator Rob Leonard.

 "The offense [will] not [be] able to know what type of packages we're going to be in, what type of coverage [or] blitz packages," safeties coach Matt Robinson said. "The more guys and the more pieces that are versatile, it allows us to be multiple."

 

 Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington Jr . are looking like a formidable RB duo. 

 

 Mendoza said early in camp that Kubiak's offense will be built on the run game. The Raiders, however, have struggled in the past with putting together a stable rushing attack, ranking last in yards per game (78.6) since 2024.

 The team's fortune could change in the fall. Jeanty has looked extremely comfortable in this outside zone scheme. He has had multiple explosive runs down the sidelines during practice. And another reason to be optimistic that the Raiders will produce better rushing numbers is rookie Washington.

 Kubiak wants Jeanty to be a bell-cow running back. But Washington has shown that he could be a major factor, as well. Washington has split reps with the first and second team. There have been moments when he has used his 6-foot-2, 228-pound size and speed to create big plays.

 During Friday's practice, Washington rushed outside, running over cornerback Jermod McCoy , and continued to sprint down the field for a big gain.

 It's hard to evaluate running backs, especially on days when the team is not in pads. But there have been plays from Jeanty and Washington that show they have the potential to be a formidable duo.

 

 The emergence of Hezekiah Masses 

 The fifth-round cornerback has played a significant amount of time with the starting defense, frequently alternating reps with Darien Porter on the outside. Playing on the opposite side of Eric Stokes , Masses has made the most of his opportunities in practice.

 "He can cover," defensive backs coach/pass game coordinator Joe Woods said. "There are some guys in [my] past that he reminds me of in terms of quickness, like Denzel Ward had that extreme lateral quickness where he can get on the body. [Masses has] that same type of trait. Not saying he's Denzel; he's got a long way to go. But there are some really good things that he's doing."

title: 2026 Miami Dolphins training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Dolphins training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Miami Dolphins  camp is taking place in Miami Gardens, and Dolphins reporter Marcel Louis-Jacques has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Dolphins camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Dolphins camp 
 
 Dolphins top pick Proctor embracing NFL learning curve 
 Miami, All-Pro LB Jordyn Brooks reach 3-year, $51.3M extension 
 Dolphins, Aaron Brewer reach 3-year, $52.5 million extension 
 Why Miami's rookies can thrive 
 
 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 Monday's return to the practice field was a standout day for the Dolphins' rookies. Wide receiver Caleb Douglas started team drills with a drop due to a loss of focus but rebounded nicely with a series of contested catches. Coach Jeff Hafley said he wanted to see the third-round pick's ability to fight through contact once pads came on at practice, and so far Douglas has delivered.

 Linebacker Jacob Rodriguez 's sideline-to-sideline ability popped Monday, as did his ability to read and react to run plays. Seventh-round defensive end Max Llewellyn sacked quarterback Quinn Ewers during team drills and cornerback Chris Johnson had an impressive pass breakup in the end zone against Douglas.

 More observations: 

 
 Tight end Greg Dulcich practiced in full for the first time since last week. He'd worn the red non-contact jersey for the past few practices with an apparent hand injury. 
 Ewers threw an interception to safety Major Burns during the team's late-game drill. He stepped up in the pocket and likely would've scrambled in a real game, but appeared to try to fit the ball through a small window -- and it went directly to Burns. 
 Quarterback Malik Willis ' arm velocity was apparent throughout the practice, particularly on an off-platform throw to Douglas that got home in the blink of an eye. His speech to the Dolphins' offense about upholding the team's standard has stuck with his teammates -- several of whom have credited his growth as a leader. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 The Dolphins held Saturday's practice at Hard Rock Stadium, but a critical moment occurred before they even set foot on the field.

 Quarterback Malik Willis addressed his teammates Friday, to ensure players continued to uphold the team's standard.

 "I just wanted to talk to the offense and just have a man-to-man conversation," Willis said Saturday. "We got to understand this is a business, and we got to take what we do personally. We got to take pride in it, and we got to do it to the best of our ability -- regardless if we're calling plays to beat the defense or not.

 "We're not calling plays to beat the defense; we're calling the plays that we want to use throughout the year. We're trying to get better at those plays. Whether we win a down or not, are we doing everything that we can do to execute the playcall?"

 Rookie offensive tackle Kadyn Proctor reference Willis' speech unprompted after practice, so the message appears to have stuck.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Wide receiver Tahj Washington made receptions of 50 and 30 yards on balls from Cam Miller and Quinn Ewers , and rookie wide receiver  Donaven McCulley  brought down a 45-yard pass from Miller in traffic, shaking off a facemask penalty in the process. 
 Safety Tanner Wall , who signed with the Dolphins on Friday, wasted no time making his presence known in his first practice with the team. He broke up a pass in the end zone during red zone drills to save a touchdown. 
 Kicker Zane Gonzalez appeared to leave the practice field after special teams work and did not return. Riley Patterson handled all kicks during team drills at the end of practice. 
 Cornerback JuJu Brents missed practice after suffering an undisclosed injury Friday, while safety Dante Trader Jr . missed his third consecutive practice. The team hopes to get Trader back in time for next week's practice with the Commanders. 
 

 

 Friday, Aug. 7 
 Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley has stressed the importance of taking the ball away to his defense, and his players have responded with gusto this summer. Miami's defense recorded four interceptions during Friday's practice, including two by second-year cornerback Miles Battle -- both off quarterback Quinn Ewers . Linebacker Jackson Woodard continued his strong week of practice with a pick-six off quarterback Mark Gronowski , and UDFA safety Louis Moore added to his big play total with an interception as well.

 The Dolphins defense has forced multiple turnovers in nearly every practice this summer. It's a direct result of the team's coaching points on and off the field.

 "One of our assistant linebacker coaches, Wendel (Davis) -- he starts every meeting with taking the ball away," linebacker Tyrel Dodson said. "So he's made excellent emphasis on those takeaway points and we've honed in on it. We've studied different techniques, punching the ball out. Jacob (Rodriguez is) good at it. So we've studied the Peanut punch and all that stuff. So it's looking good."

 More observations: 

 
 Rookie wide receiver Caleb Douglas had an explosive play on a sideline ball from Malik Willis during team drills. The third-round pick appeared to get behind cornerback Jason Marshall Jr and picked up some yards after the catch. 
 Right tackle Austin Jackson returned to practice after missing the past two practices with an undisclosed injury. As a result, defensive end Chop Robinson didn't wreak the same level of havoc he did with Jackson sidelined, but it was a fun matchup to watch. 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 

 Pressure, pressure and more pressure was the key word for the Dolphins in Thursday's practice. The team shed its shoulder pads, looking to ease back into work following Wednesday's off day, but it didn't stop coach Jeff Hafley's defense from attacking its offensive counterparts throughout team drills.

 Linebacker Jackson Woodard was a constant presence around the ball, while defensive end Chop Robinson continued his strong camp -- albeit against a banged up right side of the Dolphins' offensive line. Thursday also marked another strong performance from rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez ; defensive coordinator Sean Duggan said he could tell the game is starting to slow down for Rodriguez and the other rookie linebackers, Kyle Louis and Trey Moore .

 More conversations: 

 
 Running back Jaylen Wright broke of a couple strong runs during team drills. Speaking to the media earlier this week, he sounded calm and at peace with his career to date and ready to attack the best opportunity he's had for regular playing time since entering the league in 2024. 
 Linebacker Willie Gay Jr . intercepted quarterback Cam Miller and returned it for a long gain. We've seen Gay stand out at training camp before, the Dolphins are hoping his momentum carries into game day this preseason, and the regular season. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 If you were building a basketball team out of Dolphins players, defensive tackle Zach Sieler -- all 6-foot-6, 300 pounds of him -- might be a choice at power forward. But coach Jeff Hafley said the nine-year veteran is actually more of a point guard on the team's defensive line.

 Despite his 25.5 sacks over the past three seasons, Hafley said Sieler's ability and willingness to take on blockers and open rush lanes for his teammates really pops on tape.
